## 3. Foundation & event ledger

- ⚙️ **Monorepo workspace** — pnpm workspaces + Turborepo, TypeScript strict, Node 22, ESM, Vitest; packages `@gisik-nokma/domain`, `@gisik-nokma/rule-engine`, `@gisik-nokma/server`, `@gisik-nokma/ui`, `@gisik-nokma/app-core`, `@gisik-nokma/sync-client`, `@gisik-nokma/web`. The gate is one `build`/`test`/`typecheck` triple per workspace package — a count re-derived by running it, never written down here, because a number in prose has a shelf life that ends at the next package. `build.outputs` names `.next/**` beside `dist/**`, without which turbo would report a cache hit for a Next build whose output it never stored; `globalEnv` names `SERVER_ORIGIN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`, because the latter is BAKED INTO the browser bundle and a cached build compiled against a different one would otherwise be served as if it were current. Root configs `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `turbo.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`; dev Postgres via `docker-compose.yml`.
- ⚙️ **CI pipeline (skeleton)** — GitHub Actions workflow on every pull request and push to `main`: a single job installs via pnpm, brings up a Postgres 16 service container matching `docker-compose.yml`'s user/password/port, and runs the turbo gate (`build`, `test`, `typecheck`); IST convergence rides the same per-test-database `ALTER DATABASE` the test harness already runs, not a container-level override. The independent-CI precondition for the coordination doc's auto-merge protocol. Scoped to what Plans 1–2 landed — lint, `check:env` (Plan 11 T6), the client half of the fixtures suite and the dual-client job (Plan 10), the e2e job (Plans 4/6), and the interim-plumbing gate (Plan 10) land with their owning plans; Plan 11's own catalogue task owns the full pipeline under §13. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- ⚙️ **Event envelope & vocabulary** — the exact `EventEnvelope` contract with zod validation, ULID helpers, and the versioned event-type registry; pure `parseEvent` refuses unknown types, unknown versions, invalid payloads, malformed envelopes, and — for a registration that declares an `entityKind` — an envelope whose `entity.kind` differs (`entity-kind-mismatch`; layered with the rule engine's own kind checks by design, since fixtures and offline replicas bypass `parseEvent`). Provisional seed vocabulary: `workspace.created` v1, `workspace.renamed` v1; the registry now also holds `workflow.defined` v1 (Plan 2). `packages/domain/`
  - ⚙️ **An assistant's write is a distinct provenance, not a flavour of the web's** — `ORIGINS` carries `'mcp'` alongside `'web' | 'mobile' | 'desktop' | 'server'` (MCP plan Task 0, owner ruling 1). In a product whose stated purpose is a board that cannot lie about its own history, a write claiming `'web'` when a machine made it is the history lying about who acted. `Origin`, `z.enum(ORIGINS)` and the permission gate's `CLIENT_ORIGINS` all DERIVE from the array, so the member was the whole edit — the gate gained an `mcp` case it did not have to be told about, and no migration was needed (`origin text NOT NULL`, no `CHECK`, no Postgres enum, verified across every migration). The rule engine's fixture harness now imports `ORIGINS` instead of re-spelling it. Case 3.163. `packages/domain/src/envelope.ts`, `packages/rule-engine/src/fixtures/harness.ts`
- ⚙️ **Contest event vocabulary** — `claim.contested` v1 and `claim.contested_resolved` v1, the two types that make a sync-time refusal into ledger history instead of a silent drop (spec honesty invariant 5, coordination amendment 16). The contest carries the refused claim whole (`originalEvent`, a full `SubmittedEvent`) and is refused if the claim arrives without its `payload` — `z.unknown()` makes that key optional in zod, so the envelope door's own payload-presence check (Plan 4's amendment) is what stops the ledger from recording that something was claimed without recording what. `null` and `{}` still pass: an empty claim is a claim, an absent one is not. Resolution is `redone` | `converted-to-comment` | `discarded`, and the first two must link the event they produced — a redo without its replacement id, or a conversion without its comment id, is refused. Both types bind `entityKind: 'ticket'` in the registry, so a contest filed against a workflow or a workspace is refused at the door with `entity-kind-mismatch` rather than appended to an append-only table where it could never be corrected. Alongside them: `renderContestedClaimText(payload)`, the one attributed, IST-dated, rule-naming sentence a banner shows and a "convert to comment" writes into the ledger forever, and `plainTextToDoc(text)`, the inverse of `docToPlainText` — the minimal ProseMirror doc that conversion needs because bodies are PM JSON. `packages/domain/src/events/contest-events.ts`, registrations in `packages/domain/src/vocabulary.ts`
- ⚙️ **Backlog rank keys (`rankBetween`) and `ticket.ranked`** — backlog/closed spec §8.1, second wave, 2026-09-18 (Task 1). `rankBetween(before, after)` returns an order-preserving fractional key strictly between its neighbours over the alphabet `0-9a-z` (36 symbols, so plain string comparison IS the order), extending the shorter side — so inserting between the same two tickets forever only lengthens ONE key and renumbers nobody, which is what makes a reorder exactly one claim instead of a column rewrite. `compareByRank` orders ranked tickets first by key, then the unranked by `ticketId` ascending (a ULID is creation order), falling back to `ticketId` on equal keys so the order is total and stable rather than decided by the sort's own tie-breaking. `ticket.ranked` v1 carries `{rank}`, is registered against `entityKind: 'ticket'`, and joins `TICKET_EVENT_TYPES`; the reducer folds it onto `TicketState.rank` and moves nothing else — `stateId` is untouched for the same reason it is on the closed pair, because a reorder is not a status change and letting it look like one would put a move nobody made into the transition log four-eyes reads. **The key space excludes keys ending in `0`, and the payload door enforces it.** Nothing in the alphabet sorts below `'0'`, so `rankBetween('a', 'a0')` has no answer to give — and does not refuse one either: measured with a step cap, it appends `'0'` forever (`NONTERMINATING at i=20001`). Every producer is safe by construction (the midpoint digit appended is always >= 1), so the door is the single place a hand-written key could reach the ledger; `ticketRankedPayload` therefore refines with `isRankKey` rather than the looser `RANK_KEY_REGEX`, which admits `'a0'`. Backlog-only is the ENGINE's door (`checkTicketRanked`, Task 2), not the schema's. **A ticket nobody has ranked carries `rank: null` — the key PRESENT and null, not absent** (Task 3, 2026-09-18, superseding this bullet's Task-1 text, which said the opposite and said why it was deferring). Task 1's creation branch deliberately omitted the field because `rowToTicketState` builds a `TicketState` from COLUMNS and there was no `rank` column yet, so the reducer and the server's read could not agree in SHAPE. Task 3 adds the column, and then the decision is measured rather than weighed: the dual-client rig compares whole `TicketState`s with `toEqual`, so a reducer that omits forces the server read to omit, and an omitting server read puts an absent key on the single-ticket wire for every unranked ticket — which `mapRank` would have to tolerate, the exact shape case 13.603's second `it` forbids. **Made `rowToTicketState` omit the key when the column is NULL and 13 rig cases across all four dual-client files reddened**, every one a one-key shape mismatch. So: creation writes the null, `rowToTicketState` reads the column unconditionally, the replica reads `state.rank ?? null` at the boundary, and every reader still spells `?? null` — for the legacy test literals' sake, not the producers'. Spec §8.1 states the same answer in the domain's words (`null` = never ranked). Cases 13.694–13.696 (13.696 tightened from `rank ?? null` to `toBeNull()` by Task 3, since presence is now the contract). `packages/domain/src/rank.ts`, `packages/domain/src/events/ticket-events.ts`, `packages/domain/src/ticket-state.ts`, `packages/domain/src/entity-state.ts`, `packages/domain/src/vocabulary.ts`
- ⚙️ **Backlog rank on the wire — `proj_tickets.rank`, `TicketCard.rank`, `ListRow.rank`** — backlog/closed spec §8.1, second wave, 2026-09-18 (Task 3). The column is one field with one meaning, `text NULL`, so unlike the `closed` pair beside it there is no fold and nothing that can disagree with anything: `upsertTicket` writes it from `TicketState.rank` on both the INSERT and the ON CONFLICT SET list, and `rowToTicketState` reads it unconditionally, which is what keeps the server read model the same SHAPE as the reducer's output (the dual-client rig compares the two with `toEqual`). `TicketCard.rank` and `ListRow.rank` are REQUIRED `string | null`, and the key rides every card-building route through `assembleTicketCards` rather than a second per-route enumeration. **The client half is real, not assumed:** `mapRank` maps the key on BOTH bodies it is served on — `mapListRow` (the list) and `mapTicketState` (the single ticket) — refusing a key outside the alphabet with `isRankKey`, the domain's own predicate rather than the looser `RANK_KEY_REGEX`, and refusing an ABSENT key instead of defaulting it (the 13.603 lesson). Ordering is unchanged and deliberately so: the list route keeps its `ticket_id` keyset cursor (plan ruling R1) and carries `rank` on every row for the Backlog tab to sort client-side. There is no index on the column — the server never sorts by it, and an index no query reads is indistinguishable from one that works. Cases 13.702–13.704. `apps/server/migrations/1789200000000_proj-tickets-rank.sql`, `apps/server/src/projections/tickets.ts`, `apps/server/src/read/ticket-cards.ts`, `packages/domain/src/read-models.ts`, `packages/app-core/src/view-types.ts`, `packages/app-core/src/online/mappers.ts`, `packages/app-core/src/replica/replica-data-source.ts`
- ⚙️ **Priority is the fifth built-in field — schema, payload, reducer default (2026-09-22 spec, Task 1)** — `BUILTIN_FIELD_IDS` gains `priority`, so `ticketTypeDefSchema` refuses a custom field that shadows it exactly as it already does for `dueDate`/`startDate`. `PRIORITIES = ['P1', 'P2', 'P3']`, `prioritySchema` and `DEFAULT_PRIORITY = 'P2'` are the ONE origin every later consumer imports from — no other file spells the list. `ticketCreatedPayload` gains an optional `priority`: absent at parse means P2, the same additive-field rule `start` already follows, and the default is never written into the stored payload. The REDUCER is the one place the default is applied: `applyTicketEvent`'s `ticket.created` arm writes `fields.priority: claim(p.priority ?? DEFAULT_PRIORITY, env)` beside `fields.title`, attributed to the creator's id and both clocks, so a v1 event with no `priority` replays to a real, attributed P2 claim rather than a reader-side default. `TicketCard.priority` is `PriorityClaim`, NEVER nullable and never a three-state union like `TicketDueDate` — there is no never-claimed or cleared state, because creation always writes the claim and the engine refuses a null one (Task 2). `GROUPINGS` and `filterSpecSchema` gain `priority` (a singular level, like `stateId`). Server, mapper, replica, sheet, new-ticket and board surfaces are later tasks of the same plan and are not yet wired — every existing `TicketCard`/`BoardCard`/`ListRow` producer outside `packages/domain` now fails to typecheck on the missing key, by design (the throw-not-default rule the spec states). Cases 3.962–3.966, 7.267. `packages/domain/src/ticket-types.ts`, `events/ticket-events.ts`, `ticket-state.ts`, `read-models.ts`, `filter-spec.ts`
- ⚙️ **Client envelope builder** — `newSubmittedEvent(...)`, the one place a client mints an event: it fills `id` (ULID), `version` and `clientTime` and copies the rest of the caller's claim. `serverTime` and `seq` are absent by construction, because they are the server's to assign at ingest and a client that invented them would be asserting facts it does not own. `packages/domain/src/submit.ts`
- ⚙️ **IST day boundaries** — `istDayOf(instant)` and `istDayBounds(day)` against the fixed +05:30 offset (India has no DST), plus `IST_TIME_ZONE`: the single origin for where a day starts. "Due today", "overdue", calendar-cell assignment and day counts across the whole product resolve here, never from the server's locale or the viewer's device. `packages/domain/src/ist-day.ts`
- ⚙️ **IST instant rendering & clock skew** — `formatIstInstant(instant)` is the ONE way the product prints an absolute instant to a person (`'21 Aug 2026, 00:00 IST'`). Its day comes from `istDayOf`, so a printed timestamp can never disagree with the calendar cell the same instant lands in; it does constant-offset arithmetic with no `Intl` and no date library, because Hermes on mobile does not reliably ship a timezone database and a silent fallback to the device's zone would be the offline copy disagreeing about when things happened. Anything that is not a well-formed, real ISO instant travels back verbatim rather than as an invented time: unparseable, year-extended, calendar-impossible (`2026-02-30`), a day claim like `2026-08-20` that `Date.parse` would call midnight UTC, or a string with no stated offset that would otherwise be read in the device timezone. `IST_CLOCK_NOTE` is the line a surface puts beside a time so a collaborator in another timezone knows which clock they are reading. Beside them, `clockSkewMs` / `GROSS_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` (10 min) / `hasGrossClockSkew` compute skew from the two clocks the envelope already keeps: DERIVED, never stored and never projected, so the flag is identical wherever it is computed and an unparseable client claim counts as gross rather than as zero. `packages/domain/src/clock-skew.ts`
- ⚙️ **Plain-text document rendering** — `docToPlainText(doc: unknown): string`, a dependency-free ProseMirror/Tiptap JSON walker (coordination amendment 12): total on junk input, mention nodes `{type:'mention', attrs:{userId, label?}}` render as `@label` falling back to `@userId`, image/attachment nodes render as nothing. Pulled forward as pre-work (Plan 5 Task 1) because `proj_search` (Plan 5), Plan 7's editor, and Plan 9's notifications all consume it; landed here in §3, and Plan 5's own catalogue task (Task 16) has since run — 2026-09-02 — and deliberately LEFT it here rather than relocating it to §7, because the bullet belongs beside the ledger material it renders. - ⚙️ **Accessible-name ratchet** — the counts of `aria-label` / `role` / `aria-selected` / `aria-describedby` per route are baselined one-way, on both the signed-out and the signed-in surface, so a restyle that drops one goes red naming the route and the attribute. Built as Task 0 of the HIG per-screen plan and BEFORE any screen was touched, because that work is delegated to smaller models and **a rule enforced by a test survives a delegation while a rule enforced by attention does not**. It measures the rendered DOM, not the source, so it sees what actually reaches assistive tech. It counts rather than reads: swapping one name for another passes, losing one does not. - ✅ **Every route names its view in the document title** (exec1 P12, 2026-09-21) — `app/layout.tsx` set `{ title: 'Gisik Nokma' }` and NOTHING set a per-route title, so the browser tab, the window title, the browser history and a screen reader's page announcement read the same string on `/sign-in`, `/inbox`, `/help`, a board, a ticket sheet, `/settings`, `/privacy`, `/terms` and the 404 alike. WCAG 2.2 §2.4.2 *Page Titled* is **Level A**, and its Understanding document addresses exactly this shape of application: *"for web applications (single page applications) where the view changes dynamically, the title should also be changed dynamically to reflect the content or topic of the current view."* ⚠ **THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FIX DID NOT WORK, AND THE SUITE SAID IT DID — corrected 2026-09-21 against a browser reading, which is what this batch owed and has now paid.** It gave every `'use client'` route a `<DocumentTitle>` whose effect writes `document.title`. That is a race it loses: traced in Chrome against the built app, the effect writes `"Sign in · Gisik Nokma"` at **atMs 21**, and at **atMs 42** React — hydrating Next's `<head>` — repairs the `<title>` NODE back to the server's value, **bypassing the `title` setter entirely**. `finalTitle` was `Gisik Nokma` on `/sign-in` after 15 s and on `/help` after 4 s. **The client half landed on ZERO of its routes while its jsdom arm passed the whole time.** Two replacements were tried and also measured as failures, and are recorded in `src/document-title.tsx` so neither is re-attempted: a `useSyncExternalStore` hydration gate (the write still landed at 21 ms — React repairs *after* hydration of the subtree, so no hydration signal precedes it) and returning `<title>` for React 19 to hoist (**three** `<title>` elements in the hydrated document; React does not deduplicate them and `document.title` reads the first, which is Next's). **The fix that holds is a SERVER route-segment `layout.tsx` exporting `metadata`** — a segment layout is a server component even when the page under it is `'use client'` — so the title is in the head **before any JavaScript runs**, which is what WCAG 2.2 §2.4.2 (Level A) actually asks for. `<DocumentTitle>` survives ONLY where the topic resolves from a READ (the workspace and project names), whose writes land long after the repair; each of those keeps a server layout for the generic title shown meanwhile. **MEASURED, both halves, against the built app on lane port 3055:** every route serves its own title — `/sign-in` → `Sign in · Gisik Nokma`, `/help` → `Help · Gisik Nokma`, `/settings` → `Settings · Gisik Nokma`, `/definitely-not-a-route` → `Page not found · Gisik Nokma` — and post-hydration in Chrome each has **exactly one `<title>`**, correct at the first sample and unchanged for 4–6 s. **That last one also proves Next honours `metadata` in `not-found.tsx`**, a file its own docs do not list. `documentTitleFor` in `src/page-title.ts` is the one source for the format and carries no `'use client'` on purpose (a directive there would turn the helper into a client reference and break the server half). ⚠ The sweep walks `page.tsx` AND `not-found.tsx` (the 404 is named in the finding and is the one route a reader reaches with no context); it requires each route to be titled by its own or a sibling `metadata`, **and it has a second arm that reddens on any non-dynamic route titling itself from `<DocumentTitle>` with a literal topic** — the measured failure. Its exclusion list — `app/page.tsx`, a bare `redirect` — is asserted to still be a bare redirect so it cannot become a hiding place. Case `13.1057`. `apps/web/src/page-title.ts`, `apps/web/src/document-title.tsx`, the 19 `layout.tsx` files under `apps/web/app/`

One module holds the answer — `apps/web/src/display-label.ts`'s `displayLabelOf` (name, else email, else `''`) and `avatarNameOf` (name, else the email's LOCAL PART, because the domain is the same for everyone on a hosted service) — and **the contract that matters is that `''` means NO LABEL, so every caller omits its suffix rather than concatenating onto it**: the h1 and the button are ternaries, and neither can reproduce the dangling punctuation for a person with neither a name nor an address (`useCurrentUser` types `email` as `string | null`, so that case is reachable). ⚠ **Two things deliberately NOT changed:** `initialsOf`'s own `?` fallback stands (what changed is that the caller stops feeding it an empty string), and the account menu's header still renders `{user.name}` — it is a two-line block with the email below, so a nameless person sees one line and not a dangling one, while routing it through `displayLabelOf` would print the address TWICE, bold and muted, which is worse than the gap it would close. Not to be confused with E5-4 (the picker) or E4-6 (provenance's RULED raw-id fallback). Case `13.1054`. **⚠ AND THE RULE IS NOW STATED ONCE FOR EVERY SURFACE THAT HOLDS A ROSTER MEMBER: `packages/app-core/src/member-label.ts`, `memberLabel(member)` — name, then the email, then the id (owner request, 2026-09-22: *"Everywhere for id, show the Name; if name is empty/blank, show the email"*).** That is a DIFFERENT rule from this bullet's and the difference is the point: `displayLabelOf` labels the SIGNED-IN USER, has no roster, and returns `''` for a person with neither because its callers OMIT a suffix — while `memberLabel` labels somebody ELSE off a roster row and floors at the ID, because a row, a picker option and a claim line must all name somebody. The two share their first two steps and nothing else, and neither is derived from the other. `packages/app-core/src/member-label.ts` — cases `13.1291`–`13.1296`. `apps/web/src/display-label.ts`, `apps/web/src/account-menu.tsx`, `apps/web/app/workspaces/page.tsx`

The finding's sweep (`grep -rniE 'skip[ -]?(to|link)|gn-skip'` over four source trees) returned **zero lines** while the same sweep for `aria-label` returned 166, so the instrument traverses; **the lane WITHDREW the WCAG 2.4.1 *Bypass Blocks* citation** (landmarks satisfy it) and the surviving core is filed MINOR — the fix is argued from the measurement, not from a criterion the product already meets. Measured both ways with the `ui` package rebuilt: `preventDefault()` alone in the bubble phase left the case red (`expected "spy" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`), the capture argument is what turned it green. It deliberately does not `stopPropagation()`, so a field inside the sheet that handles Escape still receives the event. It was shadow-only under `neo` and fill-difference under `hig`/`minimal`, and a shadow was rejected as a second mechanism for one boundary. Only the UNTINTED variant was affected: `tint` is opt-in and the four `--gn-avatar--tint-*` rules set their own fill, which is why it read as intermittent. The initials still clear 4.5 as read text on the composites in all three styles and both themes (measured 8.75–10.83). Case 13.732. **THE SHEET AND ITS SCRIM NOW MOVE (owner report, 2026-09-19, case 13.961).** The owner: *"gn-sheet__scrim. the surface that shows when you open a ticket. check with the prototype and match it."* **The COLOUR was already right** in all four style × theme combinations — measured against the prototype's `--overlay` from both sides and again rendered — so the mismatch was MOTION: `.gn-sheet__scrim` computed to `animation: none 0s`, `.gn-sheet` had none at all, and `gnSlide` existed nowhere, so the sheet snapped open. Both now carry the prototype's own values (`desktop.dc.html@6d7b67c0a52c`): `gnFade .2s ease` on the scrim — which all four of its scrims carry — and `gnSlide .26s cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)` over a `translateX(28px)` on the panel, a travel checked against OUR width rather than copied blind (its sheet is 660px, ours is 640px, both docked right). **ALL THREE MODAL PANELS ARE NOW ANIMATED, and the sentence that said otherwise was the change's own worst error.** An earlier version of this bullet claimed **"the prototype draws no centred dialog anywhere"**, left `.gn-dialog` unanimated on that basis, and called `gnRise` a keyframe "used by nothing". **Every part of that was false.** A grep for the scrims' `background:var(--overlay)` returns four hits; three are side panels, and the fourth — `desktop.dc.html:1570` — is the scrim of a **CENTRED** dialog whose container (`:1569`) is `align-items:center;justify-content:center` and whose panel (`:1571`) carries exactly `animation:gnRise .24s cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)`; `mobile.dc.html:1206-1208` draws the same pair. *The grep was run; the step that would have falsified the reading — checking each hit's CONTAINER rather than the hit — was not.* So `.gn-dialog` now rises on the prototype's own `gnRise .24s` over `translateY(14px)`, the fade is on the SHARED `.gn-dialog__scrim, .gn-sheet__scrim` rule **which the prototype does support**, and the guard count is stated as it is: the `animation: none` shape was used **once** before this change (`.gn-help`'s), not three times — the others cover `transition`. **`ui.css`'s own `gnFade` comment was corrected in the same change**, because it said the keyframes lived at the foot of the Help section *"rather than in a shared block"* on the grounds that `gnFade` was *the only animation in this stylesheet* — which the overlay work makes false; all three keyframes now sit in a shared block at the head of the file. **No unit test can see any of this** (jsdom has no layout engine and no animation timeline), so the case is a declared-value scan whose docblock states its own blind spots, and **the motion itself was watched in a real browser** — Chromium via Playwright over the same stylesheet bytes and the component's own markup, with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated at the engine level. **That case's own uniqueness check was refuted and repaired in the same round:** it asserted "exactly one rule per selector" while covering only `.gn-sheet__scrim` and filtering out `none`, so an appended `.gn-sheet { animation: none; }` left the suite green with the motion dead — measured in a browser. It now counts every declaration on all three selectors, and that mutation reddens it. **The prototype's "Full screen" ticket mode is a named GAP, not built**: it turns the scrim into `var(--surface)` and makes the panel full-bleed (`sheetFullLabel`, used at `:1119`) — a feature, not a scrim value. **Modal focus containment (P8, 2026-09-21, case 13.1052):** `Dialog` and `Sheet` both declared `aria-modal="true"` — a claim that everything outside them is inert — while moving no focus, trapping none and restoring none. Failure was measurable on the running stack (focus stayed on the opener; a real Tab walked out of an open dialog into the page behind it; Escape left focus on `<body>`), and it was not inert in the product: `board.tsx:385-393` refuses a column action precisely because it judges the interaction to have arrived behind a modal as a keyboard-focus escape. Both primitives now focus the panel itself on open (`tabIndex={-1}` on the panel, not its first focusable child, so the dialog's own name is announced rather than the dismiss control's), contain Tab within it, and return focus to the opener on close, via `@react-aria/focus`'s `FocusScope contain restoreFocus` — the same standard the project page's filters sheet already met on a less-used surface (13.445/13.446). `packages/ui/src/components/`, `packages/ui/src/ui.css`, `packages/ui/test/sheet-motion.test.ts`

The ghost button gets the rule it never had. Measured 2026-09-22 — the ticket sheet's Priority row did exactly that and every case stayed green — and case `3.974` now pins the track against shadowing. **Radius is style-axis-driven as of Task 14 (2026-09-09)** — `.gn-segmented`/`.gn-segmented__item`/`.gn-field__input`/`.gn-refusal` read `var(--gn-radius-control)`, `.gn-page-header__icon` reads `var(--gn-radius-card)`, and the segmented on-state and `.gn-shell__refusal`/`.gn-shell__expired` (`apps/web/app/globals.css`) follow the same pattern. **Under `data-style="neo"` only, the field input takes the pure neomorphic look — sunken, no border** (owner ruling 2026-09-09): `[data-style="neo"] .gn-field__input` drops 13.291's border for `background: var(--gn-surface-sunken)` and `box-shadow: var(--gn-shadow-sunken)`; `hig`/`minimal` keep the bordered look unchanged. The shadow-edge contrast (1.24 light / 1.16 dark, both below 3:1) is an OWNER-ACCEPTED WAIVER, recorded rather than hidden. Case 13.339. **The SELECTED SEGMENT joins it under `neo`, 2026-09-15 (owner: *"in the prototype it was sunken style. i want it to follow that"*)** — `[data-style="neo"] .gn-segmented__item--on` (at the time) overrode the base `var(--gn-shadow-raised)` with `var(--gn-shadow-sunken)`, so the chosen segment read as PRESSED rather than lifted. The reference does not give this control one treatment but five, splitting on the style axis (`--segOnShadow` in `design-system/interactive/desktop.dc.html`): a drop shadow under `hig` in both themes, `none` under `minimal`, and `inset` pairs under `neo` in both — and the `neo` pair's own geometry (3px/3px/6px) matches neither existing shadow role exactly, which the two-role approximation above papered over. The base rule was already correct for two of the three styles at the time — `--gn-shadow-raised` resolves to `none` under `minimal` — and only `neo` was inverted, which is precisely why it read as backwards: `neo` is the shipped default. **Superseded owner round 5 (2026-09-16): a dedicated fifth `ShadowRole`, `selected`, replaces the two-role approximation** — see the Design-tokens bullet above for the primitive reuse. The base rule now reads `var(--gn-shadow-selected)` directly and resolves correctly for all five style×theme combinations without any `[data-style="neo"]` override for `box-shadow`; the override survives only for `background: var(--gn-surface-sunken)`, which is NOT `var(--gn-surface-raised)` as an earlier draft of this entry said — `neo`'s `surfaceRaised` and `surfaceSunken` are in fact byte-identical (`neoPaper` light, `neoNavy` dark, both collapsed to one hex by design), so the correction changes no rendered pixel, only the accuracy of this sentence and of `ui.css`'s own inline comment. Being the shared control, it moves everywhere `SegmentedControl` is used — sign-in's method picker, `/account`'s appearance rows, `/help`'s Manual/FAQ switch, the ticket-type editor — which is the intent, since the reference defines the component once. **The TRACK FILL came off in the same breath** (owner: *"the background also needs to be removed from the tablist"*) — `.gn-segmented` no longer paints `var(--gn-fill-tertiary)`, because once the selected segment is a well pressed into the page, a tint behind the whole control gives that well a second ground to compose against; geometry keeps the segments apart instead. **Both were caught being wrong by a test before they went further, which is the part worth recording:** `13.362` witnesses the selected tab's rendered `box-shadow` in a real Chromium page, and the first commit of the sunken change claimed nothing in the suite read a computed style here — it reddened on all three viewports. That assertion now pins the `inset` geometry AND that the old raised geometry is gone, and its declared-value control moved from `--gn-fill-tertiary` (which this component no longer uses, so it would have stayed green while naming a property that had ceased to exist) to `--gn-surface-sunken`. Cases 13.400–13.401, 13.362. **`.gn-page-header__icon` fills with `var(--gn-brand)` and labels with `var(--gn-text-inverted)`, not `accent`/`accentText`, Round 2d (2026-09-09)** — the owner's neo prototype fills this exact tile with its one fixed brand hue, not the theme-varying accent. `border-radius` stays `var(--gn-radius-card)`, unchanged: the export hardcodes a 14px literal here under every style it ships (including its own `hig` default), which maps cleanly to neither `card` (20px under neo) nor `control` (14px under neo, coincidentally) — flagged as a minor, out-of-scope geometry delta rather than guessed at. `.gn-button--ghost` now reads `var(--gn-text-accent)`, not `var(--gn-accent)` — see the design-tokens bullet above for why. It now carries a roving `tabindex` (one stop for the whole tablist, arrows within it), ArrowLeft/ArrowRight with wraparound, and Home/End, with selection following focus. ArrowUp/ArrowDown are deliberately not handled (optional in the pattern; claiming them would swallow vertical scrolling), and `aria-controls`/`tabpanel` is deliberately not added because the component is generic across seven render sites of two kinds — panel switchers (the sheet's *Details*/*History*, the help browser's sections) and setting/route switchers (the theme and style toggles, `/inbox`, `/sign-in`) — and inventing a panel relationship for callers that have none would be a worse claim than the one being fixed. **A fifth shared piece, `Popover` (sheet prototype parity, Task 1, 2026-09-22)** — `packages/ui/src/components/popover.tsx`, an anchored `role="dialog"` overlay on the same `@react-aria/overlays`/`@react-aria/focus` pieces `Select`'s panel already uses (`useOverlay`, `useOverlayPosition`, `FocusScope`, `DismissButton`), portalled to `document.body`, dismissed by Escape or an outside click, focus trapped inside and restored to the trigger on close. It is the product's first popover, built because the visibility menu (Task 5) needs an anchored fieldset dialog and `Select`'s listbox panel is not that shape. Cases 13.1267–13.1268.
- ⚙️ **Shared `Switch` and `InfoTip`** (`packages/ui/src/components/switch.tsx`, `info-tip.tsx`, 2026-09-18) — the two primitives the Settings → Workspace restyle added to the shared package. **`Switch`** is the `/account` notifications control HOISTED, not reimplemented: its CSS moved out of `apps/web/app/globals.css` (where it was five rule bodies plus a reduced-motion arm, all scoped to `.gn-account__notification-row input[type='checkbox']`, reachable only from that one page) into `ui.css` as `.gn-switch`, and both call sites now render this one component — the task's ruling was *"extract it into a shared component and use it in both places rather than copying its CSS; two toggles that drift is the divergence this repo keeps paying for."* Declarations are the originals: 51×31 track, 27px knob, the 20px of travel, and the `borderStrong` ring on the knob that pays WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 in both states and both themes (the ring exists because the prototype's hardcoded `#fff` knob is unrepresentable — no always-white role exists, the palette being theme-aware by design). It renders a real `<input type="checkbox">` restyled rather than a `role="switch"` div, so label association, checked state, disabled state and keyboard behaviour are the element's own; **the stated consequence is that to assistive technology it reads as a checkbox, not a switch.** What this component does NOT carry is `justify-content: space-between` — that is ACCOUNT row layout and stayed on `.gn-account__notification-row`, because a switch in a form field wants its control beside its label, not at the far edge of a card. **`InfoTip`** is the ⓘ disclosure beside a field, opening on hover, focus and click and closing on Escape, blur, pointer-leave or an outside click. Its mechanism is `last-project-nav.tsx`'s disclosure reduced to a single non-menu panel, and it is deliberately NOT a `title=` attribute (`ui.css:322` records the product's ruling against those). Three divergences from the nav item, each with a reason: no `suppressNextFocusOpen` ref (Escape does not move focus here, so the loop it breaks cannot form), no `role="menu"`/arrow-key navigation (one paragraph of prose is not a set of choices), and it does not take focus on open (it opens ON focus, so pulling focus inward would swallow anyone tabbing through the form). **Its `onClick` OPENS rather than toggling**, and that is a fix rather than a preference: a click focuses a button first, so React runs `onFocus` (open) and then `onClick`, and a toggling handler would read the state it had just been given and close the panel again — a click that appears to do nothing. **The panel is in the DOM only while open, so this is a DISCLOSURE and not a description**: the field it explains carries no `aria-describedby` pointing at it, and activating the button inserts a `role="note"` node that is never ANNOUNCED — no live region, no focus move — so a screen-reader user must go looking for it while a sighted user watches it appear. Both halves of that limit are recorded rather than implied away. **Two corrections the review forced, each measured rather than re-worded:** the panel carries a `border`, and that is load-bearing — it is `surfaceRaised` on a card that is also `surfaceRaised`, and `SHADOWS.minimal.raised` is `[]`, so under `minimal` the shadow resolves to `none` and the border is the only thing drawing an edge; and the trigger is **24×24**, the product's own floor for a dense in-list control (`ui.css:1246-1249`), where it shipped at 20×20. **A recorded gap with a named owner:** the 44px tap ratchet never sees this control because no roster covers the settings routes at all (`e2e-viewport/viewports.ts:171-176`, `e2e-stack/viewport.spec.ts:419-427`) — the ratchet stays green over a page it does not walk.
