- ⚙️ **Ticket sheet — per-field attribution, both clocks, rule-driven transitions** — `TicketSheet`, with `HistoryList`, `TransitionDialog`/`transitionOptions` and the `EditorSlot` seam beside it. Every field row is a VALUE plus WHO claimed it and WHEN, because a value with no claim beside it reads as a property the ticket has — the laundering invariant 4 forbids — and a nameless actor is attributed by raw id through `actorLabel`, never blank and never "system". **THE LOCATION BREADCRUMB NAMES EACH ANCESTOR ONCE, EVEN WHEN THE PARENT IS THE EPIC (E4-1/E5-3, release B08, 2026-09-21):** the server's ancestry walk returns the first epic ancestor starting from the parent, so when the direct parent IS an epic, `epic.id === parent.id` — and the bar rendered both, reading `Convenience Corner › Shop operations › Open questions › Open questions › CCSO-6`. That is 23 of the 26 seeded tickets, and a path naming one node twice states a depth the hierarchy does not have. One id comparison now omits the epic crumb when it is the parent; a `restricted` ancestor is covered by the same line, since both `ParentRef` arms carry an id. Case 17.024. **AND THE PARENT CRUMB CARRIES THE PARENT'S KEY (P3, same release):** the prototype labels its parent crumb `p.id + " " + p.title` and the product could not, because the wire carried no key for an ancestor — so a ticket whose epic and parent shared a title drew two identical crumbs. The parent ref now carries `key` (a string, or `null` when the number falls outside the snapshot, or absent for the grandparent, whose crumb is title-only in the prototype too), and only the PARENT crumb renders it. Case 17.027. **AND THE CRUMBS THAT OPEN SOMETHING ARE PAINTED IN A ROLE (E4-30, same release):** the ancestor crumb is a real `<button>`, whose rule declared `color: inherit` and was justified by a false inference from the prototype — its `<a>` sets no colour of its own, but the export's `a{color:var(--accent)}` at `:86` is a TYPE selector that beats inheritance, and **a `<button>` inherits where an `<a>` does not**. The crumb was therefore painted in exactly the ink of the non-link crumbs beside it: `cursor: pointer` and the UA focus ring were the only tells. It now takes `var(--gn-text-accent)`. Case 17.025. **The history line's HEADLINE is a SENTENCE about the change, not the wire name of the event (E4-19/E5-8, release B08, 2026-09-21):** the tab used to print `event.type` verbatim, so `CCSO-6`'s six rows read `ticket.created`, `ticket.field_set` ×3, `ticket.transitioned`, `visibility.set` — three identical lines with nothing saying which field changed or to what. `describeEvent` (`packages/app-core/src/views/history-copy.ts`) now builds each sentence from the payload the route already selects — *"Set dueDate to 30 Aug 2026"*, *"Moved to Doing"*, *"Cleared priority"* — with the wire name KEPT beside it in `.gn-history__slug`; the complaint was never that the slug was on screen but that it was the only thing on screen. An event type the file has not learned, or a payload it cannot read, falls back to the raw type rather than to an invented sentence, and person and state names go through the SAME resolvers the rows beside them use (`actorLabel` included, so an empty name falls back to the id). Cases 3.179–3.181. **E5-8 (the independent duplicate of this ruling) added a CENSUS:** every event type registered against entity kind `ticket` — read off the domain's own `TICKET_EVENT_TYPES` ∪ `CONTEST_EVENT_TYPES` ∪ {`visibility.set`}, never retyped in the test — must narrate, and the census is what found that `attachment.added` and `claim.contested_resolved` were still falling through to the wire name (two rows of eighteen). Cases 3.183–3.184. **The history tab shows BOTH CLOCKS on every line, labelled** (`claimed (device clock)` / `recorded (server)`): the claimed clock is the actor's claim about when and the recorded one is the system's record of when, both true in different senses, and a surface showing one under the word "when" asserts a moment the record never made. The fixture that proves it is skewed by THREE DAYS on purpose, so showing either clock alone prints a different string and either mutation dies; clocks seconds apart would make the whole battery vacuous. The zone is named once from the domain's `IST_CLOCK_NOTE`, and both clocks are checked unmoved from three zones against expectations computed without `formatIstInstant`. **These zone batteries are REGRESSION GUARDS, not live discriminations:** `formatIstInstant` and `formatDate` are constant +05:30 arithmetic over the UTC getters (`packages/domain/src/clock-skew.ts:51`, `packages/domain/src/ist-day.ts`) and read no local zone, so every zone prints one string against today's code and the zone loop cannot fail — measured 2026-09-02 against a `toLocale*` control in the same run that answered a different calendar day. The `TZ` probe establishes that the KNOB moves and nothing more. The teeth are the mutation: swapping in a device-reading formatter kills these cases, and each block now names its own kill count at the site. The three parent facts stay three — a RESTRICTED parent renders as existence-without-title, never as `At project root`. Transitions are prompted by the workflow's own declared rules (a comment box only where `require-comment` sits, a field only where it is not already claimed, and — where `require-evidence` sits — a real upload, with the honest sentence *"Evidence upload is not available in this build yet"* surviving ONLY for a host that supplies no uploader, which both of the web's mounts now do supply; a refused or unreachable upload gets its own sentence in the server/transport split Ruling 27 established), **where a wildcard edge and an exact edge both reach one target, the EXACT edge supplies the rules and declaration order does not matter — the engine's own resolution (`find(exact) ?? find('*')`), matched here under ruling P27 after `transitionOptions` was found resolving by declaration order while `precheck.ts` resolved correctly, one package holding two answers to one question**, the instant pre-check is advisory and prints nothing when it passes, and the SERVER's refusal renders verbatim in an `alert` beside — never instead of — a disagreeing preview. **The preview is asked what the SUBMISSION will carry, and `require-field` is the rule kind that does not fit in a payload:** `require-comment` and `require-evidence` are read from the candidate, so their values ride it; `require-field` is read from the TICKET STATE (`packages/rule-engine/src/rules/require-field.ts:9`), so the dialog's collected field values ride `precheckEvent`'s `pendingFields` and are applied to the ticket the engine is handed — the preview's stand-in for the ordered batch the real path sends. Before this the dialog rendered an input for the field, cleared its own `blocked` the moment the person typed, and kept printing *"instant check — require-field: … and it is not."* beside an ENABLED Move, for ever. Case 3.185. **`require-comment` is the third rule kind and the second half of the same omission, read off the PAYLOAD by `evaluateRequireComment` (`payload.comment?.text`): the comment box's typed value now rides the candidate, trimmed as the submission trims it, and the effect re-asks when it changes — before this the box appeared, typing enabled Move, and *"instant check — require-comment: … and none was provided."* stayed printed beside it, the exact defect the evidence fix had already closed one rule kind over. Case 3.186.** **The ledger payload is the SHIPPED spelling**, `{to, comment: {text}}` per `ticketTransitionedPayloadSchema`, not the plan's `{toStateId, comment: 'string'}` — which both the ingest door and the rule engine refuse as malformed, and which the local pre-check would put in front of the user as `malformed-payload: … at to: Required`. The workflow is read at the version the TICKET PINS, not at latest. `getTicket` REFUSED against the shipped server of the day and the refusal reached the surface AS a refusal, under its own class, with the string `Loading…` nowhere (**⚠ CORRECTED 2026-09-20: this read "`getTicket` REFUSES today (`ServingGapError`)" in the present tense. Ruling P25 clause 1 — `c86c4b5c`, 2026-09-06 — served that read, and the register has been empty since 2026-09-19. The BRANCH is unchanged and still right: a served read can still FAIL, and the property is that a failure never renders as a wait.** — the plan's single `{read.error ?? 'Loading…'}` branch dressed a permanent serving gap as a wait that will end. **The History tab makes the same three-way distinction, and the ledger is where it matters most:** `useLiveQuery` leaves `data` null both while a read is in flight and after it rejects, so the tab's earlier single `history.data ?? []` drew an empty `<ol>` for pending, failed and empty alike — on the surface that IS the ledger, an empty list reads as *this ticket has no history*. Loading, failure and empty are now three renderings under three classes, with `error` tested BEFORE `data === null` because on a rejection both hold. The failure is worded and classed as an ERROR rather than a refusal: `getTicketHistory` ANSWERS — as, since 2026-09-19, does every method, `SERVING_GAPS` being empty (this read "one of the six methods", ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-09-20) — so it may succeed on a retry, and wearing `gn-ticket-sheet__refusal` would be a false claim in the CSS. The empty branch describes the ANSWER (*No entries came back for this ticket.*), never the ticket, because the online source returns `[]` on a 404 and a live ticket always carries at least its own `ticket.created`. **And the ledger is paged:** the shipped route defaults to 200 rows (`apps/server/src/routes/ticket-history.ts:78`), so the sheet asks with an explicit `HISTORY_PAGE_LIMIT` and says *Showing the first 200 entries — this ticket's history may go on past them* whenever the page comes back full. A full page is the only partiality signal on the wire (no cursor, no `hasMore`), so it over-reports on a ticket with exactly 200 entries — taken deliberately, because an occasional *there may be more* is a weaker claim than the truth where a silent truncation is a stronger one. It also UNDER-reports if the route's `MAX_LIMIT` is ever set below this number: the clamp returns a full-but-short page, the notice does not fire, and no client can tell — recorded at the site as the second reason the two numbers must be kept in step. The dialog is mounted for the sheet's whole life, so after a committed move the comment was still in state and `submit` put it on the wire for the NEXT move: a comment written about move A recorded as move B's. The fix is NOT in the dialog — that effect cannot tell the two closes apart — but in `TicketSheet`, which remounts the dialog per committed move via a `movesCommitted` counter used as its `key`. - ✅ **Close / Reopen from the ticket sheet** (backlog/closed spec §5.3, 2026-09-17) — `TicketSheet` reads `TicketState.closed` (`{actorId, at} | null | undefined`, spec §1.2) straight off the read it already holds, `state.closed ?? null`, the same optional chain every other reader in this plan spells. A terminal, not-yet-closed ticket shows **Close**; a closed one shows **Reopen** and a header badge — *Closed by \<name\> on \<date\>* — the name resolved through the SAME `actorLabel`/roster join every claim on this sheet uses, the date through the one IST formatter (`formatDate`); the badge is a `Chip` (tone `terminal`), not a bespoke swatch. Both buttons submit one event apiece — `ticket.closed` / `ticket.reopened`, `payload: {}` (spec §1.2, the envelope alone carries actor and time) — through the SAME `make`/`ingest`/result idiom `submitTransition` uses for a move, and a `committed` answer reloads both live reads this sheet holds (`read.reload()` AND `history.reload()`, since closing writes a ledger line too). **Move…** is `disabled` while closed, with the sentence "Closed — reopen it first" beside it as TEXT — a `<span className="gn-sheet__closed-note">`, never a `title=` tooltip. A refused Close/Reopen renders its rule and reason verbatim in a NEW refusal slot beside the action row, not `TransitionDialog`'s own `serverRefusal` copy: `Dialog` returns `null` whenever `open` is false (`packages/ui/src/components/dialog.tsx:15`), so that copy is unreachable while the Move dialog is closed — exactly when Close/Reopen fire; the new slot is gated on `!moveOpen` so the two never both render, since the Move dialog's own `onClose` already clears `serverRefusal` and `submitTransition` never sets it while the dialog is closed. **Fix round 1, Ruling 31 (2026-09-17): the sheet's own dismiss button collided with this feature's Close button** — `Sheet`'s header `×` carried `aria-label="Close"`, identical to the new business button's accessible name, so `Sheet` now says `aria-label="Close sheet"` (`packages/ui/src/components/sheet.tsx`; see the Base UI components bullet above). **Ruling 32: a double-submit latch** — `const [submitting, setSubmitting]`, set before the `ingest` call and reset in a `finally` (mirroring `board.tsx`'s `MoveArrows.submitting`, `:956`/`:1029-1035`), with `Close`, `Reopen` and `Delete` carrying `disabled={submitting}` for the lifetime of their own ingest. **`Move…` WAS 'untouched, since it opens a dialog with its own submit path' — AND THAT SENTENCE IS NOW FALSE (E5-27, release B08, 2026-09-21).** The dialog's own submit path had no latch at all and no transport arm, so a slow or dropped Move left the dialog open with Move still enabled: *still sending*, *already failed* and *already succeeded* looked identical to the person deciding whether to press again. `submitTransition` now wears the SAME latch (`if (submitting) return` + `setSubmitting` in a `finally`), and `TransitionDialog` gained an optional `submitting` prop that disables its Move button (`disabled={blocked || submitting}`) — `blocked` is the FORM's validity and only that, which is why it could never express this. ONE LATCH FOR THE SHEET, deliberately: a sheet with two writes in flight has no single answer to "what is happening", and the Move dialog is modal. The consequence that `Close`/`Reopen`/`Delete` are disabled for the lifetime of a Move's ingest is the correct one rather than a cost. Case 3.182. **Ruling 33 (fix round 2): a REJECTED `ingest` gets its OWN slot, `transportError`, never `serverRefusal`** — fix round 1 had caught the rejection and reported it through `serverRefusal` under a synthetic `ingest-rejected` rule name, which review caught as the exact defect Ruling 27 removed from `board.tsx` (case 13.504): a dropped connection is not the server's own verdict, however the sentence is worded. `transportError` (rendered `<p role="alert" className="gn-refusal gn-refusal--transport">`, gated on `!moveOpen` identically to `serverRefusal`) now carries "We could not reach the server for this change — …" on a rejection and "The server did not answer this change." when `results[0]` is `undefined` (one event ingested, so `results[0]` IS the result — no more `.find(...)`); opening **Move…**, and the Move dialog's own close, now clear both slots together, not `serverRefusal` alone. **E2-29 (release B08, 2026-09-21): the Move path's own `ingest` is guarded, and the DIALOG carries the sentence** — `submitTransition` awaited `dataSource.ingest([...])` with no `catch` and is called as `void submitTransition(submission)`, so a dropped connection during a Move was an unhandled promise rejection; the slot above renders only while the dialog is CLOSED, and the dialog standing in its place was handed the literal `transportError={null}`, so nothing anywhere could speak. The await is now guarded like its sibling writes, and the dialog receives the sheet's own `transportError` — same sentence (*"We could not reach the server for this move — …"*), same `gn-refusal--transport` tone, never the refusal's words (Ruling 27). Case 3.178. **Ruling 34 (fix round 3): the silent-answer branch clears `serverRefusal` too** — a wording gap in Ruling 33 left `results[0] === undefined` setting `transportError` without clearing `serverRefusal`, so a refused click followed by a silent one rendered both notices at once; it now clears both, the same pairing the `catch` branch already carried. Cases 13.585–13.588, 13.588a–13.588c. **THE ASSIGNEE ROW IS EDITABLE (owner ruling, 2026-09-19: *"assignee should not be read only"*), cases `13.966`–`13.968`.** It is a surface on a plane already wired end to end — `ticket.assigned` is projected, read, fanned out, synced and already written by the MCP `assign_ticket` tool — so **no route was added**: the control submits through the same `make`/`ingest`/result idiom the siblings use, and **unassigning is the SAME event carrying `null`** (there is no `ticket.unassigned`; `read/assigned-provenance.ts` enumerates the event set from the reducer rather than guessing a second type), offered as an explicit `Unassigned` option because a picker with no way back cannot express a state the ledger allows. **⚠ TWO DISPATCH PREMISES WERE MEASURED FALSE AND THE FIX IS THE POINT.** (1) The dispatch priced this as *"a picker needs a roster, which is a SEVENTH thing to pass"* — **the sheet already reads the roster itself** for `nameOf` and `VisibilityEditor`, so the candidates were in the component before this task. (2) **The sheet was collapsing a REFUSED roster and a not-yet-loaded one into `[]`** (`members={members.data ?? []}`, with `members.error` read nowhere), which is the value `page.tsx`'s own docblock names as the defect: *"never `[]`, which would claim this workspace has no members."* An assignee picker offering an empty list over a refused roster asserts nobody can be assigned, so the new control **tells three states apart and adds a fourth**: refused / not-loaded / empty, and an assignee **not in the roster you can see** (the read hides guests from a non-admin), where the row says what it can and offers **no control** — because `Select` renders its placeholder when its value matches no option (`select.tsx:255`), the same rule the members page's role control settled. **The single-ticket read gained `assignedProvenance`** — the field `ListCard` has carried since the list existed, added here by calling the reader that list already uses, so the sheet's assignee row can carry the same `set by {actor} on {date}` its siblings do. Cases `13.966` (the server read, mutation-witnessed), `13.967` (`mapTicketRead` carries it and **refuses a body that OMITS the key** — absent is not `null`), `13.968` (the row: the list, the submission, the unassign payload asserted with `toEqual`, and the refusal arm with no control at all). **RULING E4-18 (closed):** the picker's options were built `...people.map((member) => ({ value: member.id, label: member.name }))` — `member.name` verbatim, which rendered a BLANK option for a member with no display name (a real, seeded fixture: `accountant@e2e.gisik-nokma.local`, `name: ''`), breaking the same honesty contract `provenance.ts` states for every other actor label on this sheet and that the sibling `visibility-editor.tsx` picker already keeps via `actorLabel`. The Assignee picker now routes through `actorLabel(member.id, member.name)` too, so a nameless member reads by id rather than as nothing. **RULING E5-4 (closed), the same defect's other two sites on this sheet:** `queryUsers` (the @mention list this ticket's description/comment editors read) filtered on `member.name.toLowerCase().includes(needle)` and mapped `name: member.name` verbatim — a nameless member was both invisible (a blank row if listed) and unreachable (typing anything could never match an empty string). The label is now resolved through `actorLabel` BEFORE matching, not after, so a nameless member is found by typing their id, the same way any other person is found by what the list actually shows for them. `packages/app-core/src/views/ticket-sheet.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/ui.css` — `const [submitting, setSubmitting]`, set before the `ingest` call and reset in a `finally` (mirroring `board.tsx`'s `MoveArrows.submitting`, `:956`/`:1029-1035`), with both `Close` and `Reopen` carrying `disabled={submitting}` for the lifetime of their own ingest; `Move…` is untouched, since it opens a dialog with its own submit path. **⚠ AND THAT `disabled` IS THE WHOLE GUARD (ruling E2-31, 2026-09-21).** The function also carried `if (submitting) return;` at its top, documented as guarding "a second click landing on the same render pass as the first, before React has re-rendered the `disabled` attribute onto the DOM" — which it could not do, because `submitting` is RENDER STATE and two calls in one render pass both close over the same pre-commit `false`. The line is REMOVED rather than kept as belt-and-braces: a guard whose stated purpose is unreachable is indistinguishable from a working one to every future reader. **The finding offers this remedy and a `submittingRef`, and the ref was declined for a measured reason** — the precedent it cites (`TicketEditorSlot.tsx`, "two `comment.added` events for one comment") reached its handler from TWO sources, a Save button AND a blur/Enter commit, and the `disabled` landing on the field is what fired the second; Close/Reopen has one source and no blur-commit, so copying that fix here would install a second guard that also cannot fire. - ⚙️ **The reopen-option flow — live children under terminal parents (owner decision)** — `submitChildEvent` / `reopenAndProceed` / `reopenStateOptions` (`src/flows/guarded-child-event.ts`) with `NewTicketDialog`, `ReopenDialog` and the wired `CreateTicketFlow`. A `hierarchy.parent-terminal` refusal is not an error: it is the moment the offer appears, at the moment of refusal, never silently applied. On acceptance the parent's `ticket.transitioned` — carrying `cause: {kind:'reopened-for-child', childTicketId}` and the SHIPPED destination spelling `to` — is ingested in its own awaited call BEFORE the child's, because the parent must be non-terminal by the time the child claim is evaluated; the child is the SAME envelope that was refused, since an interactive refusal records nothing. **The parent workflow's own transition rules still apply to the reopen:** its refusal surfaces verbatim and the child is never sent, which is what keeps the flow from being a permission escalation wearing a convenience's name. State options are STRUCTURAL only — non-terminal targets with a declared edge, rule-bearing ones included, so the server and not this client decides them. A refusal wears the name of whoever made it: `refusalOrigin` renders the instant pre-check as `instant check — ` (and submits nothing at all on that path) and only an answer that came back through `ingest` as `Refused by the server — `. A post-reopen child refusal reports both truths and compensates nothing away — the reopen is recorded history. **Known gap:** CLOSED by ruling P25 clause 1 — the offer needs the parent's state and workflow from `getTicket`, which REFUSED against the shipped server (`ServingGapError`) and now answers, so the flow builds the offer online. The refusal PATH is still pinned by 3.80 against a stubbed refusal, because what it guards is the flow's behaviour when a read it needs does not answer, whatever the cause, so online the flow renders the refusal and says the offer could not be built rather than guessing — case 3.80. **Ruling 37 (backlog/closed spec §2, 2026-09-17, Task 9): on a CLOSED parent — not merely terminal — the accepted reopen ingests `ticket.reopened` (empty payload) and the transition together, reopen FIRST, in ONE `source.ingest` batch call, before the child ever goes out; a merely-terminal (not closed) parent's batch stays the single-element array every case before this task exercised.** `ReopenPlan` gained `parentClosed: boolean`, set by `CreateTicketFlow` off `parentRead.ticket.closed ?? null` (the domain flag is optional on 441 fixtures that predate it) rather than `!== null` alone, which would misread an unflagged legacy ticket as closed. Results are read back in the batch's own order; `parentResult` in a committed outcome is always the TRANSITION's — the last element — never the reopen's. Cases 13.593a–c (`test/flows/guarded-child-event.test.ts`), 13.593 (`test/views/reopen-flow.test.tsx`). **ONE MODAL AT A TIME (E2-34, 2026-09-21):** the offer used to stack ON the New-ticket dialog — the `needs-reopen` arm returned with `dialogOpen` untouched and `open` was `dialogOpen` alone, so the DOM held two `aria-modal="true"` dialogs and told assistive technology the top one was the only modal on the page. The offer now REPLACES that dialog and hands it back when it closes, so `dialogOpen` keeps meaning "the person is composing" (the draft survives the detour) while exactly one modal renders. E5-20 (case 3.189) fixed the Escape half of the same stack; neither implies the other. - ⚙️ **`BoardFilterSpec` and `matchesBoardCard` — a filter vocabulary the board can actually answer (Task 3, 2026-09-16)** — the plan's own draft proposed a `boardCardToFilterState` adapter synthesizing a `TicketState` from a `BoardCard` so the board could reuse `matchesFilter` directly. **Rejected before being built.** `matchesFilter` fails CLOSED on every axis a `BoardCard` cannot supply — `collaboratorIds` runs `some()` over the `[]` a card has no way to carry, `dueBefore`/`dueAfter` read `claimedDueDay`, which returns `null` for a card with no claimed date, and a `fields` clause compares `null` to the wanted value — so a synthesized state would not narrow the board, it would EMPTY it, while the list tab showed real matches on the same data. Building the adapter would also mean fabricating a `FieldClaim` with an invented `actorId`/`clientTime`/`serverTime` just to satisfy `state.fields['title']`, inventing provenance nobody claimed in a product whose whole ledger is about who claimed what and when. `BoardFilterSpec` is instead `Pick<FilterSpec, 'text' | 'assigneeIds' | 'typeIds' | 'stateIds' | 'stateCategories' | 'projectIds'>` — derived with `Pick`, never hand-copied, so it cannot drift into a second vocabulary — and the four axes a board cannot answer become a **compile error** at the call site rather than a wrong answer on screen. `matchesBoardCard(card, column, projectId, spec)` evaluates the six axes directly off `BoardCard`/`BoardColumn`, agreeing with `matchesFilter` axis for axis (asserted, not assumed: a 13-case corpus runs the identical spec through both predicates against equivalent card/ticket fixtures, plus an anti-vacuous control proving at least one case actually rejects — agreement alone would pass if both sides answered `true` to everything). The compile-time negative is witnessed, not just claimed: temporarily widening the `Pick` to bare `FilterSpec` and re-running `tsc` turns both `@ts-expect-error` directives on `collaboratorIds` and `dueBefore` into `TS2578` ("Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive") — proof the narrowing itself is what rejects those axes, not a typo the compiler happened not to catch. One signature, not two: Task 4 (the `N of M shown` count) and Task 6 (which cards render) both call `matchesBoardCard` per card from the same pass, so the count is never computed independently of the render. `CalendarView`/`TimelineView` already accept a `filter?: FilterSpec` prop, confirmed by reading `calendar-view.tsx`/`timeline-view.tsx`, but wiring it is explicitly out of this task, since narrowing those tabs with no count and no chip would itself violate the invariant this task exists to satisfy) — naming the scope in the control's own name is what stops it from being a control that implies a reach it does not have. **`.gn-project__summary` is DELETED**, not left declared-and-unconsumed a second task running: the count that shipped is `.gn-project__count` inside the new strip, at its own metrics, never a reuse of the old rule. **The Filters button is NOT rendered in this task** — Task 5 owns the sheet, and an inert button that opens nothing would itself be a control that lies; it ships once it has real behaviour. **`.gn-view-tabs` is deleted from `globals.css` in this task (coordinator Ruling 7)**, both its rules (`:1244`, formerly `:1391-1392`) and the docblock sentence claiming it "survives… only on the project page" — false the moment Task 2 moved this page's own tab rail onto `.gn-segmented`, and left uncorrected in the file for one extra task rather than two. **Test 2 of the brief's own Step 5 could not be run as literally written**, and the substitution is recorded because it is a real deviation backed by a primary source: `getBoard(projectId: string)` (`data-source.ts:134`) takes no filter argument at all, so the board's own `M` is the complete board total under every value of the "Only tickets in progress" toggle, and the brief's assertion that a bare `M` would falsely claim "the project holds `M` tickets when it holds more" cannot be true of it. The real, reachable hazard is `M` sourced from `list.rows.length` (which the toggle DOES narrow, server-side) instead of from `board.data` — case 13.436 reproduces exactly that (a three-card board, a TWO-row list, the toggle on) and asserts the count reads the board's three, never the list-sourced "1 of 2". Cases 13.435–13.438 (later widened to 13.441, see the fix-round paragraph below). `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/p/[projectId]/page.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/ui.css`, `apps/web/app/globals.css`, `apps/web/test/board-narrowing.test.tsx`

**Task 4 fix round 1, same day — coordinator Ruling 10 (the search box's own reach was undisclosed) and concern 4 (an unexecuted pure function).** Two independent findings from the controller's review of the DONE_WITH_CONCERNS report. **First, `13.436` as originally shipped could not discriminate the bug it claimed to catch:** its list fixture was zero rows, so ANY wrong `M` — not only a `list.rows`-sourced one — would fail its one assertion equally; rewritten to a two-row list fixture (nonzero, unequal to the board's three) plus a negative assertion naming the specific wrong string ("1 of 2 shown") a `list.rows`-sourced bug would actually print, and confirmed by mutation: temporarily wiring `boardNarrowing`'s `total` to `list.rows?.length ?? 0` was verified to render that exact string and fail the case, before the production code was reverted byte-for-byte. **Second, and the one real behaviour change: the search box's reach was undisclosed on the tabs it does not narrow.** The box sits in the page header on every tab (Task 2's own reserved container), but only the BOARD path applies it — the identical asymmetry the spec's own search ruling exists to prevent ("one search box would... answer differently on two tabs"), now approached from the opposite direction: a WIRE search would have narrowed the list and left the board unnarrowed; this CLIENT search narrows the board and leaves List/Calendar/Timeline unnarrowed with nothing on screen saying so — a sighted person on those tabs types into the box and watches nothing happen. Fixed with the SAME mechanism already built rather than new UI: on every tab but Board, a `.gn-project__scope-note`-styled line reads *"Search narrows the board only — nothing on this tab is filtered by it yet"* — gated on a search term actually being present (a permanent sentence on three tabs would be noise nobody reads) and never on Board itself (where the limit would be a lie, since the search DOES apply there). Case 13.439. **The board's own scope-note logic (`describeUnappliedBoardAxes`) was also extracted** out of `page.tsx`'s inline `useMemo` into a standalone pure function (`apps/web/src/board-search-scope.ts`) specifically so it has a UNIT test that calls it directly (cases 13.440–13.441) rather than shipping with zero executions until Task 5's Filters sheet became its first real caller — the controller's own framing: "a function that ships having never executed is the thing that turns out to throw on its first real call." `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/p/[projectId]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/board-search-scope.ts`, `apps/web/test/board-narrowing.test.tsx`, `apps/web/test/board-search-scope.test.ts`

**Task 4 code review, same day — one Important finding: the disclosure gate enumerated a DIFFERENT axis set than the narrowing did.** `page.tsx`'s strip was gated on `activeFilterChips.length > 0 || boardUnappliedAxes.length > 0` — but `activeFilterChips` covered only `text`, `boardUnappliedAxes` covered only the four board-blind axes, while the `boardFilter` object handed to `matchesBoardCard` carries **six** (`text`, `assigneeIds`, `typeIds`, `stateIds`, `stateCategories`, `projectIds`). Five of those six could narrow the rendered cards while tripping neither gate term, silently failing to render the count and chip on cards that had, in fact, been dropped — `board.tsx:216-219` exactly. Not a live bug (only `text` has a UI control today), but reachable the instant Task 5's Filters sheet or Task 8's workflow picker writes any other axis onto the same state, which the code's own docblock says they will. **Two independent remedies, not redundant — they cover different mechanisms.** (1) The chip list is now built by `buildFilterChips` (renamed 2026-09-17; was `buildBoardFilterChips`) (`apps/web/src/board-search-scope.ts`) reading `boardFilter` itself — one enumeration of the six axes, not two hand-kept in sync — with a human-readable label and a working `onRemove` per axis: `Assignee`/`Type`/`State` resolve an id through a name map (the roster, `typeOptions`, and the board's own column names respectively, falling back to the raw id when unresolved), `Category` capitalises the bare enum value, and `Project` — no name source exists on a page already scoped to one project — states a count. (2) The gate gained a THIRD, independent term: `boardNarrowing.shown !== boardNarrowing.total` (`shouldRenderNarrowingStrip`, renamed 2026-09-17; was `shouldRenderBoardNarrowingStrip`), because Task 8's workflow picker is specified to narrow by dropping whole GROUPS, never by setting a filter axis — no enumeration of axes, however complete, could ever notice that on its own; only a fact about the actual render (fewer cards shown than exist) can. The reviewer asked for a test that would fail without remedy 2 specifically; since that state (narrowing present, no axis set) cannot be constructed from this page's own current inputs, `13.443` tests `shouldRenderNarrowingStrip` (renamed 2026-09-17; was `shouldRenderBoardNarrowingStrip`, which `13.443`'s describe title still names) as a gate expression directly rather than writing a page-render test that would pass for the wrong reason. `boardFilter` itself was also promoted out of `boardNarrowing`'s own memo into its own `useMemo`, so both consumers read the identical value. One Minor alongside it: Ruling 10's mirror note (`13.439`) had List/Timeline coverage but not Calendar — added (`13.444`). Cases 13.442–13.444. `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/p/[projectId]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/board-search-scope.ts`, `apps/web/test/board-search-scope.test.ts`, `apps/web/test/board-narrowing.test.tsx`

Five of `BoardFilterSpec`'s six axes get a control (`text` already had the search box): Assignee and Collaborators as "person row" checkbox lists over the workspace roster (**RULING E5-4 (closed):** both rows rendered `member.name` verbatim, which was blank for the magic-link population — the same defect E4-18 closed on the ticket sheet's own Assignee picker and the @mention list; here the label is resolved through `actorLabel` before either the visible text or the row's own accessible `label` prop reads it, so a nameless member is findable and checkable rather than a blank, unnamed row), Type and State as "category chip" multi-selects, and Category over the three fixed `stateCategories` values. `projectIds` gets none — the page is already scoped to the one project it shows, and Task 4's own report found no natural label source for it here. `dueBefore`/`dueAfter`/`fields` get no control either: the design spec's Filters-sheet metrics name exactly two control shapes ("person row", "category chip"), and this task's own brief curates those same two into its metrics line while dropping the spec's "Toggle" row entirely — the discriminating fact that no boolean/date control was meant to land here. Also fixed: `.gn-filters__scrim` had no `z-index`, so it would paint below `TicketSheet`'s `.gn-sheet__scrim` (`z-index: 40`) were both ever open at once — invisible to every test here, since jsdom computes no paint order; matched the house scrims' own value rather than inventing a second scale. **Ruling 12 (coordinator remediation, same session): "Clear all" made a promise its own code did not keep.** It cleared the sheet's own five axes and left `text` alone — correct about which control owns the search box, wrong about what the button's own visible label promises. The search `<input>` needed no separate reset — checked, not assumed: it is `value={filter.text ?? ''}`, controlled, no local state — so clearing `filter.text` empties it for free. **Ruling 13 (coordinator remediation, same session): Ruling 12's own fix cleared the WRONG six.** Checked axis-by-axis rather than trusting the "clears all six" claim, the reviewer found `clearAll` included `collaboratorIds` (not a `BoardFilterSpec` axis — no chip) while omitting `projectIds` (one of the six, with a working chip) — harmless only because nothing on this page sets `projectIds` yet. grep-confirmed the only referents anywhere were this file and `ui.css` itself, so the rename breaks nothing). `.gn-board__column` becomes the sunken tray — `--gn-surface-sunken` fill, `--gn-shadow-sunken`, `--gn-radius-card`, 18rem lane, its own `flex-direction: column` layout with a 10px gap between header and card list (which is also why `.gn-board__column-header`'s now-redundant `margin-bottom` was removed — the two would otherwise have stacked to roughly double the spec's own gap). `.gn-board__count`'s selector is kept (`board.test.tsx:142` queries it directly) with its body updated to 13px/18px — a size INCREASE over the prior 12.8px, so the `LABEL_FLOOR_PX` (12px) ratchet in `apps/web/e2e-viewport`/`e2e-stack` cannot regress from it. **`.gn-board-card` gets the padding**, not `.gn-card`: `board.tsx:719` already composes `gn-card gn-board-card` (`card.tsx:7`), the new rule is bare — `(0,1,0)`, the identical specificity `.gn-card` has, not higher — and it wins on SOURCE ORDER (it sits later in `ui.css` than `.gn-card`'s own rule), so every other `.gn-card` consumer in the product is untouched. **One real behaviour change, wired rather than left dead:** `.gn-board-card--pending`'s dashed in-transit outline had a rule with nothing pointing at it — `board.tsx:719` never added a pending modifier — so `BoardCardView` now reads the same `card.pending` flag the "claim in transit" chip already uses; proven both directions and mutation-checked (a never-wired class fails the positive case, an always-wired one fails the negative). **Ruling 15 (coordinator remediation, same day): the spec's `cursor: grab` is REMOVED.** It shipped in this task's first pass with no drag behaviour behind it — the same "a control that lies" shape Task 4's own brief withheld the inert Filters button for, which this task's first pass had not held itself to; it belongs in Task 14's commit, beside the behaviour it promises, not here ahead of it. **The blocked-column indicator needed no work, confirmed rather than assumed:** `board.tsx:409` already renders `<Chip tone={column.blocked ? 'blocked' : column.category}>`, and `.gn-chip--blocked .gn-chip__dot` (`ui.css:155`) already carries the tone as a coloured dot against a readable label — the prototype's tinted-ground-plus-same-hue-text version measures 3.229–4.291 against the 4.5:1 floor in all six style×theme combinations and does not ship. **A second, pre-existing finding surfaced while confirming that: `.gn-board__column--blocked`'s `border-color` had been inert since before this task** — no rule declared a `border-style`, so nothing painted, and `board.test.tsx`'s "marks a blocked state visibly" case asserts only the class string, never a computed style. **Ruling 16 (coordinator remediation, same day): the empty declaration is REMOVED**, the sixth time this session hit the same shape the dead `.gn-view-tabs` rules were (Task 4). A split into a separate `<h3>` title plus a standalone blocked chip (closer to the prototype) was considered and rejected: that chip's tone carries CATEGORY for every column, not only blocked, so separating title from chip would change what the colour means across the whole board — a semantic change outside both this geometry-only task's scope and the plan's as written. The board card now falls through to `.gn-card`'s radius and moves with the style axis like every other card; case 13.464 asserts the rule declares no `border-radius` of its own, mirroring 13.355's own source-scan shape, so the literal cannot quietly return. - ✅ **The pinned empty-board sentence is gated on zero CARDS rather than zero groups, and each empty column gets its own empty state — Ruling R6 (Task 7, 2026-09-16).** `board.tsx:70` (pre-R6; that line is unrelated comment prose today — the gate it names was superseded by this very ruling, not merely moved) — its `EMPTY_BOARD_COPY` branch used to trigger only on `board.groups.length === 0`; a project with a workflow attached and zero tickets in it (`groups.length === 1`, every column empty) took the old gate's false branch, skipped the sentence, and drew a silent rail of empty column trays — one layer under the exact "loaded, refused nothing, said nothing" failure that branch exists to prevent. R6 widens the gate to a new `totalCards` fold over every column of every group: the sentence (`emptyBanner`) renders whenever the board holds zero cards in total, and the rail keeps drawing beside it — the zero-groups case stays the ONLY one with no rail, since it alone has no columns to draw. `groups.length === 0` implies `totalCards === 0`, so this is a strict superset, not a replacement: the three pre-existing `EMPTY_BOARD_COPY` assertions (3.112, 3.113, 3.114's CONTROL) pass UNMODIFIED — run and confirmed, not assumed. **THE SENTENCE NOW FOLLOWS THE CONTROL (V1, round-2 ruling, 2026-09-21) and those three cases were updated rather than left asserting a render that no longer happens:** *"create one"* is an instruction, and the create-ticket button it names renders only when `onCreateTicket` is passed down — which **no caller in this app did** (`grep -rn 'onCreateTicket=' apps/web/app apps/web/src` → 0 across 63 files at the ruling). A mount that hands the handler down keeps the pinned sentence; a mount with nothing to hand down says *"No tickets here yet."* (`EMPTY_BOARD_UNWIRED_COPY`) instead of instructing, and the empty column's `+` glyph — the one part of that state that reads as a control — is never drawn unaccompanied. **The shell wires it: `CreateTicketFlow` gained optional `open`/`onOpenChange`, the project page lifts the dialog's open state, and the empty board's button and the header's "New ticket" now open the SAME dialog** (case 13.1162). A mutation witness (reverting the gate to `groups.length === 0`, re-running the suite, restoring with a targeted edit rather than `git checkout --`) confirms exactly two tests are R6-dependent: the new whole-board case (13.466) and one PRE-EXISTING test whose own assertion the ruling falsifies by construction — 3.114's second case (`test-cases/03-foundation-ledger.md`), which asserted `EMPTY_BOARD_COPY` absent over a single-group, all-empty-columns fixture that IS the R6 case in miniature; amended rather than left standing, its rail-survives half unchanged. **Each empty column separately renders `EMPTY_COLUMN_COPY`** ("No tickets in this column." — the "yet" was dropped later the same month, see the filter bullet below; this bullet keeps the wording as it was added, and the epic split further down is the second sentence to sit beside it, a new exported constant, deliberately not a re-spelling of `EMPTY_BOARD_COPY` since both can render on the same screen at once) plus a 34px icon circle replicating `.gn-chip`'s own three-branch chipBg/chipShadow per-style treatment on a NEW selector (`.gn-board__column-empty-icon`, never editing the shared, do-not-edit `.gn-chip`) and an optional create-ticket action. **AMENDED 2026-10-02 (prefixes/groups Task 8, BRD-19): every create-ticket control now reads "Create ticket" — the whole-board button, the header and the per-column one; the per-column button keeps its distinct accessible name (`Create ticket in <column>`) through an `aria-label`, so the two are still not identically named to assistive tech.** The action reused the SAME unscoped `onCreateTicket` handler the whole-board button already calls — `BoardProps` gained no new prop, and no per-column target existed to pass — worded differently from the whole-board button's only so two buttons rendered on one screen (a board that is both globally and per-column empty, R6) are not identically named to assistive tech. **AMENDED 2026-09-23 (starting-status design) — the "no per-column target" gap above is closed, and the button is now GATED on more than the handler existing.** `onCreateTicket` widens to `(selection?: {workflowId, stateId}) => void`; the whole-board button and the empty-board banner still call it with none, but each empty column's own "Add a ticket" now calls it WITH that column's identity, so the shell can pre-fill the New-ticket dialog's type and status. **The button (and its `+` icon) is gated on `column.creatable`, not merely on the handler being passed:** `BoardColumn` (both the wire type in `packages/domain/src/read-models.ts` and the view type in `view-types.ts`) gains a REQUIRED `creatable: boolean` — `isCreatableState(def, stateId)`, read at every site that builds a column from a workflow def (the server's `readBoard`/`appendStragglerColumns`, the online mapper's `mapBoardColumn`, and the offline replica's board query) — so a state a workflow forbids creating tickets in shows the empty-column copy with no `+` and no button, even when the shell has wired the handler. A straggler column (no published definition) is always `creatable: false`, mirroring `blocked`'s own straggler convention. - ✅ **A board's workflow group is a DISCLOSURE, and the choice is remembered (owner request, 2026-09-23).** Each group heading is a real `<button>` inside its `<h2>` — `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and a caret DRAWN through a `::after` on a separate `aria-hidden` element so the accessible name stays exactly the workflow name (the idiom `.gn-list__columns-toggle` established; case `13.1417`) — and collapsed hides the whole RAIL, columns and their per-column `Create ticket` with it, not merely the cards (`13.1409`). **⚠ THE REQUEST'S PREMISE WAS FALSE, and it is recorded because a later reader will otherwise assume this was a default change:** the request read as though the group were already collapsible; measured at `45091f08` it was neither — `board.tsx` rendered a bare `<h2 class="gn-board__workflow">` ONLY where a board had more than one workflow group, and the columns below it always rendered. So this bought a new control, a new default AND a new store. **THE DEFAULTS, which are three separate rulings:** an empty group rests COLLAPSED on a board with more than one group (`13.1407`); a group holding tickets rests expanded (`13.1408`); and a LONE group rests expanded even when empty — *"single workflow → UNCOLLAPSED, including when it is empty"* — because collapsing it would be a heading over nothing, hiding the only doors off the page (`13.1420`, with `13.1412` proving the control still exists and works and `13.1413` proving a person may still fold it by hand). The old `groups.length > 1` gate on the heading is therefore GONE: a group is collapsible even when it is the only one, so it always has a heading to click. **A GROUP THAT STOPS BEING EMPTY OPENS ITSELF, AND THAT OPENING PERSISTS:** a ticket arriving in a group that was collapsed *by the default* expands it and writes the expansion through, so a reload cannot put the new work back behind a heading (`13.1415`). **⚠ A COLLAPSE A PERSON MADE IS NEVER UNDONE BY IT (`13.1416`), and the STORED SHAPE is what guarantees that rather than a second opinion about emptiness:** the record holds ONLY choices — `{userId, projects: {"<projectId>": {"<workflowId>@<version>": boolean}}}`, `true` expanded and `false` collapsed — so a group ABSENT from it was never collapsed by anybody (the default, which the rule may reopen) while one stored as `false` was (which it must not). A shape storing resolved states would have erased that difference and silently reopened a group a person had shut. The rule is one-shot on two independent guards — what the last effect run SAW, since a stream frame re-reads this board constantly, and the `true` the write itself leaves behind — so it cannot become a write storm against a synchronous, main-thread store. **THE MEMORY IS `localStorage`, CLIENT SIDE, AND NOT THE SERVER** (owner: *"by persist i didnt mean to database/server. only on the local storage, clientside"* — an earlier reading sent this at `ProjectViewPrefs` and the server-owned preferences document and was backed out unstarted): `preferences/workflow-collapse.ts` follows `new-ticket-start.ts`'s shape — keyed by USER (a shared laptop must not inherit the previous person's collapse) and by PROJECT (two projects can hold the same workflow at the same version), `''` or an absent `currentUserId` reads and writes NOTHING, `try`/`catch` around both the accessor and the `JSON.parse`, and a corrupt or unrecognised record answers the default rather than half-honouring itself (`13.1414`, four arms, each carrying the control that the same bytes DO answer for the user or project they name). `Board` is handed `currentUserId` rather than reading `moves.currentUserId`, because the latter exists only on the movable path — the memory would otherwise work on a board with move arrows wired and silently not on the read-only one. The store is applied in a LAYOUT effect: not a `useState` initialiser, because the board is server-rendered and a render-time read would make the first client render disagree with the HTML React is hydrating against; and not a passive effect, which can paint first — drawing an empty group open and then shutting it, the flicker class case `13.1385` records on this very page. **ONE CASE ELSEWHERE WAS AMENDED, and it is a behaviour change rather than a repair:** `board-narrowing.test.tsx` `13.469` used the ABSENCE of a level-2 heading as its cross-confirmation that a fixture carries one workflow; that witness was replaced with a stronger one — exactly one group heading, naming that workflow — rather than deleted. - ⚙️ **`istToday()` — the one place this shell turns an instant into a day** — the device supplies the INSTANT, a fact it genuinely owns; `istDayOf` turns it into the IST day, and the device's own opinion about which day that is never enters. `now` is injected. Two wrong answers, two independent guards: `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (yesterday's cell for five and a half hours every night) dies on the IST-midnight pair, and `toLocaleDateString()` (a different day per collaborator) dies on the three-zone loop. Stated plainly because the branch has corrected three overclaims of this shape already: the zone loop CANNOT discriminate against the current implementation — `istDayOf` reads only `Date.parse` of an offset-bearing string and the UTC getters — so it is a regression guard whose teeth are the mutation, and the `TZ` control below it proves the knob moves, nothing more. **The shell now RE-DERIVES the day (ruling E5-43, 2026-09-21):** it was computed once per render and never on its own, so a tab left open across IST midnight kept yesterday's ring until something else re-rendered the page — the day COMPUTATION was always right, and only WHEN it was recomputed was wrong. The project page holds it as state and re-reads it on `visibilitychange` and on `focus`, which the finding allows and which needs no cadence argument a timer would: a tick must answer "how often is often enough" and every answer is wrong in one direction, while an event fires exactly when the page is about to be looked at again, which is the only moment a stale ring can be seen. Setting the same day is free — React bails out on an identical value. Cases `13.1179` (positive, both listeners, plus the control that the advanced clock alone does NOT move the ring). `apps/web/src/ist-today.ts`, `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/p/[projectId]/page.tsx`

The WebSocket is dialled DIRECTLY at `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL` because Next's dev server does not proxy protocol upgrades. A third rule for `/api/workspaces/*` was dropped when ticket reads moved to `/v1`; nothing serves that prefix, and a proxy rule for a path nothing serves fails differently through Next than direct, which is the confusing half of a 404. `test/next-config.test.ts` re-derives the served prefixes from `apps/server/src` on every run — comments stripped first, so a path merely DISCUSSED in prose cannot vouch for itself — and refuses a rule that matches none. `apps/web/next.config.ts`

An admin mints from `/w/[workspaceId]/members`; the link is `${WEB_ORIGIN}/invite/${token}` built by the SERVER, so this shell's route segment is one half of a contract already shipped. **The token is server-owned and hashed** — the raw copy leaves in the mint response and nowhere else, so the minted link renders exactly once under copy that says so, the pending list carries `expiresAt` and no token, and no "show it again" affordance exists because nothing could serve one. **RULING V2 (CRITICAL, closed):** the minted URL used to live in `MintForm`'s OWN local state, handed to `onMinted` — `loadPending`, a network re-read of the pending list the mint success also triggers. A FAILED re-read flips the page's `adminGate` away from `'admin'`, the only state that mounts `MintForm` at all, so the form unmounted and took the just-minted, un-copyable, un-re-servable URL with it — a real credential, silently gone, on a failure path that has nothing to do with whether the mint itself succeeded. `minted` is now the PAGE's own state (`MintForm` is presentational and hands the result up rather than holding it), rendered outside the `adminGate` chain so it survives whatever that gate does next. `GET /v1/invites/:token` needs no session, deliberately: the token IS the credential, so a stranger is told which workspace they are being asked to join before being made to authenticate — and the page distinguishes a session still LOADING from a signed-out one, which the plan's two-branch test does not. **Accepting is address-checked (R4, 2026-09-29 — cases 6.260–6.265, see "Invitations" in §6):** a signed-in visitor who is not the addressed account meets a 403 whose sentence (`This invitation was sent to a•••@example.com. Sign in with that account to accept it.`) the page renders verbatim under the Join button, without routing or retrying (case 6.261). A dead link says used, withdrawn **or** lapsed, all three, because the door answers one frozen 404 for all of them and a holder must learn nothing about which. Withdrawing is an ordinary `invite.revoked` through `DataSource.ingest`, gated by `ADMIN_ONLY_TYPES` at the door rather than by a second check here. **HIG surface (Task 4a, 2026-09-08):** the invite card sits on `surface-raised` with no border, and the dead-link paragraph is muted — the card's fill and the page's are what separate them, per R1(c). **Neo restyle (Task 15, 2026-09-09):** the card's literal `border-radius: 12px` — a deliberate BUMP over `.gn-card`'s then-8px base, which had inverted into an unintended SHRINK once Task 14 moved that base onto a `--gn-radius-card` token reaching 20px under neo — is removed (case 13.355); the card now simply takes `.gn-card`'s own radius at whatever style is active. No markup changed. The body sentence is UNCHANGED and pinned: the prototype's version drops the role, and a person accepting an invitation is being told what they will be able to do, so the copy rule rejects it. **Case 13.300** drives the real page in a real browser behind a stubbed summary and matches the role alternation against the shipped `InviteSummary['role']` union rather than a guessed list. What this route still LACKS is a one-way accessible-name floor — the signed-in sweep has no standing invite token, and a token-less visit would baseline the dead-link branch, so the gap is recorded in `docs/pre-launch-checklist.md` with a named owner instead of being closed wrongly. **AND THE LINK READ NOW CARRIES THE TOKEN'S EXPIRY (2026-09-19, the `isInvite` expiry ruling, case `13.988`).** `openableInvite` had read `expires_at` from the beginning — it is the whole point of its `expires_at > now()` predicate — and **threw it away**; it is now served as a fourth field on `GET /v1/invites/:token`. **An `ADDITIVE FIELD` on a read that already existed: no route, no migration.** **It is the TOKEN's window and not the invitation's, and that is the distinction the case pins:** `invite_tokens` has one row per PRESENTATION while `proj_invites` has no expiry column at all, so an invitation revoked and re-issued has one invitation row and several token rows, each with its own window — a read answering the invitation's lifetime would answer the WRONG question on a re-issued link. The value served is the row `openableInvite` matched on, so it cannot disagree with the predicate that admitted the call. **It does not erode the read's disclosure guard**, which protects the ADDRESS the invitation names — a fact belonging to somebody other than whoever holds a forwarded link — where `expiresAt` is a property of the credential the caller is already holding; that read's own docblock is corrected in the same change set (it said *"the three fields Plan 6 pinned and nothing else"*). **The invitee-facing page does not render it yet** — this row's scope is the DOOR, and the client's `expiresAt` still lives on the admin side only; owner named in the catalogue. **The mint form's Channel select offered `email`/`sms`/`whatsapp` while the door accepted only `email`/`phone` (E6-9) — two offered channels were refused 422, and the one the door accepted was never offered.** Fixed by building the select's options from `INVITE_CHANNELS` (`@gisik-nokma/domain`, exported alongside `INVITE_ROLES`) rather than a hand-written array, so the two can no longer drift; `phone` reads "Phone (SMS)" for the person filling the form, since both discontinued options reach one. Cases 3.902–3.903. **⚠ AND A LINK THAT COULD NOT BE CHECKED IS NOT A DEAD LINK (V9, 2026-09-21 — cases `17.061`/`17.062`):** `/invite/[token]`'s rejection arm set `invite = null` for ANY failure, and `null` had exactly one sentence — *"This invitation link does not open anything. It may have been used, withdrawn, or lapsed — ask whoever invited you for a new one."* So a dropped connection, a 500 or an unparseable body were all drawn as a dead link, **and that sentence retires a link that was never tried**: it tells the person to ask for a replacement for a credential that may be perfectly good. `null` is not nothing here — it is the transport's read affordance for the server's ONE frozen 404 body, which really does mean the link opens nothing. The page's state is four-valued now (`'loading' | 'unreachable' | null | InviteSummary`); the transport failure says the link could not be CHECKED, says nothing has been used up, and offers **Try again**, which re-asks and believes a second answer. **⚠ AND THE PAGE NAMES THE DEADLINE AND OFFERS A NEXT STEP (E5-18, 2026-09-21 — cases `17.066`–`17.069`):** the door has served `expiresAt` — the presented TOKEN's own window, the value `openableInvite` matched on — as a fourth field on `GET /v1/invites/:token` since 2026-09-19 (`routes/invites.ts:417`, the `isInvite` expiry ruling), and `createHttpInviteGateway` read three fields and threw it away, so a person deciding whether to act on a link NOW could not see when it stops working while `/workspaces` renders the same fact for a waiting invitation. It is carried now and rendered as *"This link lapses {day}"*, through the same `onDay` shape `/workspaces` uses rather than a second date vocabulary; a body sending none draws no line rather than an invented day. The dead-link arm, which was one `<p>` with no link at all, now links to `/workspaces` — where a person's own waiting invitations live. **⚠ DECLINE IS NOT BUILT, and the reason is recorded rather than the gap quietly closed:** the decline that exists is `MyInvitationsGateway.decline(inviteId)`, keyed by `inviteId` and matched to the SIGNED-IN person's own address — which is why `/workspaces` offers it and a token page cannot, holding a bearer token and (on a signed-out arrival) no session at all. Declining from here needs a decline-by-token door and a ruling on what a decline means for somebody who never signed in. - ✅ **The invitations addressed to YOU — and the ability to say no** (Task 17) — `GET /v1/me/invitations` answers the pending invitations for the signed-in person's **verified** email, scoped from their own `"user"` row and never from a parameter, and `/workspaces` renders them as the *"One invitation is waiting"* banner: who invited you, to what workspace, on what terms (the role as a sentence, never the raw enum), when it was sent and when it lapses, with **Accept** and **Decline**. Before this the invite surface was admin-and-token shaped — a person who lost the email had no way to discover they had been invited, and **Decline existed nowhere in the product**: the only exits from `pending` were an acceptance or an admin's revocation. `invite.declined` is the new terminal claim, attributed to the person who made it, refused from every client door for the reason `invite.accepted` is (an inviteId is readable by every member, so a client-submitted decline would let any admin destroy a pending invitation *under the invited person's name*). **Accept from the banner is a second door, not a second implementation**: the raw token is unrecoverable (sha256 at rest, one copy, handed out at mint), so a caller-scoped list has none to serve — `apps/server/src/invites/acceptance.ts` holds the acceptance sequence once and the two doors differ only in the proof they demand, link possession or a verified address, the second being strictly the narrower. All three actions spend the SAME credential row through the same conditional DELETE, so accept-by-link, accept-from-the-banner and decline are mutually exclusive by construction. An empty answer renders NOTHING — no heading, no empty state — because a person with no invitation must not be told about invitations, and a failed read is one muted line rather than the page's refusal. A name the server cannot supply becomes words rather than a hole in the sentence, blank as well as null: better-auth's `"user"."name"` is `NOT NULL` with no non-blank constraint and the dev workspace's own owner carries `''`. Named absences: phone-channel invitations do not surface here (this read is email-scoped), and a phone-only account has no verified address and is answered an empty list. **Restyled, 2026-09-15 (the workspaces-prototype-port plan's Task 8): the banner becomes a FLAT warning wash, not a card you could open.** The prior treatment (Task 17) borrowed `.gn-card`'s own raised surface (`--gn-surface-raised`/`--gn-shadow-raised`) plus an accent inline-start edge; both are gone. The fill is now `--gn-tint-warning` (the design-tokens bullet above), which holds its 4.5:1 legibility only because this banner sits at PAGE level, never inside a card — the same measurement's own precondition. A decorative, `aria-hidden` warning-circle icon sits beside the heading/list/actions, now grouped under `.gn-invitations__body` so the icon can sit as a flex sibling; no behavioural assertion changed, since the restyle is CSS and one added `<svg>` only. **The date line (`.gn-invitations__when`, "Invited … · lapses …") briefly lost its subordinate rank in this restyle** — it was merged into `.gn-invitations__offer`'s own rule and the two became typographically identical (whole-branch review, Minor 5; the prototype has only one body line, so there was nothing there to port for a second). Fixed in the same fix wave: `.gn-invitations__when` is its own rule again, smaller than `__offer`, at this branch's own established secondary-meta size (13px/18px).
