It now reads the route's project id (`useParams`), so the answer no longer depends on who wrote storage first (case 13.879). The third: the tab seed re-ran when the session landed, over a tab the person had clicked during the session read, because `tabUserId` is that effect's dependency and is `null` while loading; a chosen-here ref now outranks the memory (case 13.880) — with the residual limitation recorded rather than hidden: a tab clicked in that window is still not REMEMBERED, because there is no user id to key the write by. Two more were prose and an assertion: a docblock justifying the user+workspace key by a cross-workspace id COLLISION (impossible — `proj_projects.project_id` is the PRIMARY KEY and an entity id is a ULID belonging to exactly one workspace), corrected in the file; and 13.872's first assertion, which its own fixture satisfied — the record is now removed before the click, so only the click can produce it. **The fix round also broke fourteen cases in `test/settings-page.test.tsx` and that is worth recording as a class:** adding `useParams` to the nav made four test files' partial `next/navigation` mocks throw at import — only one rendered the nav, so three were latent — and `cacheKey`'s first spelling joined the two ids with a NUL byte, which made `grep` report its own file as BINARY and refuse to search it; it is `JSON.stringify([userId, workspaceId])` now. **Sign out keeps the exact `Sign out {name}` accessible name it always had** — and, since E2-45 (2026-09-21), **the menu closes only when the server said the session ended**: a refused sign-out (a non-2xx ANSWER, which the transport RESOLVES rather than rejects) and one that never reached a server (the promise rejects) each leave the menu open with the control's own refusal sentence beside it — *"The server refused the sign-out — you are still signed in on this device. Try again."* / *"We could not reach the server — you are still signed in on this device. Try again."* — because the menu closing IS the confirmation, and a person who walks away from a shared machine on that confirmation while the session is still live is the one outcome the manual's own sentence about somebody else's laptop promises cannot happen (cases 17.141–17.143). Before the fix `close(false)` ran before the request was even sent and a single `.then` carried no rejection arm, so a dropped connection closed the menu, pushed nothing and said nothing. — the shell's accessible-name floor is ratcheted on that string and `e2e-stack/passkey-registration.spec.ts` addresses the control by it, so the control moved and the name did not (13.418; the e2e gained a menu-opening step and its selector is otherwise unchanged). **Help stays a bar link when SIGNED OUT** — and `Account` did too until 2026-09-21 (E5-31), because `AccountMenu` needs a name, an email and a sign-out target and has none of the three, so folding them in unconditionally would have deleted the only route to `/help` from the signed-out shell, on a page explicitly reachable signed out. **E5-31 then measured what else that arm offered a visitor who could use none of it** — `Workspaces`, `Account`, the inbox icon and the scope note *"No workspace selected — pick one to reach its board, members and settings."*, and **no Sign in**: pressing Workspaces landed on `/sign-in` by a 401 bounce with no `next=`, Account repainted the page E5-13 describes, and the note told the person to pick something the bar was not offering. The signed-out bar is now **Help + Sign in** (the arm `legal-nav.tsx` already had), with `next=` carrying where they were headed, and the scope note and the whole corner are withheld until there is a session to scope (case 13.1159). **The inbox became an icon** with a `--gn-success` dot when unread, and — owner's ruling — **the count moved into the link's accessible name** (`"Inbox, 3 unread notifications"`, bare `"Inbox"` at zero) rather than being dropped: a bare dot would have deleted the number for exactly the readers least able to go looking for it, and would leave unread state signalled by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). `UnreadBadge` is untouched and still renders the number on `/inbox` itself. **Case 13.414 is SUPERSEDED — its subject is gone**, since Help is no longer a link in this bar for "Inbox immediately before Help" to be true or false about; it is replaced by 13.416, which pins the same KIND of claim at the arrangement that now exists (the inbox immediately left of the avatar). 11.185's three arms shrank by two entries each, and 13.417 is what makes that safe to assert — a shorter expected list is also what deleting the links would produce, so the reachability of Help and Account through the menu is pinned separately. Both new controls inherit the 2.75rem tap floor from `.gn-nav a, .gn-nav button`. Opening the menu focuses its first item and the arrows walk it, wrapping at both ends — **which is also what makes the Escape-returns-focus assertion measurable**: before focus moved into the menu it had never left the trigger, and that case passed with the focus-return line deleted. Cases 13.416–13.423. **Round 25 (2026-09-16), owner: "keep the last opened workspace in local storage, and based on that, the workspace scoped navbar items should be made visible. so that just moving to a separate page (inbox, help, account, etc) does not automatically hide them." `apps/web/src/use-last-workspace.ts` (NEW) remembers it under `gn-last-workspace`**, following the `gn-style`/`gn-theme` convention; `AppNav` takes the route's workspace when there is one and the remembered one otherwise, so leaving a workspace for `/inbox`, `/help` or `/account` no longer strips the workspace-scoped links. **The bar's founding rule is unchanged — a link renders only when its target exists — and the two sources are deliberately NOT treated alike.** A ROUTED workspace renders its links immediately, because standing on `/w/<id>/members` is proof it is there; a REMEMBERED one renders them only once `useWorkspaceName` resolves a name from `getMyWorkspaces()`, because a remembered id is a guess about the past and may name a workspace you have since been removed from or that was deleted — the same hazard that got the Board item removed in Round 23, arriving from storage rather than from a route. It reuses the read the bar already makes: no second request, and no second notion of "reachable" to drift from the first. **The record is KEYED BY USER (`{userId, workspaceId}`) and a record belonging to anyone else is ignored**, because `localStorage` outlives a session: sign out, hand the laptop over, and an unkeyed memory renders the previous person's workspace NAME in the next person's chrome — the defect case 11.169 exists for, one surface over. It is not cleared on sign-out but simply not honoured, which also covers the case sign-out never runs at all (a cookie expiring in place). **Two assertions in case 13.391 changed and neither was relaxed to fit the code:** the scope note is now gated on a positive "storage read, nothing remembered" rather than on the synchronous "no workspace", since the synchronous form would flash *"No workspace selected"* at every viewer who has one on every global page; and "no workspace in the ROUTE, no Settings link" became "no workspace REACHABLE, no Settings link", the old wording being exactly what this instruction revokes. 13.424 is the counterpart that keeps that honest — without it the "no Settings" assertion would also be satisfied by a nav that had stopped remembering anything. **A cost stated rather than hidden:** when a workspace is remembered but its name never resolves, neither the scoped links nor the scope note render, because the alternative — clearing the memory on a failed name — would destroy valid state on a transient read failure to recover a hint. Cases 13.424–13.427. **Round 26 (2026-09-16), owner: "the nav bar item jitters on changing pages. the workspace scoped items briefly disappears and reappears." THE MOUNT WAS THE BUG.** `Providers` lives in the root layout and survives client-side navigation, but `AppNav` is rendered by each PAGE (`app/inbox/page.tsx:210` and fourteen siblings), so every navigation unmounts and remounts it — resetting `useLastWorkspace` to `unknown` and `useWorkspaceName` to `null`, so the workspace-scoped links vanished for the tick it took to re-read storage and re-fetch the name, then returned. Round 25 made this loud by putting four links behind that state; **the workspace-NAME half predates Round 25 entirely** and flickered even when navigating between two pages of the same workspace, where it was a single item and easier to miss. Both hooks now hold their last answer in MODULE scope — which survives the remount — and initialise `useState` from it, so the second and every later navigation paints on the first frame; the first load of a session still resolves asynchronously, because nothing is known yet and painting links from no information would be inventing state. **Two hazards the fix creates and closes:** a cache read on every remount would RESURRECT a workspace you have lost (13.426's defect displaced in time), so a successful read that does not contain the workspace EVICTS while a rejected read — transient — leaves the entry alone; and neither cache passes through the stored record's user guard (the remembered-workspace cache is checked before it, the name cache is keyed by workspace id alone), so both are dropped when the observed user id changes, since signing out and back in as someone else is a client-side navigation that does not reset module state. Cases 13.428–13.429, both mutation-witnessed. **Round 27 (2026-09-18), owner: "new nav item :right to the workspace name -> last open project name. on click, open the project page (save the last open tab as well). on hover, show the non archived projects as a dropdown, and clicking them opens those projects. if there is no last opened project, then this defaults to the first in the order that we display in the workspace page." THE ITEM IS `LastProjectNav` (`apps/web/src/last-project-nav.tsx`, NEW), mounted immediately right of the workspace name and gated on the same `!noWorkspace`/`effectiveWorkspaceId` the My Work, Members and Settings links read** — one answer to "which workspace is this bar about", not a second one. It names the project you were last in, resolved through the SAME `getMyWorkspaces` read `/workspaces` renders (`apps/web/src/use-workspace-projects.ts`, NEW: the project LIST, `null` for pending/refused and never `[]`, module-cached and evicted on a successful read that lacks the workspace, exactly `use-workspace-name.ts`'s contract one level down), so it can never name something unreachable. **With nothing remembered it falls back to the first NON-ARCHIVED project in served order** — `workspace.projects` with `archived` filtered and NO client-side sort, which is precisely what `apps/web/app/workspaces/page.tsx` renders; deriving a second order was the thing to avoid. **With no reachable project it renders NOTHING**, the rule Rounds 22–23 established when the Board item was removed for offering a link that could not resolve: the workspace's `projects` list is empty, or every row in it is archived. **It is NOT the Board item returning, and the difference is the whole reason it can exist:** Board's only possible target was the route you were already standing on, so it was a link to the current page in every state it could reach; a project id is now something the bar actually has, so this is the first project-scoped destination that points somewhere else. **Archiving the project you were last in FALLS BACK rather than disappearing** (case 13.868) — the remembered id is matched against the NON-ARCHIVED rows only, because `archived` is served precisely so a client can tell and a match against all served projects would name a project the workspaces page no longer lists. **⚠ AND THAT RULE WAS APPLIED TO A QUESTION IT DOES NOT ANSWER (E5-34, round-2 ruling, 2026-09-21):** on an ARCHIVED project's own page the route's id was matched against the live rows too, so the match missed and the fallback named the FIRST LIVE project — the item showed another project's name and href and carried no `aria-current`, on the one surface the docblock calls "a function of the ROUTE". The route's own project is resolved first now, archived or not, and is badged with the same chip and the same `", archived"` name the workspace home's card uses; the DROPDOWN stays live-only, because it offers somewhere to go and an archived project is not somewhere the workspaces page will show you (case 13.1166). **The dropdown opens on HOVER and on FOCUS/click** (the owner answered both directly) and is the `account-menu.tsx` menu pattern reused rather than reinvested: `role="menu"` with the accessible name `"Projects"`, `role="menuitem"` anchors that keep their `href`, Escape closing, arrow keys walking the items and wrapping at both ends, and a pointer-down outside closing. **One deliberate divergence from that pattern, and it is load-bearing:** focus is NOT pulled into the menu on open, because this item opens on FOCUS and moving focus would make tabbing through the nav swallow the reader into the menu every time they passed it — so Escape returns focus to the trigger and a `suppressNextFocusOpen` ref breaks the loop that would otherwise reopen the menu immediately (case 13.871 measures it). **The item's ACCESSIBLE NAME is `<name>, projects menu` (and `<name>, archived, projects menu` for an archived one), and the trailing qualifier is what keeps the bar's door distinguishable from the project's own card door** (`rel/browser-findings`, 2026-09-22): on a workspace home BOTH doors point at the same project, and until this lane both carried the same name — `Shop operations` — which made the stack suite's exact-name lookup find **two** links at desktop (`a.gn-nav__project`, 148x44, and `a.gn-project-card__door`, 363x63, both to the same `/w/.../p/...`; count 2 at 1280x720 and 1 at 390, where this item is behind the phone nav). The qualifier is on THIS side because the card door's name is the project's identity — what every `within(card)` query and the suite's own lookup address — while renaming the card would have left that lookup matching this item, whose project is `routeProject ?? rememberedLive ?? live[0]`, a POSITION. The visible text is unchanged and the name still contains it (WCAG 2.5.3). Case 13.1217. **TAB MEMORY IS GLOBAL, which the owner also answered directly:** `apps/web/src/use-last-project.ts` (NEW) keeps `gn-last-project` keyed by user AND WORKSPACE — a project id is unique inside its workspace and meaningless outside it, so a record keyed by user alone would resolve `p_1` inside whichever workspace the viewer happened to be standing in (case 13.853) — and `gn-project-tabs`, a `projectId → tab` map keyed by USER, separately, because which tab you left each project on must outlive any single one of them. Both follow `use-last-workspace.ts`'s paid-for conventions rather than inventing a second set: three states (`unknown`/`none`/`remembered`, so no false sentence flashes before storage is read), every access wrapped because a blocked browser throws on the ACCESSOR, records belonging to another user answered `none` rather than cleared, and a module-scoped cache keyed by user+workspace so the remount on every client-side navigation paints on the first frame. The project PAGE consumes the tab half — `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/p/[projectId]/page.tsx` seeds `view` from the map in an EFFECT (a `useState` initialiser would read storage on the server as `null` and disagree with the client at hydration, the same reason `theme-toggle.tsx` reads `gn-theme` in one) and writes on every `setView`, so a project reached from a card, bookmark or pasted link lands you where you left off, not only one reached through this item. `view`'s union moved out of the page into `use-last-project.ts` as `ProjectTab` so the page and the hook cannot drift about which tabs exist; `Record<typeof view, string>` on the page's `TAB_NOUN` still fails `typecheck` for a member added in one place and not the other. **Clicking either the item or a dropdown row writes the project record BEFORE the navigation lands** (one exported writer, shared with the page's route-authority path), so a destination that fails to render cannot leave the memory pointing at the project you were on before, and seeds the destination's tab to its remembered value or `board`. Cases 13.850–13.877. **Also in this round, and not about the nav:** `apps/web/test/setup.ts` now clears `localStorage` before every case, because nine test files mount this page and it now writes on every tab click — and its docblock records why NOTHING in that file may import from `src/`: the first version did, which pulled `providers.tsx` and `auth-client.ts` into the module graph before any test file's hoisted `vi.mock` could register, silently answering `{ kind: 'loading' }` to every session read in the suite. **A REVIEW ROUND THEN FOUND FIVE THINGS, ALL CLOSED, AND THREE WERE REAL DEFECTS THIS PARAGRAPH WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE DESCRIBED AS WORKING.** The Critical: `useWorkspaceProjects`' cache was keyed by workspace id alone — copying `useWorkspaceName`'s key onto a list that is NOT the same for everyone, since the server serves a non-owner only the projects they hold a membership in (`apps/server/src/read/visible-projects.ts`); sign-out is a client-side navigation, so sign in as someone with narrower access and the nav's first paint names projects they cannot open. It is keyed by user AND workspace now (case 13.878). The Important: the nav took its project from memory alone, and because `AppNav` renders INSIDE the project page, its effect is a descendant of the page's writer effect — **React commits passive effects child-first, measured rather than read out of the docs** — so on every arrival that is not through the item itself the nav named the project you had just left, and self-healed one navigation later. It now reads the route's project id (`useParams`), so the answer no longer depends on who wrote storage first (case 13.879). The third: the tab seed re-ran when the session landed, over a tab the person had clicked during the session read, because `tabUserId` is that effect's dependency and is `null` while loading; a chosen-here ref now outranks the memory (case 13.880) — with the residual limitation recorded rather than hidden: a tab clicked in that window is still not REMEMBERED, because there is no user id to key the write by. Two more were prose and an assertion: a docblock justifying the user+workspace key by a cross-workspace id COLLISION (impossible — `proj_projects.project_id` is the PRIMARY KEY and an entity id is a ULID belonging to exactly one workspace), corrected in the file; and 13.872's first assertion, which its own fixture satisfied — the record is now removed before the click, so only the click can produce it. **The fix round also broke fourteen cases in `test/settings-page.test.tsx` and that is worth recording as a class:** adding `useParams` to the nav made four test files' partial `next/navigation` mocks throw at import — only one rendered the nav, so three were latent — and `cacheKey`'s first spelling joined the two ids with a NUL byte, which made `grep` report its own file as BINARY and refuse to search it; it is `JSON.stringify([userId, workspaceId])` now.

**The workspaces-prototype-port plan (2026-09-15, Tasks 1–9) restyles the `/workspaces` card and page shell against the owner's `desktop.dc.html` export, and changes the card's CONTENT CONTRACT, not only its geometry.** Three things this round changes about what the card SAYS, stated plainly because a reader of the Round 19b/19c prose above would not otherwise learn any of them happened: **(1)** the card head gains a new meta line, `"{n} projects"` (`projectCountLine`, `apps/web/src/workspace-viewer.ts`) — `live.length` alone, deliberately never summed with `nameRestrictedProjectCount`, and gated on `!viewer.countsWithheld`, so 13.380's own guest-card property ("no number anywhere") still holds; the members chip already states the member count, so the prototype's own `"5 members · 2 projects"` phrasing would say the member count twice on one card and is not reproduced. **(2)** the per-viewer role sentence (13.357) MOVES — from under the workspace name to its own line BELOW the chip row, matching the prototype's own layout. **(3)** the per-project `<ul>` Round 19c left as plain project names is GONE, replaced by one truncated project line (`projectLine`, same file) plus a decorative chevron: up to `PROJECT_LINE_CAP` (3) names joined by `·`, and past the cap a counted suffix (`· +N more`) that drops its number to `· and more` under `countsWithheld` — the same withholding rule the meta line keeps, applied to a second surface. **The `project-card-${projectId}` entity-keyed testid this page used to carry is GONE with the `<ul>` it keyed** — case 3.154, previously ✅, is now 🚫 (`test-cases/03-foundation-ledger.md`); its sibling `workspace-card-${workspaceId}` (3.153) is untouched. Cases 13.405–13.407.

**Geometry, over the same shared `ui.css`/`globals.css` this style axis already drives:** the workspace monogram grows to a 44px ROUNDED SQUARE (`size="workspace"` on `Avatar`, a new `.gn-avatar--workspace` rule — `border-radius: 0.6875rem`, not a circle — plus `flex: none`, added in the whole-branch-review fix wave, Important 3: without it a long unbroken workspace name pulls width from every flex sibling including this one, and a rendered proof against the real stylesheets measured the square compressing to 23.62px wide while staying 44px tall; with `flex: none` it holds 44×44 regardless of name length); the chip's fill moves off `surface-raised` (which made every chip invisible against the card it sits on under `hig`/`minimal`) onto `fillTertiary`, with `minimal` going fully transparent (`background: transparent`, zero horizontal padding, the prototype's own treatment) and `neo` instead carrying the CARD's own colour plus an inset `shadow-sunken` — a well carved into the card rather than a tinted pill, the same neumorphic idiom `.ticket-type-list__row` already uses; the grid swaps `auto-fill` for `auto-fit` so three workspaces no longer sit at their minimum width with dead space beside them; and the card's own "door" (the clickable wrapper Round 19b built) becomes one flex column at the prototype's 20px padding, replacing three ad-hoc top-margins with one `gap`. The page gained its own `.gn-workspaces` shell, a page title, and a one-line summary (`"N workspaces you belong to"`, gated on a SUCCESSFUL non-empty read — `workspaces !== null && workspaces.length > 0`, both terms independently mutation-proven, case 13.406).

**The changes below rode along on this page's work and reach OTHER pages, recorded here so a reader of this file is not the last to find out.** `.gn-page-title`'s `font-size`/`line-height`/`font-weight`/`letter-spacing` addition is GLOBAL — it is the base rule, not a `/workspaces`-scoped override, and reaches every page that carries the class: `/account`, `/inbox`, `/invite/[token]`, `/mcp/authorize`, `/mcp/tokens`, `/settings`, `/workspaces`, every `/w/*` screen that owns one (workspace home, members, my-work, ticket types, the ticket-type editor — standalone route and inlined — and workflows), all of which previously fell through to the browser's own `2em` default with no tracking at all. (The rule's `letter-spacing` was first shipped at `-0.025em`, dividing the prototype's `-0.4px` tracking by the ROOT font size instead of the element's own 34px — corrected same-day to `-0.0118em`, matching the two sibling `.gn-account .gn-page-title`/`.gn-help__title` rules independently corrected the same way the same day.) Separately, `.gn-workspace-list__role`'s resize (`0.8rem` → `0.9375rem`, for the card head's own sake) silently reached its two OTHER borrowers — `/settings`'s workspace-name subtitle and the workspace-home header's meta line — since all three call sites shared one rule; both are now pinned back to `0.8rem` via a dedicated `.gn-workspace-list__role--pinned` modifier class added at those two call sites only, leaving the card's own (namesake) rule at the new size. **The pin was incomplete until this fix wave: the shared rule's `margin` also changed, `0.15rem 0 0` → `0`, and only the modifier's `font-size`/`line-height` were pinned back — not the margin (whole-branch review, Minor 6).** Restored on the modifier for byte-parity with the pre-Task-6 rule, but MEASURED rather than assumed to matter, because the review's own "2.4px, under-recorded" figure was reasoned, not rendered: at `/settings`, the `<h1 className="gn-page-title">` and this subtitle `<p>` are adjacent block siblings inside `.gn-shell` (a plain block container, not flex), so their margins COLLAPSE to the larger of the two — `.gn-page-title`'s own `0.4rem` bottom margin, which already exceeds the subtitle's `0.15rem` top margin on either side of this fix. Rendered both ways (a static fixture against the real stylesheets): the gap measures 6.4px identically with the modifier's `margin-top` at `0` or `0.15rem`. The pre-existing Task 6/7 comment on this rule already said as much ("its 0.15rem top offset is gone, so the gap above it is now `.gn-page-title`'s own 0.4rem bottom margin alone") — the restoration is real and matches the pre-Task-6 rule, but it is NOT a visible change at `/settings` today. The workspace-home header's meta line is the opposite case, and here the restoration IS load-bearing: its parent, `.gn-workspace-home__header-titles`, is a FLEX column with its own `0.15rem` `gap`, and flex layout does not collapse a child's own margin into that gap — rendered proof: the modifier's bare `0.15rem 0 0` there would ADD to the gap (measured 4.8px) rather than restore anything, doubling the pre-Task-6 spacing instead of matching it. The modifier's margin is therefore zeroed specifically at that call site (`.gn-workspace-home__header-titles .gn-workspace-list__role--pinned`, measured 2.4px — the correct, pre-Task-6-equivalent gap once the parent's own `gap` is counted once). Case 13.409.

**`.gn-page-title` is not the largest-blast-radius change on this branch — four rules in the SHARED `packages/ui/src/ui.css` are, and this is their first record.** That file is imported by every web route AND by `apps/desktop/src/main.tsx`, so all four reach the desktop client too, with no style-axis or page scoping. `.gn-button`'s padding went `0.4rem 0.85rem` → `0 1.125rem` (vertical padding now supplied entirely by the pre-existing `min-height: 2.75rem` floor, so every button in the product is ~9px wider); `.gn-field`'s gap went `0.45rem` → `0.4375rem`; `.gn-field__label` went `font-size: 0.8rem` with no declared `line-height` to `0.8125rem`/`1.125rem`; `.gn-field__input`'s padding went `0 0.85rem` → `0 0.875rem` and its `font-size` went `1rem` → `1.0625rem` — every input in the product is now 17px instead of 16px. All four are Task 3's deliberate port of the prototype's control metrics (see the spec's *Blast radius* section for the reasoning); what was missing until now was this record. `.gn-chip`'s fill/metrics change is the same shared-file shape and IS already recorded, two paragraphs below (the `fillTertiary` move, minimal's transparency, neo's carved-in treatment).

The invitation banner's restyle (flat `--gn-tint-warning` wash, no shadow, no accent edge) is recorded on its own bullet above. The founding form's spacing and heading matched the prototype once (`margin-top` 1.1rem → 2.125rem, heading 1.05rem/no-line-height → 1.25rem/1.5625rem); **2026-10-02 (Task 8) the form is a dialog behind the header's Create workspace button and those rules are deleted** — see §19. `apps/web/app/workspaces/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/globals.css`, `apps/web/src/workspace-viewer.ts`, `packages/ui/src/ui.css`, `packages/ui/src/components/avatar.tsx`, `apps/web/app/settings/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app-nav.tsx`, `apps/web/src/use-workspace-name.ts`, `apps/web/src/mcp-tokens-screen.tsx`, `apps/web/app/mcp/tokens/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/inbox-nav-link.tsx`

Every device but the current one has a quiet "Sign out this device" (`POST /v1/me/devices/:key/sign-out`; accessible name carries the row title, and two rows with the SAME title are told apart by "last active …" / "never active", then "first signed in <date>", then an ordinal — case 6.348), and "Sign out all other devices" (better-auth `revokeOtherSessions`) shows once when there is more than one device. A refused sign-out renders verbatim in a `role="alert"` and the list is re-read only after a success (ruling E2-24(b), closed); no optimistic removal. **Named absence, on the same silent-omission footing as Your workspaces and Notifications above:** a failed list read collapses to the same hedged empty note an honestly-empty answer produces ("No signed-in devices to show."). Files: `packages/app-core/src/account/sessions-section.tsx`, `sessions-client.ts`, `relative-time.ts`. **Sign-in and devices, Passkeys half (Task 8):** the credentials
  `GET /v1/me/passkeys` answers (devices plan Tasks 5 and 7, 2026-10-01 — not the plugin's `listUserPasskeys`, whose schema does not know `lastUsedAt`): **grouped under a heading per authenticator** ("iCloud Keychain · 2", providers alphabetical, "Security key or other" always last), each row reading its name ("Unnamed passkey" when it has none), "Added <date>", and "Last used <relative>" or "Never used", with a quiet **Not used recently** flag when the server says it has been unused for 90 days (or never) — and each row carrying a delete control whose ACCESSIBLE
  name is its own passkey's (`Delete passkey {name}`, so three credentials are three distinguishable
  controls rather than three announcements of "Delete"), a named empty state ("You have no passkeys
  yet."), and a name field plus "Add a passkey" that runs the real WebAuthn registration ceremony
  through `authClient.passkey.addPasskey({ name })`. An empty name is allowed through deliberately —
  the plugin then labels the credential from its AAGUID, which is a better answer than a disabled
  button with no reason. Add and remove both RE-READ the server rather than editing the list locally:
  the stored label is the server's answer, so a locally-invented row could show a name the account
  does not carry. **The three client member names were settled by the COMPILER, not by documentation
  or by a grep:** only `signIn.passkey` and `passkey.addPasskey` are hand-declared by
  `@better-auth/passkey@1.7.2`'s client plugin; `deletePasskey` (and, no longer used for the list, `listUserPasskeys`) are generated
  from the server endpoint paths (`/passkey/list-user-passkeys`, `/passkey/delete-passkey`) by the
  same `PathToObject`/`CamelCase` machinery the Sessions half documents, and a typecheck probe WITH a
  negative control (an invented member, which failed `TS2339`) is what rules out the vacuous reading
  that the surface is `any`. **Unlike every other section on this page, a refusal here is NOT silent
  and NOT collapsed:** a refused add or remove renders better-auth's own message verbatim in a
  `role="alert"` (`gn-refusal gn-refusal--server` — **corrected by the final whole-branch review**:
  this used to be the same `.gn-shell__refusal` class Profile's save refusal uses, copied forward from
  Task 3's ruling without noticing `PasskeysSection` lives in `@gisik-nokma/app-core`, not `apps/web`,
  and `.gn-shell__refusal` is defined only in `apps/web/app/globals.css` — invisible on `apps/desktop`,
  which never loads that stylesheet. `gn-refusal`/`gn-refusal--server` is the real, visually identical
  app-core-level equivalent, already used the same way by three other app-core views), and a refusal
  that carries NO message still surfaces, because `error?.message ?? null` would read a message-less
  refusal as success and a silent no-op after somebody touched a fingerprint sensor is
  indistinguishable from the passkey having been saved. **RULING E2-23 (closed):** the passive list read no longer keeps the silent-omission treatment its three siblings have, either. A failed list read used to collapse to `[]`, and the named empty state above ("You have no passkeys yet.") then asserted a fact about the account nobody had confirmed — the same shape `sessions-section.tsx`'s sibling read still carries, hedged only by wording ("…to show"), never by a distinct state. `PasskeysSection` now takes a `listFailed` flag, independent of the add/remove `error` above: it states "Your passkeys could not be loaded." instead of the empty claim, but ONLY when there is nothing else to show — a caller still holding a real, previously-read list keeps rendering it even if a later poll fails. **The passkey list is also the one mount-time
  read on this page that is GATED** (on `user !== null`): `GET /v1/me/passkeys` answers 401 to an anonymous visitor, so an
  anonymous `/account` load would make a request that cannot succeed (until 2026-10-01 it was the plugin's
  `/passkey/list-user-passkeys` under `/api/auth/*`, where that request also spent a unit of everyone's sign-in budget — measured as a real 401 in
  `apps/server/test/auth/sign-in-flows.test.ts`). **Named cost,
  disclosed rather than slipped in:** for a SIGNED-IN visitor this adds `auth:` charges per
  `/account` load (`/get-session` only — the device list moved to `/v1/me/devices` and the passkey list to `/v1/me/passkeys` on 2026-10-01, `/v1/*` routes the limiter never charges) against a
  `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX` of 10; `/passkey/*` is absent from `SIGN_IN_PREFIXES`, so none of it touches
  the tighter `signin:` bucket. **And the CEREMONIES cost more than the page load, which is the half of
  this disclosure an operator actually has to act on:** counted from `@better-auth/passkey`'s own
  `dist/client.mjs`, a successful Add is **2** units (`generate-register-options`,
  `verify-registration`; the re-list is a `/v1/*` read and is not charged), an Add aborted at the prompt is **1**, a Delete is **1**,
  and a passkey sign-in click on `/sign-in` is **2** (`generate-authenticate-options`,
  `verify-authentication` — so a completed click costs two, not one). Arriving on `/account` and
  registering once is three units of ten, and a person who fumbles the prompt a few times and retries can
  exhaust the window on a key shared across every browser behind the web container. **This does NOT
  weaken the rate-limit-neutral constraint and the two must not be run together:** that constraint is
  specifically about an ANONYMOUS `/sign-in` PAGE LOAD, which still charges ZERO — measured in a real
  browser as one `GET /v1/auth/methods`, a `/v1/*` route the limiter never charges, and nothing under
  `/api/auth/*`. Every figure above is a deliberate action by a signed-in person; the remedy if it ever

  which is the phone's More TAB (an identity header over three groups of navigation links) and not
  this page at all; the owner's "it still doesn't match the Style" is what caught it, and every value
  below was then measured against the real reference in a rendered browser rather than eyeballed.

  colour field to match the prototype's seed `w.bg`) and an accent "Open" at the trailing edge, the
  same `.gn-workspace-card__door` shape, with `aria-label="Open <name>"` so the link is named once
  rather than repeating the name `Avatar` gives itself. **This row navigation is the one piece of new

  nothing under it, measured live — worded that way because the page collapses a FAILED read to `[]`

  digest row: no email delivery exists for notifications, so those are the invented-data trap the

  one prototype detail this port refuses, on a measurement rather than a preference.** A tinted
  version was built and then removed: measured in a real browser across all six theme x style

  named rather than rediscovered and NOT fixed here** (both are product-wide palette decisions, not

  light/`neo` — `neo` being the aggravating factor, since it collapses `surfaceRaised` onto the same
  near-white paper as `surfaceSunken`, dropping a pairing that clears 5.05 in `hig`. Zero colour
  literals (gated) and zero new `CONTRAST_PAIRS` rows — not because a row was considered and
  declined, but because the tint could not have been DECLARED at 4.5 in the first place: at 3.84 it
  would have failed the moment it was added to that array, which is exactly what the array is for. The three docblocks

  `passkeys-section.tsx`) are retracted in the same change set. **Card ORDER is now the spec's, which is the

- ✅ **The people page, gated by the server's own 403** — the roster from `GET /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/members`, and for owners and admins the mint form, the pending list and per-invite withdraw. **The role gate is the pending read's 403 (`INVITE_ADMIN_ONLY_BODY`), not a client-side role check** — an adaptation, because Task 15b gates on the caller's role from `/v1/me/workspaces` and `getMyWorkspaces` refuses whole, so no client on this branch can read it and a role-only mapper would be routing around a refusal. The door already answers 403 to a non-admin because an invitation's address is PII, so the read IS the question, asked of the thing that knows; the cost is one round trip a member makes and a 403 in the server's log. A member sees the roster, no invite machinery, and the door's own sentence rather than a silence they must interpret. The role picker offers no `owner` and the projects field is hidden on `guest` with the KEY omitted from the body, both matching refusals `inviteSentPayload` would otherwise make. **The roster itself is now the prototype's members screen (2026-09-18, cases 13.760–13.766):** `desktop.dc.html@6d7b67c0a52c:651-798` draws a five-column table and two side panels, and the port is partial BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by omission — `readMembers` selects `user_id`, `u."name"` and `role` (`apps/server/src/routes/builder-reads.ts:254`) — plus `u."email"` since 2026-09-19, and NOTHING ELSE, so the Person and Role columns are what the wire can fill and **Project access, Assigned, Last seen and the "Ticket-only access" panel with its "Add to workspace" button (`:700-718`) are all deliberately ABSENT** — named as such in the page's own file docblock and in the commit message, not left to be inferred from an empty column, and not minted as catalogue cases because they are scope decisions about surface nobody wrote rather than scenarios with an assertion. **(The `Email` line inside the Person cell, `:675`, was in that list and has LEFT it — see the fallback paragraph below. The copy says "no tickets" and not "no columns": the server will not invent default columns for a project whose workflows the viewer may not read, so the client cannot tell "no work" from "none visible", and the sentence is true of both. **AMENDED 2026-09-20 (owner ruling): THE BOARD NOW SPLITS ONE CASE OFF, BECAUSE IT CAN.** An all-epic board reads *"No tickets in this view — epics appear in the List."* (`EMPTY_BOARD_EPICS_COPY`) — the epic is real work this view refuses to draw, and *"create one"* named the one action that could not help. **A genuinely empty project keeps the sentence above, unchanged**: it was true before the ruling and is true after it, and the two cases must not read the same words (they are the SAME state at this component — the epic is dropped before `total` increments and `isNarrowed` is deliberately false here — so the distinction arrives as the optional `epicsHidden` prop, computed in `boardNarrowing` where both sets exist). ⚠ The "none visible" half of this bullet still stands and is NOT the same question: the board still cannot tell a viewer *why else* it might be seeing nothing. `packages/app-core/src/views/board.tsx`
- ⚙️ **`HttpError` carries the refusal BODY, and `refusalText` reads it** — every write door on this branch answers a refusal as a body and uses the status only to classify it (`INVALID_NAME_BODY` at 400, an `IngestResult` at 422, `INVITE_ADMIN_ONLY_BODY` at 403), so until this field existed the most a shell could show was `HTTP 422 for /v1/workspaces` — the shell paraphrasing a refusal it had never read, the same failure `shell-refusal.tsx` prevents for the six refusing READS. `undefined` is distinct from a parsed `null`: a proxy's HTML 502 must not surface as a `SyntaxError` naming neither the status nor the door. `refusalText` reads `message` and `reason` and answers `null` otherwise, never a manufactured sentence. `packages/app-core/src/online/http.ts`

It is kept off the gate by TWO independent facts — `test` is `vitest run` while the smoke is `test:e2e`, and `vitest.config.ts` includes `test/**` only — because one being edited away should not silently put a browser download on CI's critical path. **Every stub names the `apps/server/src/...:line` that registers the contract it stands in for**, which is the discipline this file exists under: the coordination doc records a missing route hiding behind this very smoke, so a stub with no named owner is that failure waiting to recur. Added because a Next server component needs `themeStylesheet()` and nothing else, and importing the root drags two `useEffect` components into a server module graph. `packages/ui/package.json`
- ⚙️ **The ONE local storage interface** — `SyncStorage` (`run`, `all`, `transaction`, `close`) over `SqlValue`/`SqlRow`, the single seam every offline replica writes through (coordination amendment 17): better-sqlite3 answers those four methods today, in tests and the dual-client harness; it is the seam op-sqlite (React Native, Plan 10 Task 16) and tauri-plugin-sql (desktop, Task 17) will answer, and neither exists yet, and `storageConformanceTests(name, make)` is the shared Vitest suite that keeps them honest — DDL/DML round-trip, commit-and-rollback, and no interleaving of concurrent transactions. JSON travels as TEXT: the replica owns (de)serialisation so adapters stay dumb. The native engine and the conformance suite ship behind the package's `./testing` subpath ONLY; the root barrel names its five exports one by one and a standing guard walks the module graph from it, so a Tauri or Expo bundle can never be handed a node-gyp addon or a test framework by the entry point. `packages/sync-client/src/storage/`, guard in `packages/sync-client/test/barrel.test.ts`
- ⚙️ **Local replica schema** — `migrateLocal(storage)` and `LOCAL_SCHEMA_VERSION`, idempotent DDL for the NINE replica tables — eight until ruling P36 added `snapshot_provenance`, a SIBLING table rather than a column on `snapshots` because `migrateLocal` runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and nothing else, and `LOCAL_SCHEMA_VERSION` is written into `meta` and never read back by anything, so a new column would work on a fresh device and throw `no such column` on every existing one: `snapshot_provenance` (the state and assignment claims a snapshot-bounded bootstrap cannot otherwise carry), `events` (the visibility-scoped local ledger, keeping BOTH `seq` for entity replay and `workspace_seq` for the resume cursor, because dropping either forces the replica to invent an order it was never told), `snapshots`, the reducer-folded read models `tickets` / `workflows` / `ticket_types`, `contests`, the ordered `outbox`, and `meta`. The read models are folded locally by the domain reducer — they are NEVER a downloaded copy of the server's `proj_*` projections. `client_time` / `server_time` hold the server's Z-normalised ISO instants verbatim, so string order IS chronological order and a device-offset label must never be written there. No column carries a hand-written ULID CHECK: `ULID_REGEX` in `@gisik-nokma/domain` stays the one definition of that format, and a second one in SQL would drift. Table shapes only — snapshot policy and bounded replay belong to later Plan 10 tasks. `packages/sync-client/src/storage/schema.ts`
- ⚙️ **Rule-engine boundary** — `evaluateEvent(env, ctx)` returning Accept or a Refusal that names its rule; pass-through internals that Plan 2 replaces. `packages/rule-engine/`
- ✅ **Event ingest API** — `POST /v1/events` batch ingest: parse at the door → advisory-locked per-entity `seq` and per-workspace `workspace_seq` (workspace lock first, then entity) + `serverTime` → entity↔workspace guard → permission gate (client door only) → rule-engine gate → append + projections in one transaction → index-aligned per-event committed/invalid/refused results. `GET /healthz`. `apps/server/src/routes/events.ts`, `apps/server/src/ingest/`
  - ✅ **Envelope-origin gate (partial permission gate)** — the ingest service has two entry points, and which one a caller uses is the whole design: `ingestClientBatch` is the client door and refuses any event whose envelope `origin` is `'server'` (rule `permission.role`, reason `Only the server itself may record server-origin events.`), while `ingestBatch` is the internal door and is not gated, because the server's own appends are legitimately server-origin. **Envelope-origin is the provenance enum `'web' | 'mobile' | 'desktop' | 'server' | 'mcp'`, NOT the browser `Origin` header — nothing here concerns CSRF.** Closes the forgery that let a client wear the server's provenance to walk past `contest.server-only` and write a permanent, un-deletable `claim.contested` attributing a fabricated claim to any actor in any workspace. Applied inside the ingest transaction (coordination decision 15), so Plan 10's `POST /v1/sync` inherits it by calling the client door. Deliberately partial and it names its own absences: no actor-identity, role, membership or visibility check yet — Task 5 fills those in on top. Landed here in §3 pending Plan 4's own catalogue task, which may relocate this bullet to §6 — Features.md has no §6 yet, and minting one early would break the mirror `test-cases/` keeps with these sections, which is why the case for it is 3.31 in `test-cases/03-foundation-ledger.md` rather than a new bucket. **`check-permission.ts`'s own status list (above `SERVER_ORIGIN_REASON`) said `POST /v1/sync` "does not exist yet" for 16 days after it existed, called this gate and was witnessed (E3-32) — Features.md was accurate throughout, the source docblock was not.** Fixed to CLOSED, with a content-accuracy test (case 12.398, `check-permission.test.ts`) reading the docblock back so the next drift reddens rather than waiting for a reviewer. `apps/server/src/permissions/check-permission.ts`, `apps/server/src/ingest/ingest-service.ts`
  - ⚙️ **Error surface** — schema refusals reach the client verbatim, naming the exact rule that fired; an unexpected failure answers one fixed 500 body and never an exception message, so no SQL fragment, constraint or table name leaves through the product's only door. `apps/server/src/app.ts`
- ⚙️ **Append-only ledger** — Postgres `events` table where UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE are refused by trigger, `(entity_kind, entity_id, seq)` is unique, and both clocks are `timestamptz` absolute instants: `client_time` the claimed instant beside `server_time` the received one, so they sort and compare without a cast and one moment stated in two offsets is one moment; `snapshots` table ready to bound future replay. `apps/server/migrations/`
- ⚙️ **Asia/Kolkata everywhere** — every pooled connection, the dev Postgres server, and every test database run with session timezone `Asia/Kolkata`, so an ad-hoc query reads the same clock the product shows. `apps/server/src/db.ts`, `docker-compose.yml`, `apps/server/test/helpers/db.ts`
- ⚙️ **Workspace stream cursor** — `workspace_seq`, unique per `(workspace_id, workspace_seq)` and assigned in the ingest transaction under a per-workspace advisory lock, is the only order a workspace stream may resume by; per-entity `seq` keeps entity history, replay and snapshots. Server-enriched and opaque to clients (coordination §18). `apps/server/src/ledger/event-store.ts`
- ⚙️ **Workspace stream cursor read** — `readStreamSeq(db, workspaceId)` returns the workspace's high-water `events.workspace_seq` (`0` for an empty workspace): the one position bootstrap, `subscribe.afterSeq` and `caught-up` all resume by (coordination §18). Deliberately not the envelope's per-entity `seq`, which restarts at 1 for every new entity and so silently skips their early events when used as a workspace cursor. Safe as a high-water read because ingest assigns the cursor under `lockWorkspace` inside the appending transaction. `apps/server/src/sync/stream-seq.ts`
- ⚙️ **Projection framework** — registry of deterministic `apply`/`reset` read models applied in the ingest transaction; `rebuildProjection` replays the canonical order; reference projection `proj_entity_heads` (newest event per entity, replay-safe). `apps/server/src/projections/`
- ⚙️ **Broadcast hook** — `onEventCommitted(cb)` fires only after commit, never for refused or invalid events; Plan 5 attaches WebSocket fan-out. `apps/server/src/ingest/ingest-service.ts`
- ⚙️ **Projection verifier** — `verify-projections` CLI re-derives every projection into a shadow schema, diffs against live in both directions, names drifted rows, exits nonzero on drift. `apps/server/src/tools/verify-projections.ts`

- ⚙️ **Environment contract & gate** — `.env.example` documents every configuration variable the product reads; each section names the plan that READS its group, and a variable whose plan has not landed is marked as documented ahead of its reader, not live, so an operator is never told to configure something inert without being told so. `pnpm check:env`, a step of the CI `gate` job, fails naming any variable code reads that the file does not document. Its roots are `apps/server/src`, **`apps/web`** and `packages`: `apps/web/src` alone would have missed `SERVER_ORIGIN` in `apps/web/next.config.ts`, and would miss a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable baked into the browser bundle from a page under `apps/web/app/`. The checker recognises three shapes rather than the one the plan specified: `process.env.NAME` access, destructuring off the environment, and — because this server hands the whole environment to `loadConfig` and declares its contract as zod schema KEYS — UPPER_SNAKE object keys inside files that mention `process.env`/`ProcessEnv`, which today is the ONLY shape the shipped code uses. A `process.env`-only gate would have reported “0 referenced in code” and passed vacuously forever, so two guards keep this one honest: finding zero variables anywhere is itself a failure, and so is `apps/server/src/config.ts` contributing none. `.env.example`, `scripts/check-env-example.mjs`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- ⚙️ **Task ledger & drift gate** — `docs/lanes/task-ledger.tsv` carries one row per `### Task N:` heading across the eleven implementation plans (177 today), and `pnpm check:tasks` validates it. The denominator is re-derived from the plan files on every run and is never hand-typed: before this, task-level completion was tracked nowhere — only step counts were — so progress was reconstructed each session from whatever prose was nearest, and both 167 and 177 had been recorded as "the total". Status is hand-asserted and machine-validated, never inferred from commit or PR titles (four incompatible formats appear in the merged set, and this repo has already recorded commit messages as an unreliable completion signal). `done` requires the PR's MERGE commit — not the implementing commit, which a squash-merge leaves unreachable from `main` — to be an ancestor of `origin/main`; `claimed` marks completion asserted only at plan or branch granularity, counted separately and never as complete, so the honest split between verified and inherited progress is visible on the face of the report. The gate fails on a plan task with no row, a row naming a task no plan contains, a duplicate row, an unknown status, a `done` row with no evidence, and evidence not reachable from `origin/main`; it also lists merged PRs no row cites, the direction that catches implementation work landing unrecorded. Its denominator carries a positive control — every numbered plan must yield at least one task, the coordination doc exactly zero — because the instrument that first counted these headings returned BLANK, not 0, for two plans with very long lines, and a tracker whose denominator can silently reach zero reports 0/0 = clean forever. `docs/lanes/task-ledger.tsv`, `scripts/check-task-ledger.mjs`

## 4. Workflow engine & rule vocabulary

- ⚙️ **Workflow vocabulary** — workflow definitions as data: states with open/active/terminal categories, transitions (including from-any), and the closed five-rule vocabulary (restrict-to, require-comment, require-evidence, require-field, require-different-user) as zod schemas; `workflow.defined` payloads carry the full definition plus an optional stateMapping. A workflow's name and every state's name are held to ruling P15's refinement (`displayName`, `packages/domain/src/display-name.ts` — the one schema the workspace, project, ticket-type, field and option names share since E6-20, 2026-09-21): a state named `" "` used to commit and head a board column with no header; it is refused now with *"a name of only spaces names nothing"* (cases 4.56, 5.79). Also the one forward state-id walk, `foldStateIdForward` — pure, and in domain because the engine, the server's ticket projection and the offline replica must all fold identically. `packages/domain/src/workflow.ts` Also the one forward state-id walk, `foldStateIdForward` — pure, and in domain because the engine, the server's ticket projection and the offline replica must all fold identically. `packages/domain/src/workflow.ts`
- ⚙️ **Structural validation** — `validateWorkflowDef`, pure and I/O-free so the future builder UI shares it: eleven plain-language checks covering workflows that cannot finish, states that cannot be reached or entered, duplicate ids/edges, and rules that can never fire or be satisfied — including `rdu-unenterable-state`, a four-eyes rule watching a state nothing in this version enters. `packages/domain/src/validate-workflow.ts` — `validateWorkflowDef`, pure and I/O-free so the future builder UI shares it: plain-language checks covering workflows that cannot finish, states that cannot be reached or entered, duplicate ids/edges, a declaration of the reserved `backlog` state, and rules that can never fire or be satisfied — including `rdu-unenterable-state`, a four-eyes rule watching a state nothing in this version enters. `packages/domain/src/validate-workflow.ts`
- ⚙️ **Advisory tier** — `adviseWorkflowDef`, a separate function returning warnings the builder shows without blocking publish; the rule engine never calls it, because everything `validateWorkflowDef` returns becomes a refusal. Two codes, answering two different questions. `rdu-bypassable` names a four-eyes rule whose guarded move is reachable without ever entering the watched state. `rule-bypassable` names a rule of ANY of the five kinds — restrict-to, require-comment, require-evidence, require-field and require-different-user alike — guarding one edge into a state while another edge enters that same state carrying no rule of that kind; the from-any edge is the archetype, and a plain fast-track edge voids a guard exactly as thoroughly. A covering guard on the other edge silences it, cover being same-kind-present rather than rule-set equivalence — parameters are never compared, which is what lets the owner's sanctioned fix (the anywhere arrow carrying its own guard) actually clear the warning. **The advisory tier cannot catch ONE class of dead rule, and the require-field PICKER is what stops it instead** (spec 2026-09-22): a `require-field` rule refuses only on an ABSENT or blank value, so a rule naming a built-in that every ticket always carries could never fire — and `priority`, the fifth built-in, is exactly that, since the reducer writes a non-blank level on every `ticket.created`. `adviseWorkflowDef` has no term for it (it reasons about EDGES, not about whether a field can be unset), so the guard is upstream: `BUILTIN_FIELD_CHOICES` (`packages/app-core/src/workflow-builder/fields.ts`) offers the four built-ins a rule can genuinely gate on and **deliberately omits `priority`**, which makes the two lists different on purpose rather than by oversight. Case `3.972` pins the difference as a SET DIFFERENCE against `BUILTIN_FIELD_IDS`, so a sixth built-in forces the question and a "fix" that puts `priority` back reddens. `packages/domain/src/advise-workflow.ts`
- ⚙️ **Universal Backlog state** (`BACKLOG_STATE`, `statesWithBacklog`, `transitionsWithBacklog`, the reserved id) — backlog/closed spec §1.1, 2026-09-17; cases 13.562–13.564. `packages/domain/src/workflow.ts`, `validate-workflow.ts`, `workflow-helpers.ts`
- ⚙️ **Starting status at ticket creation** (owner request 2026-09-23) — `isCreatableState(def, stateId)` (`packages/domain/src/workflow-helpers.ts`) is THE ONE HELPER every layer that decides whether a new ticket may be born somewhere calls: the state must exist, be neither the universal Backlog nor `category: 'terminal'`, and its new `creatable` flag (`workflowStateSchema`, absent means true, mirroring `blocked`) must not be `false`. `validateWorkflowDef` refuses a workflow whose start state has `creatable: false` (`start-state-not-creatable`) — such a workflow could never receive a ticket at all. `checkTicketCreated` (`packages/rule-engine/src/checks/hierarchy.ts`) refuses a `ticket.created` naming a non-creatable `stateId` with `workflow.state-not-creatable` ("Tickets cannot start in "<state>". Pick another status, or allow it in the workflow's settings."), placed the first line the workflow resolves — before every parent branch, since it is a fact about the workflow alone. **The client precheck previews the same refusal** (`precheckCreatableState`, `packages/app-core/src/precheck.ts`) — a NEW `ticket.created` branch ahead of the existing `precheckParentTerminal` fall-through, hand-rolled rather than routed through `evaluateEvent`/`contextFromCache` (that path throws on `ticket.created` for want of a ticket-type store — the CANARY in `precheck.test.ts` pins it). It reads the workflow off a NEW `PrecheckDeps.workflowId` the caller supplies (this cache cannot resolve the payload's `typeId` to a workflow itself), and defers (`not-evaluated`) rather than guessing when that dependency, or the definition it names, is not to hand. Case 4.57 (the helper alone), 4.58 (the validate refusal), 4.62 (the engine refusal), 4.63 (the client precheck, agreeing with the engine byte-for-byte on one fixture). `packages/rule-engine/src/checks/refusals.ts` (`workflowStateNotCreatableRefusal`), `packages/app-core/src/precheck.ts`.
- ⚙️ **The engine learns the universal edges, and the closed flag gets two doors** — backlog/closed spec §1.1/§2, 2026-09-17. Four new refusals: `checkTicketClosed` (`checks/close.ts`) accepts closing a terminal ticket and refuses `close-requires-terminal` (naming the state) or `already-closed` — and, since E6-8 (2026-09-21, case 4.55), refuses `parent-terminal-with-open-children` (`This ticket cannot be closed while N of its child tickets is/are still open.`) for a parent with a non-terminal child, the invariant's LAST door: a workflow republish can put a parent in a terminal category over open work (a kept state promoted to terminal, a dropped open state mapped onto a terminal one — both accepted at publish on purpose, since publish legality never reads occupancy), and nothing can close it there; `checkTicketReopened` accepts reopening a closed ticket and refuses `not-closed`; `evaluateTicketTransitioned` refuses `closed-ticket` ("This ticket is closed — reopen it first.") *before any edge is looked at* — a closed ticket has no legal move until an explicit `ticket.reopened` clears the flag. `transition.ts`'s state and edge resolution moved from `latest.states`/`latest.transitions` to `statesWithBacklog`/`transitionsWithBacklog`, so Start (`backlog → initialStateId`) and Send-to-backlog are legal without a workflow declaring them, and the parent-terminal invariant counts a backlog child as open. **Controller ruling extending the task brief**: a declared wildcard edge (`from: '*'`) means "from any AUTHORED state" — its author never knew about the universal Backlog — so a wildcard edge never applies FROM backlog; when the ticket's resolved current state is `BACKLOG_STATE_ID`, only the universal Start edge from `universalTransitions(latest)` can resolve, and declared exact/wildcard edges are not consulted at all. Without that guard a workflow's `* → done` would let a backlog ticket skip Start entirely. Cases 13.568–13.571. `packages/rule-engine/src/checks/close.ts`, `evaluate.ts`, `transition.ts`, `refusal-rules.ts`
- ⚙️ **Engine: `rank-requires-backlog`** — backlog/closed spec §8.1, second wave, 2026-09-18 (Task 2). `checkTicketRanked` (`packages/rule-engine/src/checks/rank.ts`) accepts a `ticket.ranked` whose ticket sits in the universal Backlog, and refuses every other ticket with `rank-requires-backlog` — `Only a backlog ticket can be ranked; this one is in "<state name>".` The test is `stateId` and NOT `stateCategory`: the universal `BACKLOG_STATE` is `category: 'open'`, so a category test would admit every open ticket in the workspace, and the backlog is one reserved id rather than a category. The state NAME is resolved over `statesWithBacklog(def)` (the synthetic Backlog state is appended by that helper, never authored by a workflow) and degrades to the bare state id when the reader cannot resolve the definition — the exact shape `close-requires-terminal` takes. A closed ticket is refused here too rather than by a flag test, because closing does not clear `stateId` (spec §2 keeps the final state visible), so a closed ticket is terminal and not backlog. `evaluateEvent` dispatches the arm, and `packages/app-core/src/precheck.ts`'s `precheckTicketRanked` mirrors the same verdict and the same sentence client-side — the two copies held together by case 13.604's agreement table, which drives both producers and asserts byte-identical reasons — on **both** branches the sentence can be produced on, the cached definition and the withheld one, because the degraded-name fallback is a second expression and a table that drove only the first left it pinned by nothing until fix round 1. Cases 13.700–13.701. `packages/rule-engine/src/checks/rank.ts`, `refusal-rules.ts`, `evaluate.ts`, `packages/app-core/src/precheck.ts`
- ⚙️ **Rule engine** — the real `evaluateEvent`: `ticket.transitioned` checked against authoritative state (transition legality, version walks across stateMappings, the parent-terminal-with-open-children invariant that no author can switch off — guarded from BOTH sides since E3-19 (2026-09-21): a parent may not enter terminal over open children, and a child may not leave a terminal state for a non-terminal one while its parent is terminal, refused `child-open-under-terminal-parent` with the parent's title and state named (`"<parent>" is finished (<state>); reopen it before moving this ticket back to "<state>".`); only the move that CREATES the relation is refused, so a child already open under a terminal parent keeps its ordinary moves — transition rules in order with first-refusal-wins); `workflow.defined` checked for structure, consecutive versioning, and stranding. `require-different-user` skips transition-log entries belonging to a workflow the ticket has been migrated off and resolves the rest forward through the version chain before comparing, so neither dropping and remapping a state nor a workflow migration can disarm four-eyes. It reads the log in ascending `seq` — the ordering is established at the point of use rather than inherited from whichever projection appended the entries — and it fails CLOSED: an entry it cannot resolve forward refuses the move ("this ticket's history cannot be read against its current workflow") instead of being skipped, because a history that cannot be read is not the same answer as a history with nobody in it. Every refusal names its rule and reasons in plain language. `packages/rule-engine/src/`
- ⚙️ **Contest evaluators** — the rule half of the contest lifecycle, run by the same shared engine on server and client. `claim.contested` is refused `contest.server-only` unless it arrives with `origin: 'server'`: a contest is the system's own record of a refusal, and a client that could forge one could forge its own exoneration. `claim.contested_resolved` is refused `contest.unknown` when it names no recorded contest, `contest.wrong-ticket` when the contest it names sits on a different ticket, and `contest.already-resolved` on a second resolution, because settling a settled contest would rewrite history. There is deliberately NO role gate on resolution — restricting it to the claimant or to an admin would leave contests rotting on tickets whose own collaborators could settle them, and the resolution is itself a recorded, attributed event. The lookup joins `EngineContext` as an OPTIONAL `getContest`, so every context predating contests still typechecks; a context that cannot answer it makes the evaluator THROW rather than refuse, because a wiring bug is not a claim about the world — without that guard the same missing lookup degrades into a `contest.unknown` refusal that reads entirely legitimate. Rule ids are dotted where `REFUSAL_RULES` are bare, deliberately: a rule id is an opaque string compared character for character by fixtures, the server's error surface and both clients. `packages/rule-engine/src/contests.ts`
- ⚙️ **Planted-defect fixture suite** — one JSON fixture per refusal path plus accepting twins, run by an in-memory harness and exported so server and client builds prove the same refusals against the same defects. **The count of fixtures is deliberately not restated in this bullet:** it is pinned where it is enforced, by the exact-count gate in `packages/rule-engine/test/fixtures.test.ts`, whose own comment requires that number to move in the same commit as any fixture — so it is the one copy an edit cannot leave behind. A literal here would be a second, unguarded copy, and it has already drifted once: this bullet said 84 while the directory holds 86. **Hedged (backlog/closed spec §2, 2026-09-17, Task 3's own ruling):** the five refusals `close-requires-terminal`, `already-closed`, `not-closed` and `closed-ticket` (backlog/closed spec §2, 2026-09-17) and `rank-requires-backlog` (second wave, spec §8.1, 2026-09-18) are NOT yet in this suite — "one per refusal path" is not exhaustive over every rule id `REFUSAL_RULES` now names, only over the ones a fixture was written for; parked as a named follow-on rather than built in that task, since the fixture-suite convention is Plan 10's own precedent and the closing paragraph of `test-cases/13-deployment-dogfooding.md`'s "Backlog and closed" section names it again. The harness prior-event schemas mirror their domain twins in PRESENCE and deliberately not in VALUE FORMAT: a fixture may use `t1` and `ws_1` because a prior event never passes `parseEvent`'s door, but it may not omit a key the real door requires — a looser prior door stages a world the server could never have produced, and the suite then proves a refusal against history that cannot exist. Each may carry an optional `notes` string — the only comment JSON allows — for a fixture whose shape is load-bearing beyond the outcome it asserts. The harness completes every prior event BEFORE filtering contest events out of the ticket-state fold, and the order is load-bearing rather than stylistic: default event ids are `fx_evt_<seq>` derived from POSITION, so filtering first REMOVES the contests before they are ever given ids — and a two-list variant that keeps them RENUMBERS the survivors instead. Either way a fixture naming `fx_evt_1` addresses nothing, and a double resolution refuses `contest.unknown` where it meant `contest.already-resolved`: still refused, wrong rule. The filter itself is mandatory, not hygiene: the fold throws on any type it does not know. `packages/rule-engine/fixtures/`, `packages/rule-engine/src/fixtures/harness.ts`
- ⚙️ **Workflow projection** — `proj_workflows` keeps every published version queryable (the engine's version walk needs intermediates and their mappings) and backs the server's `getWorkflowDef`; each row records the ledger position it was published at, so a definition can be asked for as of a point in the ledger rather than only as of now; idempotent apply, deterministic rebuild. `apps/server/src/projections/workflows.ts`
- ⚙️ **Type↔kind binding at the door (G1)** — `workflow.defined`'s registration declares `entityKind: 'workflow'`; `parseEvent` refuses any envelope naming that type against a different entity kind (`entity-kind-mismatch`), the same general door every entity-kind-declaring registration gets (coordination doc §11). Layered with the engine's own kind checks by design: fixtures and Plan 10's offline replica reach `evaluateEvent` directly, bypassing `parseEvent`, so the door alone would leave them unguarded. `packages/domain/src/parse-event.ts`, `packages/domain/src/registry.ts`
- ⚙️ **Entity↔workspace binding at ingest (G2)** — an entity belongs to one workspace forever: `commitOne` reads `proj_entity_heads` after both locks and before the engine runs, and refuses `entity-workspace-mismatch` when an envelope's `workspaceId` disagrees with the entity's recorded one. A server-side door, deliberately not a shared-engine rule — a workspace-scoped client replica cannot see that an entity id is already bound elsewhere, so Plan 10's offline replica must mirror this door knowingly rather than find it in the fixtures. No fixture; proven by integration test. `apps/server/src/ingest/ingest-service.ts`
- ⚙️ **Projection registration order, pinned (G3)** — `buildProjectionRegistry()` registers `proj_entity_heads` before `proj_workflows`; registration order is application order inside the ingest transaction (coordination doc §8), so a projection may read a table an earlier one wrote in the same transaction. A DB-free test pins the exact array, so a re-ordering breaks loudly rather than silently before any later projection comes to depend on it. `apps/server/src/projections/index.ts`

*(The **Contest evaluators** bullet above, and the six contest fixtures now counted by **Planted-defect fixture suite** — one per `CONTEST_RULES` refusal path, plus two accepting twins — are Plan 10 Task 2 — the rule half of offline sync's contest lifecycle, landed in §4 because they are rule-engine code and §4 is where the engine and its fixture suite are catalogued. Plan 10's own catalogue task (Task 18) owns `Features.md` §12 and `test-cases/12-*.md` with pre-pinned 12.x case numbers, and may relocate them there; they sit in §4 for now on the same precedent as the §3 bullets above. *(Plan 3's keystone plus Chain A and Chain B Tasks 9–13 — the ticket type model, the event vocabulary, the engine-context rider, the reducer, the hierarchy and field refusals, all three ticket projections (`proj_ticket_types`, `proj_tickets`, `proj_rollups`), the server `EngineContext` that reads them, and the ticket history route. - ⚙️ **Ticket type system** — built-in ladder epic(1)/story(2)/task(3)/sub-task(4) as seed data plus custom reusable types defined by `ticket-type.defined` events: name, icon, rank, workflow binding, and typed custom fields (text, number, date, select, person), Zod-validated. A custom type's re-rank is accepted whatever tickets already sit where (E6-3, 2026-09-21, case 5.76 — a recorded decision: the rank invariants are write-time invariants and occupancy is never an engine input, so tickets already placed keep their parents and the placements the new rank forbids are refused only when someone next tries to make them; the type editor says so at the moment the rank changes, 10.120). A select field cannot exist without its choices, no custom field may shadow a built-in id, and `DEEPEST_RANK` is a pinned constant rather than a maximum over the defined types — the rank at or below which a type's tickets will require a parent must not shift underfoot when an admin defines a deeper type. `packages/domain/src/ticket-types.ts` The type's name, each field's name and each select option are held to ruling P15's `displayName` (E6-20 — a `" "` option was a choice with no label; case 5.79). null` folded an omitted value into a clearing claim nobody made; with the key required that coalesce was unreachable and has been dropped, because keeping it would state the defect as the design), `ticket.reparented`, `ticket.workflow_rebound`, `comment.added` (opaque doc body), `attachment.added` (a `kind`-discriminated union: an `upload` carrying the server's sniffed mime/size and its `sha256` of the stored bytes, or a `drive-reference` carrying the pointer plus the name, mimeType and `capturedAt` last seen on a file this product does not hold). ⚠ **The eleven above are a MOMENT, not the vocabulary.** The registry holds **thirty-four** types, **eighteen** of them filed against `entityKind: 'ticket'`, and **eight** of those are not named above: `claim.contested` and `claim.contested_resolved` (their own bullet in §4), `visibility.set`, and the closure and soft-delete pairs — `ticket.closed`, `ticket.reopened`, `ticket.ranked`, `ticket.deleted`, `ticket.restored`.
