Cases 14.317–14.324.
- ✅ **The assistant can find people and list tickets across a workspace** (MCP CRUD plan Task 8; `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/read-tools.ts`; both doors, through `allTools`) — `list_members` reads `/v1/workspaces/:id/members` (name, role, and a real email where the server serves one) and falls back to `/actor-names` ONLY on that route's 404, which is how the server says a guest may not see the roster: a guest gets the names of the people on tickets shared with them — no role, no email — and a stranger is told "workspace not found or not visible to you". `list_tickets` takes EXACTLY ONE of `projectId` (`/v1/projects/:id/tickets`) or `workspaceId` (`/v1/workspaces/:id/ticket-list`, every project the caller can see, archived projects excluded — NOT `/tickets`, which is Plan 4's visibility list); both or neither is refused with a plain sentence before anything is sent. The `filter` is the domain schema, so it takes `"me"` in assignee/collaborator slots and the plural keys (`assigneeIds`, `collaboratorIds`, `typeIds`, `stateIds`, `stateCategories`, `priorities` P1–P3); a singular+plural pair of one field is refused with "a field takes a single value OR a list, not both", and the server's bare `invalid_filter` 400 is turned into a sentence naming what can be wrong. The tool count is now seventeen. Cases 14.328–14.335.

## 15. Notes

- ⚙️ **A note is an entity in the ledger** — nine `note.*` events (`packages/domain/src/events/note-events.ts`), folded by `applyNoteEvent` (`packages/domain/src/note-state.ts`); `comment.added` is filed against notes as well as tickets. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-notes-design.md` §3.
- ⚙️ **The detach rule is derived in the reducer** — the last detach of an inherit-scoped note reverts to the remembered scope or to private (`applyNoteEvent`, spec §3.3–3.4).
- ⚙️ **Notes are projected into `proj_notes`, `proj_note_attachments`, `proj_note_comments`** — whole-row writes from the reducer, verifier-clean, no history table (versions are read from `events`).
- ⚙️ **One reader predicate, two spellings, asserted equal** — `canReadNote` and `visibleNotesWhere` (spec §4.1, §4.3).
- ⚙️ **Note writes are gated by `checkNotePermission`** — author/admin-reader/owner edit; readers attach on tickets they can see; readers comment (spec §4.2; admins have no override beyond what they can read, per `can-see.ts`).
- ✅ **Notes can be read back through the API** — list, one note, a ticket's notes, comments, history and a version, every read filtered by the reader predicate; an unreadable note is a 404 identical to an absent one (spec §6.4).
- ⚙️ **The client data source exposes seven note reads** (`getNotes`, `getDeletedNotes`, `getNote`, `getNotesForTicket`, `getNoteComments`, `getNoteHistory`, `getNoteVersion`) — answered by the ONLINE source from the routes and, since Plan 2, by the REPLICA from the local tables.
- ⚙️ **Files uploaded into a note are owned by the note** — upload needs author/admin-reader/owner, download needs a reader (spec §4.4).
- ⚙️ **A note cannot be filed under a project nobody founded** — spec §3.3's existence precondition, asked in `checkProjectExists` (existence) before `checkNotePermission` (membership), so the refusal names the actual fault. The archived half is deliberately NOT enforced, for notes or for tickets.
- ⚙️ **Note events stream to readers only** — a new `note` audience class; widening announces `reach-granted` with a `notes` arm, so a device whose cursor ran past a note while it was invisible is told the id and head position to pull (spec §5.1; narrowing is client-driven — never a server purge, ruling P23).
- ⚙️ **A ticket becoming visible brings its inherit-scoped notes with it** — a ticket grant trigger also names the `inherit` notes attached to it and to its inheriting descendants, filtered to the notes the reader can actually read; a note that does not depend on the ticket (project, workspace, explicit) is not announced (spec §5.2).
- ⚙️ **Narrowing reaches devices through reconcile** — the client presents the note ids it holds as `heldNoteIds` and drops the ones the server now refuses (`restrictedNotes`); an unknown id answers exactly as a genuine loss, so the reply carries no existence oracle (ruling P23; spec §5.1's server-side purge is deliberately not built).
- ⚙️ **A device can pull one note's history** (`GET /v1/notes/:id/events`, the same row shape the ticket events route serves) and receives every readable note's ledger at bootstrap, so a fresh device and a new member need no notice (spec §5.1).
- ⚙️ **Notes live in the local replica** (`notes`, `note_comments`, local schema version 2) — folded by the same `applyNoteEvent` the server's projection uses, removed by `purgeEntity` and workspace-scoped by `revokeScope`; `getDeletedNotes` applies the deleted-note gate (author, admin or owner), which is narrower than the read rule (spec §5.3).
- ✅ **Notes work offline on the web app and are ready for desktop and mobile** — every note read is answered from the local replica, and a note that arrives by pull emits a `refresh` frame so an open screen re-reads it (spec §5.3).
- ⚙️ **The client seam has a witness** — the engine, the SHIPPED HTTP transport and the REAL routes are wired to each other (`apps/server/test/sync/notes-client-seam.test.ts`), which is the one place a frame ladder, a body schema and an engine request are measured together rather than each against a fake of the next.
- ⚙️ **Two-device behaviour of notes is exercised end to end** on the dual-client rig — reach lost by a scope change and by the last detach, reach gained by a widening, the ticket cascade, and delete/restore — against the REAL stream filter, reconcile rule and replica together (Plan 2 Task 8).
- ⚙️ **Gaining reach pulls the note's history; losing it purges through reconcile** — the engine queues the ids a `reach-granted` notice admits (each with its head position, so a complete copy is not re-fetched), pulls them through `GET /v1/notes/:id/events`, and presents every held note id to `reconcile` on catch-up (spec §5.1).
- ⚙️ **The database gains `pg_trgm` and `pgvector`** — migration `1790200000000_note-search.sql`; every Postgres image (two compose files, two CI service blocks) is `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`; a pre-flight tool (`pnpm --filter @gisik-nokma/server run search:preflight`) checks a target database before the migration runs, because `vector` is not a trusted extension and so needs a superuser to create.
- ⚙️ **A small embedding model runs inside the server process** — `minishlab/potion-base-32M`, 512 dims, static (one vector per token; no ONNX and no network), bundled under `apps/server/models/` and reaching the image through `pnpm deploy`. Measured by Task 2's spike: the plan's first choice, MiniLM/ONNX, fails on the `node:22-alpine` runtime image with `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`. `apps/server/src/search/embedding.ts` (`CURRENT_MODEL`, `EMBEDDING_DIM`, `embedTexts`, `embedQuery`); `search_note_chunks` (migration `1790300000000_note-chunks.sql`) is a cache with `source_seq`/`model` provenance, **not** a projection. **The tokenizer path has no native dependency either** (task/notes-3-runtime-fix, 2026-09-23): Task 2's own tokenizer, `@huggingface/transformers`'s `AutoTokenizer`, dlopens `onnxruntime-node` at import time regardless of which export is used — the same `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` the ONNX spike hit, just one import away — and crashed the server at boot in the real image. `embedding.ts` now builds a `@huggingface/tokenizers` `Tokenizer` directly over the committed `tokenizer.json`/`tokenizer_config.json`; that package is the SAME code `AutoTokenizer` bundles, reached through a public entry point that never links a native binding (`@huggingface/transformers` stays a `devDependency`, used only by the host-only equivalence test, and `pnpm deploy --prod` does not ship it). Guarded by case 18.164, which runs the built module in a fresh process with `process.dlopen` wrapped and asserts zero native loads, and case 18.166 (🧪, `DOCKER_BOOT_CHECK=1`), which builds and boots the real image.
- ⚙️ **Notes are indexed for full-text search** — `proj_note_search` (folded title, body and attached-ticket text, with a generated `tsv` weighted A/B/C) and `proj_note_lexemes` (a trigram-indexed vocabulary per workspace), kept current by `noteSearchProjection` and replays clean under `verifyProjections`. Folding is `foldSearchText` (`packages/domain/src/search-fold.ts`): the four spellings of the raka mark are unified, and the mark is removed only between two letters. **Visibility is applied at read time only** — the index is complete and the reader predicate is in every query.
- ⚙️ **An in-process worker keeps note embeddings current** — `startEmbedWorker` (`apps/server/src/search/embed-worker.ts`) runs every `EMBED_WORKER_INTERVAL_MS` (10 s), is nudged after a commit by a listener `buildApp` registers (`onNoteBodyCommitted`, forwarded from `index.ts`), and is also the backfill and the re-index after a model change. One pass at a time; a deleted note's chunks are dropped in the same pass. `EMBED_WORKER_ENABLED=false` stops it without stopping the server.
- ⚙️ **Three note search queries** — prefix lexical (last word `:*`, `ts_rank_cd` order), trigram correction on zero hits (one rerun, never two), and nearest-chunk meaning (`DISTINCT ON`, 200 candidates, first 20) — all in `apps/server/src/read/note-search.ts`, each with `visibleNotesWhere` INSIDE the statement. `HEADLINE_OPTIONS` moved to `read/headline.ts` so the ticket search and the note search cut snippets the same way.
- ✅ **Notes are searchable through the same search API as tickets**, labelled by kind, with meaning search behind `mode=meaning`. `NoteSearchHit` on the client (`packages/app-core/src/view-types.ts`) carries `source`, which the SERVER does not send — the mode is the request's own parameter — and `mapNoteSearchHits` stamps it from the `mode` the caller asked for. The replica refuses `searchNotes` with a `ReplicaGapError`: the device has neither index, and serving the lexical half alone would make the screen work while typing and fail after the pause.
- ✅ **Search as you type**: spelling results on every keystroke (100 ms debounce, REPLACING the list), meaning results appended after a pause (400 ms after the last change), and **never reordering what is shown** — the fast half is what a person is reading when the slow half arrives. A response for a superseded query updates nothing, including `corrected`. `apps/web/src/use-notes-search.ts` (spec §7.8).
- ⚙️ **Search is measured against a real corpus, and the Garo evaluation awaits pairs** — `seed:search-corpus` (`apps/server/src/tools/seed-search-corpus.ts`) submits 10 000 notes over 3 workspaces through the CLIENT door, so projections and chunks fill the way the product fills them; `apps/server/test/search/perf.test.ts` runs only with `NOTES_PERF=1` and records p95 per mode (spec §7.9). `apps/server/test/fixtures/garo-eval.json` ships EMPTY and its case skips with a printed reason until the owner supplies 30–50 pairs (spec §7.10).
- ✅ **A Notes page at `/notes`**, linked left of Inbox, listing every workspace and project the person belongs to (spec §9.1–9.2). The link is the nav's first PREFIX match — it stays lit on `/notes/<id>`, which draws the same view with a note open (`apps/web/src/notes-nav-link.tsx`, `apps/web/src/notes/notes-page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/notes/`).
- ✅ **The notes tree**: notes under their workspace or project, newest first, ticket keys beside attached notes, a Deleted group with Restore, and a title filter that narrows every section (`apps/web/src/notes/workspace-notes-section.tsx`, `apps/web/src/notes/note-row.tsx`).
- ✅ **Create a note anywhere you belong**, choosing its home and scope; change scope later from the byline chip (spec §9.3; D3). **The chip's scope change commits (case `18.430`):** `scope-editor.tsx` used to send `note.scope_set` with the scope NESTED under `scope` — only `note.created` nests it; `noteScopeSetPayload` IS the scope — so the door answered `invalid-payload` to every change from Private, Workspace or Specific people; the caller now sends the flat shape. The people picker is one component shared with the ticket visibility editor (`apps/web/src/notes/create-note-dialog.tsx`, `apps/web/src/notes/scope-editor.tsx`, `packages/app-core/src/views/people-picker.tsx`). **The typed title survives a page re-render (case `18.433`):** the dialog re-seeds on open, keyed on the home's and ticket's ids rather than the `defaultHome` object `NotesPage` rebuilds every render, so a live-list refresh no longer empties the title mid-typing (`apps/web/src/notes/create-note-dialog.tsx`).
- ✅ **A note's page**: breadcrumb, editable title, byline with author, scope and attached tickets, reading time, Copy as Markdown, the shared editor with wiki-links (spec §9.2, §8.5). A reader gets a static title, a static scope chip, a read-only editor with no toolbar, and no detach × on its badges — an editor (author, admin-reader or owner) gets all four (`apps/web/src/notes/note-document.tsx`, `note-title.tsx`, `note-byline.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/components/note-badge.tsx`). **Opening a note does not flash "That note is no longer shared with you."** — the workspace search's found note is the live query's initial answer (`note-document.tsx`; owner report 2026-09-29, cases 18.460–18.461), and the page holds the document back (a "Loading…" hint) until the workspaces read has answered, so a slow read never draws it either (`notes-page.tsx`; case 18.462).
- ✅ **Notes save themselves** — one `note.body_set` per 2 s typing pause (not per keystroke), a draft kept on the device (`localStorage`, keyed by user and note) until the server accepts it, and a Saved / Saving… / Not saved (kept on this device) indicator in the editor's own footer (spec §9.4, D14). The draft also flushes on blur, on `beforeunload`, and on leaving the note; reopening a note with a newer local draft than its last server save loads the draft, not the stale server copy (`apps/web/src/notes/use-note-autosave.ts`). **Reopening with a recovered draft shows a "Restored unsaved changes from Nm ago" banner (KB `DraftRestoreBanner`, adapted):** Keep hides it and the draft saves as any edit; Discard cancels the pending write, deletes the key and remounts the editor over the server's body (`useNoteAutosave().restoredAt` / `discardDraft`, `apps/web/src/notes/draft-restore-banner.tsx`, `.gn-notes__draft-banner`). Editors only.
- ✅ **History**: every saved version of a note, newest first, each named by who recorded it and when; opening one shows it read-only with a "Viewing version from…" banner, and Restore returns the note to that body (spec §9.5, D15). Open to any viewer — Restore is what `canEdit` gates, not the panel itself (`apps/web/src/notes/history-panel.tsx`).
- ✅ **Comments on notes**, the same thread tickets have (D19) — `CommentsThread` (`packages/app-core`), mounted under the editor, reused rather than duplicated; a note's `comment.added` files against `{ kind: 'note', id }` and the thread reloads on commit. Open to every reader, not gated by `canEdit`: notes have no author-only comment restriction (`apps/web/src/notes/note-comments.tsx`).
- ✅ **Mentioning people in a note** (owner ruling 2026-09-29: "yes, notify on note mentions") — the `@` picker is wired into the note body editor and the note comment box, both drawing from `mentionCandidatesOf`, the ONE source the ticket sheet's editors use too (`packages/app-core/src/mention-candidates.ts`, `apps/web/src/notes/note-document.tsx`, `note-comments.tsx`). At and below 60rem nothing changes (one page scroll; the tree is the toggle panel) — `@media (width > 60rem)` is the exact complement of the existing `max-width: 60rem` block, so the breakpoint is still the one. A heading jumped to lands 1rem under the column's top. Opening a different note returns the document column to the top (a hash link is left to its own scroll; in production a note change REMOUNTS the page — App Router keys the segment by its param — so the column starts at the top for free and the effect covers a reused page). **Each scroller is also `position: relative`** (N1b, measured in a browser: the page still scrolled at 1280px because the editor's visually-hidden `disabledReason` span in `TicketEditorSlot.tsx` is inline `position: absolute` with no positioned ancestor — rendered on every note, since the note editor passes no `submit` — and so escaped the column's `overflow` and stretched the page; as the containing block each column clips it. Not on `.gn-notes` (it does not clip) and no `overflow: clip` (it would hide the next stray element); `position: relative` makes no containing block for `position: fixed`, so the popups, the TOC launcher and the progress bar still anchor to the viewport). **The tree keeps its scroll across that remount** — `carryTreeScroll` (`apps/web/src/notes/tree-scroll.ts`) records the offset in a module-level value and re-applies it as the new tree's rows load (a browser clamps `scrollTop` to what is scrollable), until the reader takes over or five seconds pass; lifting the tree into `app/notes/layout.tsx` was not done (it would stop `getMyWorkspaces` re-running per note and break the one-shot lost-access toast and the drawer reset). - ⚙️ **Ticket references survive everywhere a document goes** — plain text (`packages/domain/src/doc-text.ts`), the comment renderer (`packages/app-core/src/views/comment-body.tsx`, `comments-thread.tsx`), and the mobile WebView bridge (`ticketQuery`/`ticketResults`, `packages/editor/src/webview/`). `renderCommentBody`'s new optional `ticketHref` parameter links a chip only when the caller supplies a resolver; absent, it renders a plain span.
- ⚙️ **The `:ticket` picker searches the workspace's tickets** through the existing search; the key rides on every hit, and the project page puts the current project's own hits first, a stable partition (`apps/web/src/ticket-ref-callbacks.ts`, `packages/app-core/src/online/mappers.ts`). Offline, the picker says "Search needs a connection" instead of "No tickets match", and the editor still mounts (`packages/editor/src/extensions/ticket-ref.ts`). **`:ticket` with nothing typed yet never reaches `search`** (bug fix, owner report 2026-09-23, case 9.313): the server's search route refuses an empty term outright, so a bare `:ticket` used to look like it "did not open" — it now answers from `getTickets(projectId, {}, 'flat')`, the current project's tickets, matching `:note`'s own empty-query behaviour (`apps/web/src/ticket-ref-callbacks.ts`). **In a note's editor and a note's comment box — contexts with NO project — the same bare `:ticket` lists the workspace's recent visible tickets instead** (Unit 6e, owner ruling 2026-09-29, case 18.310): it used to hand `search('')` the empty term and draw "Search needs a connection". `buildWorkspaceQueryTickets` reads `getTickets` for every live project `getMyWorkspaces` lists (so the server's own visibility decides what is offered) and merges them newest-created first (ULID order — `ListRow` has no updated-at); one failing project does not blank the picker, only all failing does. A typed query is `search` as before (`apps/web/src/ticket-ref-callbacks.ts`, `apps/web/src/notes/note-document.tsx`, `apps/web/src/notes/note-comments.tsx`).
- ✅ **Tagging a ticket links back to it wherever the reference is shown** — on the project page's description and comments, and in a note's own comments — `TicketSheet` and `NoteComments` supply `queryTickets`/`resolveTicketHref`, and `CommentsThread` forwards `ticketHref` to the comment renderer.
- ✅ **Tagging a note in a ticket comment attaches it** (D27–D28) — posting a comment that references one or more notes ingests the comment, then a further ingest of the implied `note.attached` events; the ticket's Notes section reloads and shows the new badges. A refused or unreachable attachment leaves the comment posted and shows a toast naming the note and the reason; a note's OWN comment thread never implies an attachment, whatever it references. `packages/app-core/src/flows/attachments-implied-by.ts`, wired in `ticket-sheet.tsx`'s `submitComment`.
- ✅ **A note's title pastes and drops PLAIN TEXT only** (owner report, 2026-09-24 — "my title became huge when i pasted ... Title should always paste format stripped text only"). The `<h1 contentEditable>` had no `onPaste`/`onDrop` of its own, so the browser inserted the clipboard's HTML verbatim; both handlers now `preventDefault` that insertion and hand the `text/plain` payload to `insertPlainText` (`document.execCommand('insertText', …)`, falling back to a Selection/Range insertion where that is unavailable — jsdom, notably, which is why the fallback is real code and not dead code), through `sanitizePastedTitleText`, which collapses every run of whitespace, including newlines, to one space. **`contentEditable="plaintext-only"` — the brief's own suggested second line of defence — was tried and DROPPED**: it silently breaks `@testing-library/user-event`'s `type()`/`clear()` for this element (their `isContentEditable` check recognises only `contenteditable="true"`/`""`), which is a cost the handlers alone do not need paid, since `preventDefault()` is a complete fix on its own in every browser. A repo-wide sweep for `contentEditable` outside the rich editor, across `apps/web`, `packages/app-core` and `packages/ui`, found exactly one other candidate — none: the note title is the ONLY one; the ticket title is a real `<input>`, immune to this class of defect by construction. `apps/web/src/notes/note-title.tsx`.
- ✅ **A note's breadcrumb omits an absent level entirely — no empty segment, no stray separator** (owner report, 2026-09-24: a note's crumb read "Convenience Corner /  / Furniture"). A WORKSPACE-scoped note's `homeProjectId` is legitimately `''` (the domain refuses an empty one only for `scope.mode === 'project'`), and the old JSX rendered the project `<li>` regardless, painting a `.find()` miss over with `?? ''` instead of omitting the slot; `.gn-breadcrumb__item + .gn-breadcrumb__item::before` draws its separator only between two RENDERED siblings, so omitting the `<li>` removes the stray separator for free. `apps/web/src/notes/note-document.tsx`.

## 16. Archive, delete and purge

- ⚙️ **Eight lifecycle event types** — `workspace.archived`/`restored`, `workspace.deleted`/`undeleted`, `project.deleted`/`undeleted`, `purge.marked`/`unmarked` (`packages/domain/src/events/lifecycle-events.ts`), registered in `packages/domain/src/vocabulary.ts`. Every payload is `{}` and `.strict()`: the item is `entity.id`, so a payload has nothing left to name, and `.strict()` turns a stranger's field (including a client-supplied `dueAt`) into a refusal rather than a silent drop. Undelete is spelled `*.undeleted` for projects and workspaces because `*.restored` already means un-archive for both; tickets and notes keep their existing `*.restored` for delete/undelete, unchanged by this plan. `purge.marked`/`purge.unmarked` are filed against any of the four purgeable kinds (workspace, project, ticket, note) — the registry's `entityKind` takes a list, the same mechanism `comment.added` uses. `PURGE_DELAY_DAYS = 15` (`packages/domain/src/lifecycle.ts`) is the only place the purge window is spelled; `purgeDueAt(markedAt)` derives the due instant from the mark's `server_time`, never carried in a payload (spec §4, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-trash-and-purge-design.md`). Case ids `19.001`–`19.004` (`test-cases/19-trash.md`).
- ⚙️ **`proj_workspaces`** (`apps/server/migrations/1790500000000_lifecycle.sql`) — the lifecycle-only projection table for workspaces: a row exists only once a workspace has had a lifecycle event (`archived`, `deleted_at`/`deleted_by`, `purge_marked_at`/`purge_marked_by`); absence means live, unarchived, unmarked, and there is no backfill for the same reason a ledger rebuild would not create one either. The workspace's NAME is not here — it stays folded from the ledger elsewhere. `proj_projects`, `proj_tickets` and `proj_notes` each gain `purge_marked_at`/`purge_marked_by`, and `proj_projects`/`proj_notes` also gain `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` (`proj_tickets` already had that pair). `apps/server/src/projections/lifecycle.ts`'s `lifecycleProjection` folds all eight lifecycle types, registered directly after `notesProjection` (`projections/index.ts`) so every row a mark can name already exists; it writes `event.serverTime`, never `now()`, so a rebuild reproduces the live row exactly. It declares only `proj_workspaces` in `tables` — the one table it resets — while the lifecycle columns it also writes onto `proj_projects`/`proj_tickets`/`proj_notes` are covered by `verifyProjections` through those tables' OWN owning projections, since the shadow rebuild replays every registered projection into the same shadow schema before diffing (case 19.015 proves this with a hand-write control on each of the four tables). `apps/server/src/projections/notes.ts`'s `note.deleted`/`note.restored` handling now also writes `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` beside the existing `deleted` flag, computed from the event (never the reducer, since these two columns are server-projection-only) and preserved across every other note event. Case ids `19.010`–`19.015` (`test-cases/19-trash.md`).
- ⚙️ **Authority (T3)** (`apps/server/src/permissions/check-permission.ts`) — spec §4's matrix, all enforced at the real `POST /v1/events` door. Workspace archive/restore/delete/undelete and a workspace mark/unmark are `role === 'owner'` only (`WORKSPACE_OWNER_ONLY_REASON`, exported), checked beside `workspace.renamed`'s own gate and deliberately narrower than `isWorkspaceAdmin` — an admin who could delete or purge-mark a workspace could take away everyone's access to it. `project.deleted`/`project.undeleted` join `ADMIN_ONLY_TYPES` (the same set `project.archived`/`project.restored` are in); a project mark/unmark answers the same workspace admin/owner question beside it. A ticket mark/unmark inherits `ticket.deleted`'s project-admin rule (`ticketDeleteAuthorityReason`, widened to `'mark' | 'unmark'`) in `checkVisibilityPermission`. A note mark/unmark inherits `note.deleted`'s author/admin-reader/owner rule via `NOTE_AUTHOR_EVENTS`. `project.deleted`/`undeleted` and a project purge mark also pass `checkProjectExists` (`projectsNamedBy`'s arms), kind-aware for the purge mark since it is filed against any of the four purgeable kinds and only a PROJECT-kind mark is a project id. **A pre-existing gate needed widening to make the feature reachable at all**: `packages/rule-engine/src/checks/deletion.ts`'s `checkTicketLive` refuses every write against a soft-deleted ticket except a short exempt list — `purge.marked`/`purge.unmarked` had to join it, since marking an already-deleted ticket for purge is exactly what Task 4's future `DELETE_FIRST_REASON` requires, not an exception to it (`test/live-ticket.test.ts`'s own registry-derived completeness check caught the omission). Case ids `19.020`–`19.023` (`test-cases/19-trash.md`).
- ⚙️ **State refusals (`checkLifecycle`)** (`apps/server/src/permissions/check-lifecycle.ts`) — spec §4's state machine: `ALREADY_DELETED_REASON`/`NOT_DELETED_REASON`/`DELETE_FIRST_REASON`/`ALREADY_MARKED_REASON`/`NOT_MARKED_REASON`/`UNMARK_FIRST_REASON`/`PURGE_DUE_REASON` (all `(kind) => string`) plus `WORKSPACE_DELETED_REASON`/`PROJECT_DELETED_REASON`, reported under `LIFECYCLE_RULE = 'lifecycle.state'`. Wired into `checkPermission`'s chain after `checkPrefixReservation` and before `checkVisibilityPermission`; `now` is a parameter (the door passes `new Date()`) so a test can pin the purge-due boundary. Reads Task 2's columns directly — a workspace, project, ticket or note's own `deleted_at`/`purge_marked_at` — never the payload, since none of the eight lifecycle events carry state to check. `ticket.restored`/`note.restored`'s "not deleted" refusal is deliberately NOT duplicated here: the rule engine (`checkTicketRestored`) and the note reducer (`applyNoteEvent`) already answer it byte-identically; `checkLifecycle` adds only the marked arm for those two. Containment (`purge.marked` refused when the item's container is already deleted): a ticket's container is its project; a project-scoped note's is its home project (a workspace-level note's is the workspace itself, left to Task 5's broader workspace gate rather than duplicated here); a project's is its workspace. A mark surviving its parent's later deletion is NOT cleared by that deletion — the column stays exactly as the mark left it (case 19.034's control). Case ids `19.030`–`19.035` (`test-cases/19-trash.md`).
- ⚙️ **A deleted workspace is hidden from every read, recoverable at the write door** (spec T10) — the CHOKE POINT: `resolveEffectiveRole(db, userId, workspaceId, { includeDeleted? })` (`apps/server/src/permissions/effective-role.ts`) resolves a member of a workspace with `proj_workspaces.deleted_at IS NOT NULL` as the exact value a stranger gets (`workspaceRole: null`, empty `projects` — the SAME early-return branch, never a hand-built copy), by DEFAULT (`includeDeleted` defaults `false`). Since all 27 call sites already route through this one function, every read it feeds — `GET /v1/me/work`, `GET /v1/search`, every `:workspaceId` route, `GET /v1/tickets/:id/history`, `GET /v1/stream`'s subscribe handler (`stream/routes.ts`), `POST /v1/sync/bootstrap` and `.../sync/reconcile` — needed zero code changes; measured empirically with case 19.040's stranger-vs-member response-equality comparisons. Two call sites are deliberately exempted with `includeDeleted: true`: the write door's own `checkPermission` (Review Focus 1 — an owner must still be able to submit `workspace.undeleted`/`purge.marked`/`purge.unmarked` on their own deleted workspace) and `engine-context.ts`'s `readMembershipState` (the rule engine judges truth and must never filter). `checkLifecycle` gains a workspace-wide gate, checked FIRST before its per-type switch: inside a deleted workspace, every event is refused `WORKSPACE_DELETED_REASON` except the workspace's own `workspace.undeleted`/`purge.marked`/`purge.unmarked` (the brief's three) and, by ruling, its own `workspace.deleted` too (so a second delete still answers the more specific `ALREADY_DELETED_REASON`, the same precedent `LIVE_GATE_EXEMPT` sets for `ticket.deleted`). Of the plan's five named DIRECT `proj_memberships` reads, only `GET /v1/me/workspaces` (`routes/workspaces.ts`) needed a code change (`LEFT JOIN proj_workspaces`, filtered on `deleted_at IS NULL`, serving `coalesce(pw.archived, false)`) — the other four are either unreachable for a deleted workspace (their one caller already gates through the resolver first: `workspace-counts.ts`'s `visibleMemberCount`, `builder-reads.ts`'s `readMembers`) or a background tool whose behavior change is cosmetic-only (`sweep-user-preferences.ts`: a member of a merely-deleted, not-yet-purged workspace now reports as `noRevocationEvidence` instead of `currentMembers`, but Step 3's fail-closed guard means nothing is actually swept without a real `membership.revoked` event, which a workspace deletion never writes). `WorkspaceRef.archived: boolean` (`packages/app-core/src/view-types.ts`) is REQUIRED, never optional — T8 says an archived workspace is still served in full, so this is metadata every viewer sees; the online mapper (`packages/app-core/src/online/mappers.ts`) reads it with `asBoolean`, refusing a row that omits it, the same discipline `project.archived` already gets. The replica's `getMyWorkspaces` needed no change for this field: it already throws `ReplicaGapError` unconditionally (a pre-existing gap, confirmed by reading — the brief's premise of a partially-working function did not match current reality). **Two consequences recorded, not fixed, both inherited from the plan's own chain order**: (1) since `checkLifecycle` runs before `checkVisibilityPermission`, a member who cannot SEE a ticket can still learn it is deleted/marked by sending `ticket.restored`/`purge.marked` and reading which lifecycle reason comes back, instead of the visibility refusal they would otherwise get; (2) `checkLifecycle`'s own row reads (`readLifecycle`, `ticketProjectId`, `noteHomeProjectId`) query by bare entity id with no `workspace_id` clause — safe only because `ingest-service.ts`'s `ENTITY_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH_RULE` guard already refuses any envelope whose entity belongs to a different workspace before `checkPermission` ever runs (confirmed by reading the ingest pipeline's ordering). Case ids `19.040`–`19.045` (`test-cases/19-trash.md`).
- ⚙️ **A deleted project is hidden with its contents, one container down from Task 5** (spec T10) — the same choke-point discipline, applied to `LIVE_TICKET_WHERE` (`apps/server/src/read/visible-where.ts`), which gains a container clause: `t.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM proj_projects dp WHERE dp.project_id = t.project_id AND dp.deleted_at IS NOT NULL)`. **The coverage sweep, run fresh rather than trusted from the docblock's own withdrawn count**: `grep -rln LIVE_TICKET_WHERE apps/server/src` names 16 files (all view reads or the two event sweeps, `auto-close`/`notifications` — neither touches an engine or projection write path, so the constant change reaches every one of them safely); `git grep -nE 'deleted_at +IS +NULL' -- apps/server/src` finds 5 real (non-comment) predicates. Three converted: `projections/note-search.ts:183` (splices the constant directly, `t` already the alias), `routes/builder-reads.ts:505` (hand-written on alias `k`, the one site whose `t` is taken), `visibility/rollup.ts:269` (hand-written, keeping its `OR t.ticket_id IS NULL` join-miss escape — the `NOT EXISTS` is moot, not fighting, when `t` is absent). **Two documented as unconvertible rather than converted-but-untestable** (`projections/rollups.ts:221` and `:320`, both in `recomputeParent`/`recomputeProject`): `hierarchy.cross-project` means every child of one parent shares that parent's project, so a project's deletion excludes ALL of a parent's live children or none, never a subset — the all-excluded case makes `recomputeParent`'s `HAVING count(*) > 0` write NOTHING, leaving whatever row was on disk from when the project was live STALE rather than corrected (a real, pre-existing gap: the `workflow.defined` trigger has no trailing DELETE the way the ticket-delete path's `recomputeProject` does), so there is no case that could ever observe the clause firing there. `visibility/rollup.ts`'s `rollupFor` has no such staleness gap (computed fresh every call, never cached) — a deleted-project child LEAVES the enumeration exactly as an individually-deleted one already does (the module's own docblock: "the child LEAVES the enumeration" — a WHERE predicate, not the join's ON clause), so `total` drops rather than the child moving to `uncategorized`. `routes/my-work.ts:364`'s one TypeScript application (`LIVE_TICKET_WHERE`'s rule at the one surface that cannot filter its own row) gained a second `LEFT JOIN proj_projects p ON p.project_id = t.project_id`, blanking a contested claim's title when either `t.deleted_at` or `p.deleted_at` is set, the row itself still served (unchanged reasoning from Task 5's docblock there). `read/visible-projects.ts`'s `visibleProjects` gained a `deleted_at` column and a POST-resolution filter — prefixes are STILL resolved over every row including deleted ones (`resolveProjectPrefixes` runs first), and only the deleted row is dropped from the served list afterward; filtering the SQL `WHERE` first was the wrong shape considered and rejected, since it would let a live sibling's derived prefix SHIFT the moment its neighbour is trashed and shift back on undelete, rewriting every ticket key in it for readers who had already quoted one (case 19.050's control: same-name, prefix-colliding sibling, unchanged). `read/notes.ts` gained one shared clause (`NOT EXISTS (... dp.project_id = n.home_project_id ...)`, trivially true for `home_project_id = ''`) added once to `listNotes` and once to `listNotesForTicket` — `getNoteDetail` is NOT covered (not in the plan's Files list, recorded here as an uncovered direct-read door of the same class Task 5 found for workspaces). **Project gate at the door** (`checkLifecycle`, `apps/server/src/permissions/check-lifecycle.ts`): a NEW gate, same shape as Task 5's workspace-wide one, checked directly after it and before the per-type switch — resolves "this event's project" from `env.entity`/`payload.projectId` (`ticket.created`, `note.created` — no row exists yet, same reason Task 4 reads the payload for `ticket.created`) or the row (`ticketProjectId`/`noteHomeProjectId`, every other ticket/note event), and refuses `PROJECT_DELETED_REASON` when it resolves and is deleted. **Ruling, diverging from the brief's literal exempt list**: the brief names only `project.undeleted`/`purge.marked`/`purge.unmarked` as exempt from the project's own gate; `project.deleted` is exempt too, by the same reasoning Task 5 ruled for `workspace.deleted` — without it, a SECOND `project.deleted` would answer this gate's generic reason instead of falling through to the per-type switch's more specific `ALREADY_DELETED_REASON` (case 19.030, pre-existing and unmoved by this task). This makes three of Task 4's `purge.marked` containment arms (ticket, note, project) now provably redundant with the two general gates above — removed from the switch rather than left as dead code the reader has to re-derive is still correct. Case ids `19.050`–`19.055` (`test-cases/19-trash.md`).
- ⚙️ **`GET /v1/me/deleted-items`** (`apps/server/src/read/deleted-items.ts`, `routes/deleted-items.ts`; spec §6.3's read) — every deleted workspace, project, ticket or note this caller may currently restore or mark, BY CURRENT AUTHORITY (T3), never by who deleted it. The app connects as the cluster's only user, so the guard is the trigger's check, not a privilege boundary (measured 2026-09-28). New tables `purged_entities` (content-free registry, D2) and `purge_pending_objects`. Cases 19.100–19.107.

## 17. Styling system

The owner's twelve rules (2026-09-29), applied through the shared layers so every screen inherits them. Plan A: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-29-styling-system-refresh.md`; Plan B: `…-refresh-b-screens.md`; cases `test-cases/20-styling-system.md`.

- ⚙️ **Recessed grounds and the accessible edge** (styling refresh Plan A Task 1; `packages/ui/src/tokens.ts`) — `surfaceTrack` (a track that holds raised items on the page — board columns) and `surfaceWell` (a recessed group inside a raised panel — the sheet's fields), both identified by their inset shadow rather than their fill (1.08/1.10:1, measured), with `text`/`textMuted`/`textSubtle` declared on each at 4.5; `accentEdge`, the primary button's ≥ 3:1 edge and hover fill; and `border` — already the accessible grey since the border sweep — now also declared on raised and well grounds. `lineStrong` (2.03:1) is resolved by no role, measured rather than assumed. `CONTRAST_PAIRS` 33 → 44. Cases 20.001–20.004.
- ⚙️ **Depth, radius, spacing and motion tokens** (styling refresh Plan A Task 2; `packages/ui/src/tokens.ts`) — nine shadow roles (`lift`, `lift-near`, `lift-press`, `lift-drag`, `track`, `action`, `action-near`, `action-press`, `sheet`): hig takes the owner-approved mockup's values exactly (lit top edge, shadow falling down, a 3-layer spreading "near" shadow for a hovered card), plus `lift-drag`, a deeper 4-layer fall for a DRAGGED card built from the same primitives, neo expresses each in its own dual-shadow language (rest = `raised`, track = `sunken`, press = `selected`, the near lift a larger raised pair and the drag lift larger still), and minimal stays flat (`none`); a shadow layer can now carry a spread. `radius.track` = card + 8 per style (rule 05). `--gn-space-1/2/3` (8/16/24) and `--gn-motion-feedback/move/lift/done/ease-out` (100/200/220/300ms, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)`) are emitted once under the bare `:root`, so `apps/desktop` receives them through `installTheme` too. Cases 20.011–20.015.
- ✅ **The shared `Button` follows the button rules** (styling refresh Plan A Task 3; `packages/ui/src/ui.css` `.gn-button*`) — the primary is 48px tall with 24px sides, a 17px semibold label, a pill radius, a 10px icon gap, the accent fill with a ≥ 3:1 `accentEdge` edge, resting on the `action` shadow; hover brings it TOWARD the user (`scale(1.04)`, the near shadow, 200ms ease-out) and press pushes it back (`scale(0.98)`, 100ms), all off under reduced motion. The danger button shares that geometry and lift on neutral shadows. The ghost — every quiet control — is transparent with a 1px accessible edge and a text2 label (supersedes R1(c) for buttons; 13.289/13.284 amended). Product-wide: 26 primary usages in 21 files (listed in the plan). No spinner/check yet — `Button` has no pending state (D8). Cases 20.021–20.026.
- ⚙️ **Raised surfaces** (styling refresh Plan A Task 4; `ui.css` `.gn-card`, `.gn-dialog`) — every `Card` rests on the lit-edge, falling `lift` shadow (rule 04), product-wide in one declaration; a `Dialog` panel floats on `lift-near` with the 24/28px track radius. `Card` stays non-interactive, so nothing lifts on hover unless its own interactive class asks (pattern P-LIFT). Cases 20.031–20.032.
- ✅ **The board's columns are recessed tracks and a hovered card's shadow deepens** (styling refresh Plan A Task 5; `ui.css` `.gn-board__column`, `.gn-board-card`, `.gn-board__card-slot`) — each column is a track (the `surfaceTrack` ground, an inset shadow lit from above, radius 24 — neo 28 — and 8px padding), each card is raised on the lit-edge `lift` shadow with 16px padding and radius 16 (= 24 − 8; neo 20 = 28 − 8), columns 16px apart. Hovering a card changes its SHADOW ONLY (owner ruling 2026-09-29, "hover = shadow only"): a 3-layer spreading shadow above its neighbours, 220ms ease-out; press settles the shadow within 100ms. Nothing scales (the lift belongs to the drag, Task 5A), so a move dialog opened from the card stays viewport-centred with no guard. The header's **Create ticket** is the board's one loud element (the shared primary). Cases 20.041–20.046.
- ✅ **A dragged card lifts toward you and leaves a placeholder** (styling refresh Plan A Task 5A; `packages/app-core/src/views/board-drag-image.ts`, `board.tsx` `BoardCardSlot` and the column section, `ui.css` `.gn-board-drag-image`, `.gn-board__card-slot--placeholder`, `.gn-board__column--drop-target`) — owner ruling 2026-09-29: the full lift happens only while dragging. The drag image is a detached clone of the card tilted 2.5°, scaled 1.03 and on the deeper `lift-drag` shadow (no tilt or scale under reduced motion; the browser adds its own translucency). The card's own slot stays put as a recessed dashed placeholder the size of the card, so nothing jumps, and the column under the pointer gains an accent outline (and, since the 2026-09-30 drag fixes, a landing placeholder or a "can't drop here" state — see the next bullet; plan D25's "outline only" is superseded by owner feedback 2026-09-30). Feature-checked, so a browser without `setDragImage` still drags. Cases 20.101–20.105.
- ✅ **A dragged card shows where it will land, and a drop back on its own column does nothing** (board drag fixes D1 + D2, owner feedback 2026-09-30 — two bugs found on the dev stack; supersedes plan D25; `board.tsx` `BoardGroupSection`, `BoardGroupWithMoves.handleDrop`, `landingIndex`; `ui.css` `.gn-board__drop-placeholder`, `.gn-board__column--drop-refused`) — **(D1)** dropping a card on the column it already sits in is a no-op: no attempt, no `Can't move there — try …` refusal, no move event (the drop is still `preventDefault`ed). **(D2)** while a card is over a LEGAL column (`moveOutcome` says the move exists — the decision the arrows use, no second rule) the column holds one `aria-hidden` placeholder of the card's measured height at the slot it will occupy, and the cards below slide down over 200ms ease-out (none under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`). The slot is the card's ticket-id order among the column's cards (every board read orders by `ticket_id`; `landingIndex` cites them), so a card created earlier lands above a later one. Over an ILLEGAL column there is no placeholder: the column is muted with a `not-allowed` cursor and `dragover` sets `dropEffect = 'none'` (Chromium may then cancel the drop, in which case the refusal is reachable through the arrows; a drop that does fire still shows it). The card's own column keeps just the source placeholder. The accent outline stays on a legal target (it is the only signal on a collapsed strip, which has no list and so no placeholder, and on a drag from another workflow group, whose card this group cannot see; a strip shows the outline or the muted look, never a placeholder). The group learns the dragged card (id, state, height) from the source slot at `dragstart`, because a browser hides a drag's data during `dragover`. Cases 20.106–20.110, 20.123–20.124.

## 18. The web app on phones

Every screen working and looking intentional at phone width (≤40rem), with a slim top bar, a customizable bottom bar, a one-column board with a Move sheet, a full-screen ticket sheet and bottom-sheet dialogs. Owner request 2026-10-01 (a Galaxy Z Flip 7 screenshot of `/workspaces`). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-01-mobile-web.md`; spec `…/specs/2026-10-01-mobile-web-design.md`; cases `test-cases/21-mobile-web.md`. Ships on `release/mobile`.

- ⚙️ **Phone foundation** (mobile-web plan Task 1; cases 21.001–21.003) — the phone arm is the existing `@media (max-width: 40rem)`; `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` exports a `viewport` (`viewportFit: 'cover'` so `env(safe-area-inset-*)` is real on iOS, `interactiveWidget: 'resizes-content'` so the on-screen keyboard shrinks the layout); `--gn-phone-bar-height` (3.5rem) and `--gn-phone-top-height` (3.25rem) are emitted once under the bare `:root` (`packages/ui/src/tokens.ts` `phone`); `PHONE_OWNERS` (`packages/ui/test/helpers/style-patterns.ts`) names the task that owns each of the 26 routes and `phone-inventory.test.ts` fails on a route with no owner.
- ✅ **Phone top bar** (mobile-web plan Task 2; cases 21.010–21.015) — at ≤40rem the bar is one row (`--gn-phone-top-height`): brand, a quiet **switcher** and the corner. The switcher reads "Choose a workspace" with none chosen, the workspace name inside one, "<project> — <workspace>" inside a project; its sheet lists live projects (current marked `aria-current` + a check) and live workspaces plus "All workspaces". It replaces the member link row and the scope note, which are `display: none` there (still in the DOM). Page titles are one ellipsised line at the heading size. Signed out keeps `Help` + `Sign in`. `apps/web/src/phone-switcher.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app-nav.tsx`, `apps/web/app/globals.css` (the 40rem arm; no top-level `.gn-nav*` rule changed).
- ✅ **Customizable bottom bar** (mobile-web plan Task 3; cases 21.020–21.033) — at ≤40rem a fixed bar of four slots the person chose (default Board · My work · Notes · Inbox) plus **More**, above the home-indicator inset, hidden while the on-screen keyboard is up. The current slot is marked by tone AND an indicator; Inbox carries the unread dot; project views (Board/List/Calendar/Timeline/Backlog) open the last project on that tab. Workspace-scoped slots appear only when a workspace resolves. **More** lists everything not in the bar plus Settings, Account, Help and **Edit bottom bar** (− / + / ↑ / ↓ / Reset to default; at most four). The choice is per device and per user (`packages/app-core/src/preferences/bottom-bar.ts`, `localStorage` `gn-bottom-bar`, never the server). At phone width the bar replaces the corner's Notes and Inbox links (`useIsPhone`, `apps/web/src/use-is-phone.ts`); `apps/web/src/bottom-bar.tsx`, `apps/web/src/use-keyboard-open.ts`, `apps/web/app/globals.css`.
- ✅ **Board on a phone** (mobile-web plan Task 4; cases 21.040–21.050) — at ≤40rem the board shows one full-width column at a time (CSS scroll-snap over the existing rail) under a **Column** picker (one option per column, "<name> <count>", collapsed ones included; choosing scrolls the rail, scrolling the rail moves the selection); column collapse is not applied there and the stored choices are left alone. No touch drag-and-drop: the ‹ › arrows are hidden and each card carries a **Move** button that opens the move dialog over every board destination (both directions, Backlog excluded, gated ones marked "needs a comment"), disabled with the refusal sentence as its description when none is legal. `packages/app-core/src/views/board-phone-picker.tsx`, `use-phone-board.ts`, `board-arrows.ts` (`allBoardTargets`), `board.tsx`, `transition-dialog.tsx` (`markRules`), `packages/ui/src/ui.css`.
- ✅ **Move to… on desktop cards** (mobile-web plan Task 5; cases 21.060–21.062) — above 40rem each card's footer gains a ghost **Move to…** after the ‹ › arrows (≥44px), the same button the phone shows as **Move**: it opens the move dialog over every board destination in both directions, so a branching state's far targets are one click away without the arrows' picker. One accessible name ("Move to another state") at every width; the visible word is swapped by CSS. Amends 20.052's footer list. `packages/app-core/src/views/board.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/ui.css`.
- ✅ **The ticket sheet full screen, and dialogs as bottom sheets** (mobile-web plan Task 6; cases 21.070–21.074) — at ≤40rem the ticket sheet fills the screen (the `.gn-sheet--full` form, forced: `width: 100%`, square, no shadow) and its Full-screen toggle is hidden; its header sticks to the top and carries a phone-only **Move** shortcut (accessible name "Move this ticket") that calls the same `openMove` handler as the State row's **Move…**, so one dialog opens. Dialogs (`.gn-dialog`) become bottom sheets: pinned to the bottom, full width, rounded on top only, at most `90dvh`, clear of the home-indicator inset; they keep the `gnRise` entrance and none under reduced motion. CSS-only except the shortcut. `packages/ui/src/ui.css`, `packages/app-core/src/views/ticket-sheet.tsx`.
- ✅ **Phone screens: workspaces, workspace home, Members, Inbox** (mobile-web plan Task 7; cases 21.090–21.093) — at ≤40rem `/workspaces` and the workspace home are single-column, the Create workspace button spans the header's width and the Create project button wraps under the Projects heading (the dialogs are the Dialog's own phone sheet); the workspace home's section links become a scrollable row of compact chips (22.148); Members is stacked rows (name + email, role select full width, Remove under it) with the pending-invitation rows wrapping and the invite form full width; Inbox rows keep a ≥44px tap height with the unread dot and badge, and "Load more" spans the list. Desktop and tablet are unchanged. `apps/web/app/globals.css`, `packages/ui/src/ui.css` (the `.gn-inbox__*` arm).

## 19. Prefixes, project groups and Create buttons

Workspace and project prefixes can change (every key re-reads; former keys stay findable and reserved), projects can be filed into a four-level group tree, and Create workspace / Create project / Create ticket become consistent primary icon buttons. Owner spec 2026-10-01 (R1–R7); plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-01-prefixes-groups-create-buttons.md`; cases `test-cases/22-prefixes-and-groups.md`. Ships on `release/prefix-groups-ux`.

- ⚙️ **The prefix and group-assignment events** (prefixes and groups plan Task 1; cases 22.001–22.002) — `workspace.prefix_changed` (`{ prefix }`, filed against the workspace) is registered, and `project.updated` carries optional `prefix` and `groupId` (`null` ungroups; at least one of name, description, prefix, groupId must be present). Schemas only: the projection and readers learn the prefix in Task 2 (below), the permission door in Task 3, and groups in Task 6. A rename alone still never moves a key. `packages/domain/src/events/membership.ts`, `packages/domain/src/vocabulary.ts`.
- ⚙️ **Prefix history and reserved prefixes** (prefixes and groups plan Task 2; cases 22.020–22.029) — a `project.updated` carrying `prefix` files the prefix the project answers to NOW (entered, or derived from `founding_name`) in the new projection table `proj_project_prefixes` as a FORMER, reserved prefix (`until_time` = the event's `serverTime`), sets `proj_projects.prefix`, and drops the new value from the former list when going back to one. `projectPrefixHistory(db, workspaceId)` serves `{ current, former: [{ prefix, until }] }` per project; both prefix readers (`projectPrefixesInWorkspace`, `visibleProjects`) pass the workspace's reserved set to `resolveProjectPrefixes(claims, reserved?)`, so a DERIVED prefix flees a reserved one (`SO` → `SO2`) while an entered one is untouched. `workspaceIdentityFromLedger` folds `workspace.prefix_changed` (current = the last one, `formerPrefixes` = the earlier values with when they stopped), so every ticket key re-reads. The table is declared in `proj_projects`' `tables` and emptied by its `reset`, so `verify-projections` rebuilds it. Reads only: the door (Task 3) and the key lookup (Task 4) come later. `apps/server/migrations/1791100000000_prefix-history.sql`, `apps/server/src/projections/proj-projects.ts`, `apps/server/src/read/visible-projects.ts`, `apps/server/src/workspaces/workspace-name.ts`, `packages/domain/src/prefix.ts`. A permanent purge deletes the former prefixes with their project or workspace (`PURGE_TABLE_RULES` `proj_project_prefixes: erase`, and its statement in `purge/erasure.ts`'s `eraseRows`; cases 22.028–22.029).
- ✅ **The door: a retired prefix is refused, and the holder may take it back** (prefixes and groups plan Task 3; cases 22.040–22.046) — `checkPrefixReservation` now covers `project.created` AND `project.updated` carrying a `prefix`: another project's CURRENT prefix is refused `project.prefix-taken` (text unchanged), then one another project has moved OFF is refused `project.prefix-reserved` (`PROJECT_PREFIX_RESERVED_RULE`) — *"SO was Shop operations' prefix until 1 Oct. Its old ticket keys still point there, so it can't be reused."* (the holder's CURRENT name, the IST day it moved off, `d MMM`). Both are by project id, never by value, so a project may go SO → SH → SO and a retry of its own earlier event reaches `duplicate-event-id`. `workspace.prefix_changed` is admin-only (`ADMIN_ONLY_TYPES`; a member is refused `permission.role`); a workspace may reuse its own former prefix, so it has no reservation check. `apps/server/src/permissions/check-permission.ts`.
- ✅ **A ticket is found by its key, current or former** (prefixes and groups plan Task 4, FD1; cases 22.060–22.068) — nothing turned a key back into a ticket before: search indexed title, description and comments only. `parseTicketKey(text)` (`packages/domain/src/prefix.ts`) reads `' ccso-12 '` as `{ letters: "CCSO", number: 12 }` (two to six ASCII letters, then at most ONE trailing digit 2–9, a hyphen, one to seven digits, trimmed and upper-cased; the digit is the collision suffix of a derived project prefix, so the `<ws>SO2-1` the product shows is searchable; `CCSO12`, `CC1O-12`, `C-1` and prose are `null`). `GET /v1/search` — and the hosted MCP `search_tickets` that calls it — resolves a key-shaped query (`ticketIdsForKey`, `apps/server/src/read/ticket-key-lookup.ts`) by splitting the letters against the workspace's current AND former prefixes × each project's current and former prefixes (Task 2's history; R2 keeps the split unambiguous), then taking the ticket numbered `number` in each matching project (`ticketIdsAtNumber`, `read/ticket-numbers.ts`). Those ids are admitted to the match beside the text match and ordered FIRST, so the key's ticket leads the hits, appears once even if its title also mentions the key, and its card shows the CURRENT key (`CCSO-12` after `SO` → `SH` still finds it and reads `CCSH-12`). They pass through the SAME WHERE as every text hit — tenancy, `visibleTicketsWhere`, soft delete, the filter — so a key finds only what the caller may already see (an owner-only ticket, another workspace's key, a guest's non-listed work: nothing). A hit found only by its key reports `matchedIn: "title"`. Note chips keep their inserted key text by design (FD2) and find the ticket the same way. `apps/server/src/routes/search.ts`, `apps/server/src/read/ticket-key-lookup.ts`, `apps/server/src/read/ticket-numbers.ts`, `packages/domain/src/prefix.ts`, `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/read-tools.ts`.
- ⚙️ **The note-search index follows a prefix change** (prefixes and groups plan Task 5, FD7; cases 22.080–22.082) — `proj_note_search.ticket_text` bakes the ticket KEY, so `project.updated` carrying a `prefix` re-derives every note attached to a ticket of that project, and `workspace.prefix_changed` every note in the workspace with an attachment (`reindexNote`, as the ticket-title path does); each pass ends with `rederiveWorkspaceLexemes`, because the never-deleted lexemes would otherwise keep the old key's words live while a `verify-projections` rebuild (which reads the other projections and the workspace prefix in their FINAL state) never produces them. Only the NEW key is indexed for notes; the old key still finds the ticket through the key search (Task 4). `apps/server/src/projections/note-search.ts`.
- ✅ **The group tree: events, projection, door and read route** (prefixes and groups plan Task 6; cases 22.090–22.107) — `group.created` (`{ parentId, level 1–4, name, rank }`), `group.renamed`, `group.reordered` and `group.deleted` are registered against the new `group` entity kind and project into `proj_groups` (`apps/server/migrations/1791200000000_groups.sql`, `projections/proj-groups.ts`); `proj_projects.group_id` is written by `project.updated`'s `groupId`. The door (`permissions/check-permission.ts`, `checkGroupRules`) is owner/admin only and refuses an unknown parent (`group.unknown`), a level that is not the parent's plus one (`group.level-mismatch`), a sibling name taken in any letter case (`group.name-taken`), deleting a group a project (trashed ones included) is filed under (`group.in-use`) or one with children (`group.has-children`), and filing a project under a group that is not live in its own workspace (`project.group-unknown`). `GET /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/groups` serves the tree, siblings in rank order, with project (trashed ones counted) and child counts to any member (404 to guests and outsiders; `routes/groups.ts`), and every `/v1/me/workspaces` project row carries `groupId` (`null` when ungrouped; `app-core` mapper requires the key). Group events are `withheld` from replica visibility until a later task folds them (`visibility/visible-events-for.ts`). (`packages/domain/src/events/groups.ts`; `apps/server/test/groups/`)
- ✅ **The workspace home: nav row on top, the Projects heading row, and the Grouped view** (prefixes and groups plan Task 7; cases 22.120–22.124, 22.140–22.149) — `/w/[workspaceId]` now leads with the section links, then a Projects heading row: the `h2`, the archived toggle, a "Show projects" Grouped/Plain segmented control (hidden for guests, whose groups route 404s) and the Create project button (admins; prefixes and groups Task 8, 22.152 — it mounted into a `data-slot="create-project"` placeholder until then). **Grouped** reads the workspace's group tree (`getGroups`, `GET /v1/workspaces/:id/groups`, mapped by `mapGroupRows`; the replica door answers with a registered gap) and draws nested sections L1→L4 in rank order, each headed by a level strip (`data-level`, `aria-label="Level N group: <name>"`, coloured by the new `--gn-level-1`…`4` tokens, which clear 3:1 on the card surface in every style × theme), a project under its own group, empty groups omitted, and an "Ungrouped" section last (absent when every project has a group); **Plain** is the unchanged flat grid. The choice is remembered per user and per workspace in `localStorage` (`readProjectGrouping` / `rememberProjectGrouping`); a failed groups read keeps the plain list and says so. The project card becomes one "Open <project>" link plus an admin overflow menu (see the amendment under the workspace home above); on a phone the title takes its own line, the controls share one row, and the section links scroll as chips. Retires case 13.1297. `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/grouped-projects.tsx`, `apps/web/src/overflow-menu.tsx` (`triggerRef`), `apps/web/app/globals.css`, `packages/app-core/src/preferences/project-grouping.ts`, `packages/app-core/src/online/mappers.ts`, `packages/ui/src/tokens.ts`
- ✅ **Create workspace, Create project and Create ticket are consistent primary icon buttons that open their forms** (prefixes and groups plan Task 8, BRD-19; cases 22.150–22.153, 22.155–22.156) — each is a `Button variant="primary"` with the shared `PlusIcon` (`packages/ui/src/icons/plus-icon.tsx`) and the name "Create …". "Create workspace" sits in the `/workspaces` header grid and opens a `Dialog` holding the founding form (name, prefix, Cancel / Create workspace); the always-visible form is gone. "Create project" sits in the workspace home's Projects heading row beside the archived toggle, admin-only, and opens a `Dialog` with the New-project form (name, description, prefix, an empty `group-picker` slot for Task 9, Cancel / Create project), and a refusal from the door is drawn inside it and not announced a second time on the page; a non-admin gets "Only an owner or admin can create a project." and the empty state reads "No projects yet. Create the first one." Every create-ticket entry point — the page header, the empty board's banner, each column's button (accessible name `Create ticket in <column>`), the dialog's title and submit — says "Create ticket". `apps/web/app/workspaces/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/p/[projectId]/page.tsx`, `packages/app-core/src/views/{create-ticket-flow,new-ticket-dialog,board}.tsx`, `apps/web/app/globals.css`.
- ✅ **The group picker: four type-ahead levels with inline create** (prefixes and groups plan Task 9; cases 22.160–22.170) — `GroupPicker` is one labelled combobox per level (Level 1 group … Level 4 group, 44 px, sentence case), each listing only the children of the pick above it, enabled only once that level has a value; emptying a level clears those below. An exact name (any case) selects the existing group on blur or Enter; any other text becomes a pending "New" group (a "Create “…”" option sits last in the list; Enter and Escape stay inside the picker, and `aria-activedescendant` follows the highlighted option). The value is a `GroupChoice` (`groupId` = the deepest existing pick, `pendingNames` = groups still to create) and `groupSeeds` turns it into one `group.created` per pending name (parent chained, rank after the last sibling) plus the id the project files under (refusing a chain past `GROUP_MAX_LEVEL`), for the form to submit in one ordered batch ahead of its own claim — each event commits or is refused on its own (FD3: a batch is not atomic). When a re-read of the groups shows a pending name now exists (someone created it first), the picker adopts it and says "Using the existing …". Hand-rolled WAI-ARIA combobox, because the react-aria packages are `packages/ui`-only. `apps/web/src/group-picker.tsx`, `apps/web/src/group-picker-seeds.ts`, `apps/web/app/globals.css` (`.gn-group-picker`)
